chunks.text: Impeaching credit of witness — The credit of a witness may be impeached by: (1) evidence of persons that they do not believe the witness on oath; (2) proof that the witness has been bribed or accepted offers; (3) former inconsistent statements; (4) evidence of general reputation for untruthfulness.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Primary and secondary evidence — Primary evidence means the document itself produced for inspection. Secondary evidence means copies, counterparts, oral accounts of document content admissible when primary evidence is unavailable.
chunks.text: Primary and secondary evidence — Primary evidence means the document itself produced for inspection. Secondary evidence means copies, counterparts, oral accounts of document content admissible when primary evidence is unavailable.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Proof of documents — Documents must be proved by primary evidence except in cases where secondary evidence is permitted by this Order.
chunks.text: Proof of documents — Documents must be proved by primary evidence except in cases where secondary evidence is permitted by this Order.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Public documents — The following are public documents: (1) documents forming the acts or records of sovereign authority, official bodies, courts; (2) public records kept in Pakistan of private documents; (3) published official documents.
chunks.text: Public documents — The following are public documents: (1) documents forming the acts or records of sovereign authority, official bodies, courts; (2) public records kept in Pakistan of private documents; (3) published official documents.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Private documents — All documents that are not public documents are private documents.
chunks.text: Private documents — All documents that are not public documents are private documents.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Certified copies — Every public officer having custody of a public document must give a certified copy on demand, on payment of the legal fees. Certified copies may be proved without production of the original.
chunks.text: Certified copies — Every public officer having custody of a public document must give a certified copy on demand, on payment of the legal fees. Certified copies may be proved without production of the original.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Presumptions as to documents — The court shall presume the genuineness of every document purporting to be a certified copy, or an official gazette, or a gazette notification, or a document certified by a Pakistani diplomatic or consular officer.
chunks.text: Presumptions as to documents — The court shall presume the genuineness of every document purporting to be a certified copy, or an official gazette, or a gazette notification, or a document certified by a Pakistani diplomatic or consular officer.

chunks.title: Qanun-e-Shahadat Order, 1984 (President's Order No. 10 of 1984)
chunks.chunkTitle: Judicial notice — The court shall take judicial notice of: all laws in force in Pakistan, international treaties, the seals of courts, the seals of notaries public, the accession and sign manuals of the President, geographical divisions, and public holidays.
chunks.text: Judicial notice — The court shall take judicial notice of: all laws in force in Pakistan, international treaties, the seals of courts, the seals of notaries public, the accession and sign manuals of the President, geographical divisions, and public holidays.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908) — Consolidates the law of limitation for suits, appeals and applications in Pakistan. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.
chunks.text: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908) — Consolidates the law of limitation for suits, appeals and applications in Pakistan. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation bars remedy not right — When the period of limitation prescribed for a suit has expired, the plaintiff shall not be entitled to any remedy. The right itself is not extinguished except in certain specific cases (property recovery).
chunks.text: Limitation bars remedy not right — When the period of limitation prescribed for a suit has expired, the plaintiff shall not be entitled to any remedy. The right itself is not extinguished except in certain specific cases (property recovery).

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Dismissal of suit if barred — Every suit instituted after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence. The court must consider limitation even if not pleaded.
chunks.text: Dismissal of suit if barred — Every suit instituted after the prescribed period shall be dismissed, although limitation has not been set up as a defence. The court must consider limitation even if not pleaded.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Expiry of court vacation — Where the prescribed period expires on a day when the court is closed, the suit may be instituted on the day when the court reopens.
chunks.text: Expiry of court vacation — Where the prescribed period expires on a day when the court is closed, the suit may be instituted on the day when the court reopens.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Extension in certain cases — An appeal or application for review or revision may be admitted after the prescribed period if the appellant/applicant satisfies the court that there was sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within the period.
chunks.text: Extension in certain cases — An appeal or application for review or revision may be admitted after the prescribed period if the appellant/applicant satisfies the court that there was sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal or making the application within the period.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Legal disability — A person entitled to institute a suit who is a minor or insane may institute the suit within the same period after the disability has ceased, unless the period expires before the cessation of disability.
chunks.text: Legal disability — A person entitled to institute a suit who is a minor or insane may institute the suit within the same period after the disability has ceased, unless the period expires before the cessation of disability.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Continuing disability — Where a person is under disability at the time of the right to sue accruing, and dies while still under disability, no time runs against his legal representative.
chunks.text: Continuing disability — Where a person is under disability at the time of the right to sue accruing, and dies while still under disability, no time runs against his legal representative.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Exclusion of time for obtaining copy — In computing the period of limitation for a suit, appeal or application, the day from which the period begins to run shall be excluded. For appeals, the time spent in obtaining a certified copy of the decree/order appealed from is excluded.
chunks.text: Exclusion of time for obtaining copy — In computing the period of limitation for a suit, appeal or application, the day from which the period begins to run shall be excluded. For appeals, the time spent in obtaining a certified copy of the decree/order appealed from is excluded.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Exclusion of time for defendant absence — Where the defendant is absent from Pakistan, time during which the defendant was absent beyond the limits of Pakistan shall be excluded.
chunks.text: Exclusion of time for defendant absence — Where the defendant is absent from Pakistan, time during which the defendant was absent beyond the limits of Pakistan shall be excluded.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction — In computing the period of limitation, time during which the plaintiff has been prosecuting a civil proceeding in good faith in a court which lacks jurisdiction shall be excluded.
chunks.text: Exclusion of time of proceeding bona fide in court without jurisdiction — In computing the period of limitation, time during which the plaintiff has been prosecuting a civil proceeding in good faith in a court which lacks jurisdiction shall be excluded.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Exclusion of time for injunction — Where the institution of a suit has been stayed by injunction or order, the time of the continuance of the injunction shall be excluded.
chunks.text: Exclusion of time for injunction — Where the institution of a suit has been stayed by injunction or order, the time of the continuance of the injunction shall be excluded.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Acknowledgment in writing — Where an acknowledgment of liability in writing signed by the party is made before the expiration of the period, fresh period starts from the date of acknowledgment.
chunks.text: Acknowledgment in writing — Where an acknowledgment of liability in writing signed by the party is made before the expiration of the period, fresh period starts from the date of acknowledgment.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Payment on account — Where part payment of a debt or interest is made before the expiry of limitation, fresh period starts from the date of payment.
chunks.text: Payment on account — Where part payment of a debt or interest is made before the expiry of limitation, fresh period starts from the date of payment.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Continuing breach of contract — In the case of a continuing breach of contract or continuing tort, a fresh period begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or tort continues.
chunks.text: Continuing breach of contract — In the case of a continuing breach of contract or continuing tort, a fresh period begins to run at every moment of the time during which the breach or tort continues.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Suits for compensation for torts not continuing — For torts not continuing, the period runs from the date when the act complained of is done.
chunks.text: Suits for compensation for torts not continuing — For torts not continuing, the period runs from the date when the act complained of is done.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Concealed fraud — Where fraud or mistake is the basis, limitation runs from the date of discovery of the fraud or mistake.
chunks.text: Concealed fraud — Where fraud or mistake is the basis, limitation runs from the date of discovery of the fraud or mistake.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Death of plaintiff or defendant — Where the right to sue survives after the death of a plaintiff or defendant, the legal representative may continue the suit.
chunks.text: Death of plaintiff or defendant — Where the right to sue survives after the death of a plaintiff or defendant, the legal representative may continue the suit.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for suits under Contract Act — Suits for specific performance of contract: 3 years from the date fixed for performance. Suits for breach of contract: 3 years from the date of breach. Suits for money lent: 3 years from default.
chunks.text: Limitation for suits under Contract Act — Suits for specific performance of contract: 3 years from the date fixed for performance. Suits for breach of contract: 3 years from the date of breach. Suits for money lent: 3 years from default.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for recovery of property — Recovery of immovable property: 12 years from the date when possession becomes adverse. Recovery of movable property: 3 years from the date of wrongful taking.
chunks.text: Limitation for recovery of property — Recovery of immovable property: 12 years from the date when possession becomes adverse. Recovery of movable property: 3 years from the date of wrongful taking.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for torts — Suits for compensation for wrong to person: 1 year (assault, battery, false imprisonment). Defamation: 1 year. Malicious prosecution: 1 year. Wrongful detention of property: 3 years.
chunks.text: Limitation for torts — Suits for compensation for wrong to person: 1 year (assault, battery, false imprisonment). Defamation: 1 year. Malicious prosecution: 1 year. Wrongful detention of property: 3 years.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for mortgage suits — Suits by mortgagee for foreclosure: 30 years from due date. Suits for sale: 12 years from due date. Redemption by mortgagor: 30 years from due date.
chunks.text: Limitation for mortgage suits — Suits by mortgagee for foreclosure: 30 years from due date. Suits for sale: 12 years from due date. Redemption by mortgagor: 30 years from due date.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for government suits — Suits by or against the government: 30 years or as otherwise provided.
chunks.text: Limitation for government suits — Suits by or against the government: 30 years or as otherwise provided.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Suits relating to public charities — Suits relating to public trusts or charities: 6 years from the date when the right to sue accrues.
chunks.text: Suits relating to public charities — Suits relating to public trusts or charities: 6 years from the date when the right to sue accrues.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for appeals — Appeal from a decree of the Civil Court: 30 days (Supreme Court), 90 days (High Court), 30 days (District Court). Appeals from orders: 30 days.
chunks.text: Limitation for appeals — Appeal from a decree of the Civil Court: 30 days (Supreme Court), 90 days (High Court), 30 days (District Court). Appeals from orders: 30 days.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Applications — Application for execution of decree: 6 years from the date of decree or the last order of execution.
chunks.text: Applications — Application for execution of decree: 6 years from the date of decree or the last order of execution.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Attachment — Applications for attachment of property: 3 years from the date of the order granting attachment.
chunks.text: Attachment — Applications for attachment of property: 3 years from the date of the order granting attachment.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Specific limitation periods — Recovery of land: 12 years. Recovery of rent: 3 years. Redemption of mortgage: 30 years. Partition of property: 12 years. Accounting: 3 years. Trust property: no limitation. Inheritance: 12 years.
chunks.text: Specific limitation periods — Recovery of land: 12 years. Recovery of rent: 3 years. Redemption of mortgage: 30 years. Partition of property: 12 years. Accounting: 3 years. Trust property: no limitation. Inheritance: 12 years.

chunks.title: The Limitation Act, 1908 (Act IX of 1908)
chunks.chunkTitle: Limitation for criminal appeals — Criminal appeals: 30 days from the date of judgment from Sessions Court to High Court. 30 days from the date of order to Sessions Court from Magistrate.
chunks.text: Limitation for criminal appeals — Criminal appeals: 30 days from the date of judgment from Sessions Court to High Court. 30 days from the date of order to Sessions Court from Magistrate.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act No. XIX of 2017) — Consolidates and amends the law relating to companies in Pakistan. Repeals the Companies Ordinance 1984. Source: SECP (secp.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT. Administering Authority: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP).
chunks.text: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act No. XIX of 2017) — Consolidates and amends the law relating to companies in Pakistan. Repeals the Companies Ordinance 1984. Source: SECP (secp.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT. Administering Authority: Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP).

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Definitions — 'Company' means a company formed and registered under this Act. 'Public company' means a company not being a private company. 'Private company' means a company which restricts the right to transfer shares, limits membership to 50, and prohibits public subscription. 'Member' means the subscriber to the memorandum. 'Director' includes any person occupying the position of director.
chunks.text: Definitions — 'Company' means a company formed and registered under this Act. 'Public company' means a company not being a private company. 'Private company' means a company which restricts the right to transfer shares, limits membership to 50, and prohibits public subscription. 'Member' means the subscriber to the memorandum. 'Director' includes any person occupying the position of director.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Incorporation — Any seven or more persons (two for private company) may form a company by subscribing their names to the memorandum and complying with registration requirements. Members must be of age of majority.
chunks.text: Incorporation — Any seven or more persons (two for private company) may form a company by subscribing their names to the memorandum and complying with registration requirements. Members must be of age of majority.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Memorandum of Association — The memorandum must state: (1) the company name (ending with 'Limited' or '(Pvt) Ltd'); (2) the province of registered office; (3) the principal line of business; (4) the liability of members (limited or unlimited); (5) the authorized share capital.
chunks.text: Memorandum of Association — The memorandum must state: (1) the company name (ending with 'Limited' or '(Pvt) Ltd'); (2) the province of registered office; (3) the principal line of business; (4) the liability of members (limited or unlimited); (5) the authorized share capital.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Articles of Association — The articles contain regulations for the management of the company. Public companies must file articles. Private companies require articles. Table A in Schedule 1 applies where articles are not registered.
chunks.text: Articles of Association — The articles contain regulations for the management of the company. Public companies must file articles. Private companies require articles. Table A in Schedule 1 applies where articles are not registered.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Name — No company shall be registered with a name which is identical or deceptively similar to an existing company. Names must not be offensive or prohibited under the Emblems and Names Act.
chunks.text: Name — No company shall be registered with a name which is identical or deceptively similar to an existing company. Names must not be offensive or prohibited under the Emblems and Names Act.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Registered office — Every company must have a registered office in Pakistan, open to the public during business hours. Notice of registered office must be given to the registrar within 30 days.
chunks.text: Registered office — Every company must have a registered office in Pakistan, open to the public during business hours. Notice of registered office must be given to the registrar within 30 days.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Commencement of business — A public company having a share capital cannot commence business until the certificate of commencement is obtained.
chunks.text: Commencement of business — A public company having a share capital cannot commence business until the certificate of commencement is obtained.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Alteration of memorandum — A company may alter its memorandum by special resolution, subject to confirmation by the registrar or court for certain changes.
chunks.text: Alteration of memorandum — A company may alter its memorandum by special resolution, subject to confirmation by the registrar or court for certain changes.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Doctrine of ultra vires — Any act of the company beyond the objects stated in the memorandum is void and cannot be ratified even by unanimous consent of shareholders.
chunks.text: Doctrine of ultra vires — Any act of the company beyond the objects stated in the memorandum is void and cannot be ratified even by unanimous consent of shareholders.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Shares and debentures — Shares means the share capital of the company. Debentures includes debenture stock, bonds and any other securities of the company whether constituting a charge on assets or not.
chunks.text: Shares and debentures — Shares means the share capital of the company. Debentures includes debenture stock, bonds and any other securities of the company whether constituting a charge on assets or not.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Prospectus — A public company offering shares to the public must issue a prospectus containing all material information for investors. Civil and criminal liability attaches to misstatements in prospectus.
chunks.text: Prospectus — A public company offering shares to the public must issue a prospectus containing all material information for investors. Civil and criminal liability attaches to misstatements in prospectus.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Share capital — Minimum paid-up capital for a public company: PKR 200,000. For a private company: PKR 100,000. The company may increase, reduce or reorganize share capital by special resolution.
chunks.text: Share capital — Minimum paid-up capital for a public company: PKR 200,000. For a private company: PKR 100,000. The company may increase, reduce or reorganize share capital by special resolution.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Directors — Every company must have at least two directors (private) or three directors (public). Directors must be natural persons of sound mind and not disqualified.
chunks.text: Directors — Every company must have at least two directors (private) or three directors (public). Directors must be natural persons of sound mind and not disqualified.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Chief Executive — Every company must have a chief executive appointed by the board from among the directors.
chunks.text: Chief Executive — Every company must have a chief executive appointed by the board from among the directors.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Meetings — Annual General Meeting: every company must hold an AGM each year within 4 months of the close of the financial year. Extraordinary General Meeting: may be called by directors or by members holding 10% of paid-up capital.
chunks.text: Meetings — Annual General Meeting: every company must hold an AGM each year within 4 months of the close of the financial year. Extraordinary General Meeting: may be called by directors or by members holding 10% of paid-up capital.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Accounts — Every company must keep proper books of account reflecting true and fair view of affairs. Financial statements must be approved by the board and audited by a chartered accountant.
chunks.text: Accounts — Every company must keep proper books of account reflecting true and fair view of affairs. Financial statements must be approved by the board and audited by a chartered accountant.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Audit — Every company must appoint an auditor at each AGM. The auditor must be a chartered accountant or firm of chartered accountants. Auditor's report must be attached to financial statements.
chunks.text: Audit — Every company must appoint an auditor at each AGM. The auditor must be a chartered accountant or firm of chartered accountants. Auditor's report must be attached to financial statements.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Dividends — Dividends may be declared only out of profits. No dividend shall be declared without providing for depreciation. Directors may recommend dividend subject to approval by members.
chunks.text: Dividends — Dividends may be declared only out of profits. No dividend shall be declared without providing for depreciation. Directors may recommend dividend subject to approval by members.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Winding up — A company may be wound up by the court (compulsory) or voluntarily. Grounds for compulsory winding up include: inability to pay debts, default in filing statutory documents, just and equitable ground.
chunks.text: Winding up — A company may be wound up by the court (compulsory) or voluntarily. Grounds for compulsory winding up include: inability to pay debts, default in filing statutory documents, just and equitable ground.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Oppression and mismanagement — A member may petition the court if affairs of the company are being conducted oppressively or prejudicial to public interest or the members. The court may pass orders including removal of directors.
chunks.text: Oppression and mismanagement — A member may petition the court if affairs of the company are being conducted oppressively or prejudicial to public interest or the members. The court may pass orders including removal of directors.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Removal of directors — A company may remove a director by ordinary resolution before the expiry of his term. Special notice of at least 14 days is required.
chunks.text: Removal of directors — A company may remove a director by ordinary resolution before the expiry of his term. Special notice of at least 14 days is required.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Insider trading — No director, officer or employee of a company shall deal in securities of the company while in possession of unpublished price-sensitive information. Penalty: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine.
chunks.text: Insider trading — No director, officer or employee of a company shall deal in securities of the company while in possession of unpublished price-sensitive information. Penalty: imprisonment up to 5 years or fine.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Single member company — A single member may form a private company limited by shares. Only natural persons who are citizens and residents of Pakistan may form a single member company.
chunks.text: Single member company — A single member may form a private company limited by shares. Only natural persons who are citizens and residents of Pakistan may form a single member company.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: SECP powers — SECP has regulatory authority over companies, may conduct investigations, issue directions, impose penalties for non-compliance, and compound offences.
chunks.text: SECP powers — SECP has regulatory authority over companies, may conduct investigations, issue directions, impose penalties for non-compliance, and compound offences.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Offences and penalties — Failure to file returns, hold meetings, maintain accounts or comply with SECP requirements attract penalties. Continuing default attracts daily penalties.
chunks.text: Offences and penalties — Failure to file returns, hold meetings, maintain accounts or comply with SECP requirements attract penalties. Continuing default attracts daily penalties.

chunks.title: The Companies Act, 2017 (Act XIX of 2017)
chunks.chunkTitle: Merger and amalgamation — Two or more companies may amalgamate by order of the court or SECP under the Mergers (Courts and SECP) Procedure. Scheme of arrangement requires board approval, member approval (75%), and court sanction.
chunks.text: Merger and amalgamation — Two or more companies may amalgamate by order of the court or SECP under the Mergers (Courts and SECP) Procedure. Scheme of arrangement requires board approval, member approval (75%), and court sanction.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. LVII of 1962) — Regulates banking companies in Pakistan. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.
chunks.text: Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 (Ordinance No. LVII of 1962) — Regulates banking companies in Pakistan. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 — SBP is the central bank of Pakistan. Functions: issue currency, regulate money supply, supervise banks, manage foreign exchange, advise government. SBP sets monetary policy through the Monetary Policy Committee. SBP licenses and regulates all banks.
chunks.text: State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956 — SBP is the central bank of Pakistan. Functions: issue currency, regulate money supply, supervise banks, manage foreign exchange, advise government. SBP sets monetary policy through the Monetary Policy Committee. SBP licenses and regulates all banks.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Banking regulation — No company may carry on banking business without a license from SBP. Minimum paid-up capital for banks is prescribed by SBP. Banks must maintain cash reserve and liquidity ratios.
chunks.text: Banking regulation — No company may carry on banking business without a license from SBP. Minimum paid-up capital for banks is prescribed by SBP. Banks must maintain cash reserve and liquidity ratios.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Types of banks — (a) Commercial banks (HBL, NBP, UBL, etc.); (b) Islamic banks (Meezan, Dubai Islamic, etc.); (c) Microfinance banks; (d) Development finance institutions (SME Bank, ZTBL). Islamic banking operates on Shariah-compliant principles (Murabaha, Ijara, Musharaka, Mudaraba).

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Depositor protection — Deposits are insured by the Deposit Protection Corporation up to PKR 500,000 per depositor per bank. Banks must maintain secrecy of customer accounts.
chunks.text: Depositor protection — Deposits are insured by the Deposit Protection Corporation up to PKR 500,000 per depositor per bank. Banks must maintain secrecy of customer accounts.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Loans and advances — Banks may grant loans, advances, overdrafts and cash finance. Loans must be secured. NPL (non-performing loan) classification: substandard (90 days overdue), doubtful (180 days), loss (365 days).
chunks.text: Loans and advances — Banks may grant loans, advances, overdrafts and cash finance. Loans must be secured. NPL (non-performing loan) classification: substandard (90 days overdue), doubtful (180 days), loss (365 days).

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Banking Court — Banking disputes involving amounts above PKR 500,000 are tried by Banking Courts. Summary procedure applies. Appeals lie to the High Court within 30 days.
chunks.text: Banking Court — Banking disputes involving amounts above PKR 500,000 are tried by Banking Courts. Summary procedure applies. Appeals lie to the High Court within 30 days.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 — Cheques, promissory notes and bills of exchange are negotiable instruments. A cheque is a bill of exchange drawn on a specified banker. Dishonour of cheque: PPC Section 489-F criminalizes cheque dishonour. Holder must give notice within 30 days. Offender punishable with imprisonment up to 3 years.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 — SBP regulates foreign currency transactions. Restrictions on taking foreign currency out of Pakistan. Authorized dealers (banks) may deal in foreign exchange.
chunks.text: Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947 — SBP regulates foreign currency transactions. Restrictions on taking foreign currency out of Pakistan. Authorized dealers (banks) may deal in foreign exchange.

chunks.title: Banking, Negotiable Instruments and SBP Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Digital banking — SBP has issued regulations for digital/online banking, branchless banking (Raast, JazzCash, Easypaisa), and payment service providers. E-money institutions are regulated by SBP.
chunks.text: Digital banking — SBP has issued regulations for digital/online banking, branchless banking (Raast, JazzCash, Easypaisa), and payment service providers. E-money institutions are regulated by SBP.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Tax Laws of Pakistan — Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) administers federal taxes: Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs, Federal Excise. Source: FBR (fbr.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.
chunks.text: Tax Laws of Pakistan — Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) administers federal taxes: Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs, Federal Excise. Source: FBR (fbr.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 — The primary income tax law. Income tax is charged on: salary, business/profession income, capital gains, property income, dividend, interest, and other sources. Tax rates are progressive for individuals (0% to 35%) and flat for companies (29%).
chunks.text: Income Tax Ordinance, 2001 — The primary income tax law. Income tax is charged on: salary, business/profession income, capital gains, property income, dividend, interest, and other sources. Tax rates are progressive for individuals (0% to 35%) and flat for companies (29%).

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Filer vs Non-Filer — Active taxpayers (filers) who file annual returns benefit from lower withholding tax rates. Non-filers pay higher rates on banking transactions, property purchases, vehicle registration, and utility bills.
chunks.text: Filer vs Non-Filer — Active taxpayers (filers) who file annual returns benefit from lower withholding tax rates. Non-filers pay higher rates on banking transactions, property purchases, vehicle registration, and utility bills.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: NTN Registration — Every person with taxable income must obtain a National Tax Number (NTN). Companies require NTN upon incorporation. NTN is mandatory for property transactions, business registration, and banking.
chunks.text: NTN Registration — Every person with taxable income must obtain a National Tax Number (NTN). Companies require NTN upon incorporation. NTN is mandatory for property transactions, business registration, and banking.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Sales Tax Act, 1990 — Sales tax is charged at 18% on goods supplied in Pakistan. Some services are taxed by provinces under the Sindh Sales Tax, Punjab Sales Tax, etc. Registered persons must file monthly returns.
chunks.text: Sales Tax Act, 1990 — Sales tax is charged at 18% on goods supplied in Pakistan. Some services are taxed by provinces under the Sindh Sales Tax, Punjab Sales Tax, etc. Registered persons must file monthly returns.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Customs Act, 1969 — Customs duties on imports and exports. Valuation of goods, tariff classification, and assessment by Pakistan Customs. Appeals to the Customs Appellate Tribunal, then High Court.
chunks.text: Customs Act, 1969 — Customs duties on imports and exports. Valuation of goods, tariff classification, and assessment by Pakistan Customs. Appeals to the Customs Appellate Tribunal, then High Court.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Federal Excise Act, 2005 — Federal excise duty on certain goods manufactured in Pakistan and on services. Administered by FBR.
chunks.text: Federal Excise Act, 2005 — Federal excise duty on certain goods manufactured in Pakistan and on services. Administered by FBR.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Appellate system — FBR assessments may be appealed: (a) Commissioner (Appeals); (b) Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue; (c) High Court on substantial question of law; (d) Supreme Court.
chunks.text: Appellate system — FBR assessments may be appealed: (a) Commissioner (Appeals); (b) Appellate Tribunal Inland Revenue; (c) High Court on substantial question of law; (d) Supreme Court.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Tax avoidance and evasion — Tax evasion (illegal non-payment) is an offence punishable with imprisonment and fine. Tax avoidance (legal minimization) is distinguished. FBR has anti-avoidance powers.
chunks.text: Tax avoidance and evasion — Tax evasion (illegal non-payment) is an offence punishable with imprisonment and fine. Tax avoidance (legal minimization) is distinguished. FBR has anti-avoidance powers.

chunks.title: Tax Laws of Pakistan (Income Tax, Sales Tax, Customs)
chunks.chunkTitle: Property tax — Provincial governments levy property tax on immovable property (urban immovable property tax). Rates vary by province. Mutation and transfer require payment of capital gains tax and withholding tax.
chunks.text: Property tax — Provincial governments levy property tax on immovable property (urban immovable property tax). Rates vary by province. Mutation and transfer require payment of capital gains tax and withholding tax.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance No. XVIII of 1999) — The primary anti-corruption law in Pakistan. Establishes the National Accountability Bureau (NAB). Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.
chunks.text: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance No. XVIII of 1999) — The primary anti-corruption law in Pakistan. Establishes the National Accountability Bureau (NAB). Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Definitions — 'Holder of public office' includes Presidents, Prime Ministers, federal/provincial ministers, MNAs, MPAs, judges, public servants, government employees, and employees of state-owned corporations. 'Corrupt practice' and 'corruption' defined broadly.
chunks.text: Definitions — 'Holder of public office' includes Presidents, Prime Ministers, federal/provincial ministers, MNAs, MPAs, judges, public servants, government employees, and employees of state-owned corporations. 'Corrupt practice' and 'corruption' defined broadly.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Establishment of NAB — NAB is established as the primary anti-corruption agency. The Chairman is appointed by the President in consultation with the Leader of the House and the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly.
chunks.text: Establishment of NAB — NAB is established as the primary anti-corruption agency. The Chairman is appointed by the President in consultation with the Leader of the House and the Leader of the Opposition in the National Assembly.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: NAB Chairman — The Chairman holds office for a term of 4 years and is eligible for reappointment. The Chairman may not be removed except on grounds of physical/mental incapacity or misconduct.
chunks.text: NAB Chairman — The Chairman holds office for a term of 4 years and is eligible for reappointment. The Chairman may not be removed except on grounds of physical/mental incapacity or misconduct.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: NAB Prosecutor General — The Prosecutor General is appointed by the President on the advice of the Chairman NAB. He is assisted by Deputy Prosecutors General.
chunks.text: NAB Prosecutor General — The Prosecutor General is appointed by the President on the advice of the Chairman NAB. He is assisted by Deputy Prosecutors General.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Offences of corruption — The following are offences: (a) bribery (offering or accepting gratification); (b) criminal breach of trust; (c) cheating, fraud and misappropriation; (d) misuse of authority; (e) assets disproportionate to known sources of income; (f) willful default in payment of government dues.
chunks.text: Offences of corruption — The following are offences: (a) bribery (offering or accepting gratification); (b) criminal breach of trust; (c) cheating, fraud and misappropriation; (d) misuse of authority; (e) assets disproportionate to known sources of income; (f) willful default in payment of government dues.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Graft, bribery — A holder of public office who solicits or accepts any gratification as a motive or reward for doing any official act commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.
chunks.text: Graft, bribery — A holder of public office who solicits or accepts any gratification as a motive or reward for doing any official act commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Criminal breach of trust — A holder of public office who commits criminal breach of trust in respect of public property commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.
chunks.text: Criminal breach of trust — A holder of public office who commits criminal breach of trust in respect of public property commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Cheating, fraud — Fraudulent acquisition of public property or funds. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.
chunks.text: Cheating, fraud — Fraudulent acquisition of public property or funds. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Misuse of authority — Wilful misuse of authority causing loss to the public or gain to any person. Punishment: imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.
chunks.text: Misuse of authority — Wilful misuse of authority causing loss to the public or gain to any person. Punishment: imprisonment up to 10 years and fine.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Assets disproportionate to income — A holder of public office or any other person who holds assets disproportionate to known sources of income commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine. Property acquired through corruption may be forfeited.
chunks.text: Assets disproportionate to income — A holder of public office or any other person who holds assets disproportionate to known sources of income commits an offence. Punishment: imprisonment up to 14 years and fine. Property acquired through corruption may be forfeited.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Willful default — Willful default in payment of tax, duty or other government dues. Punishment: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.
chunks.text: Willful default — Willful default in payment of tax, duty or other government dues. Punishment: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Punishment for abetment — Whoever abets the commission of an offence under this Ordinance shall be punished with the same punishment as the principal offender.
chunks.text: Punishment for abetment — Whoever abets the commission of an offence under this Ordinance shall be punished with the same punishment as the principal offender.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Investigation — NAB may investigate any alleged offence. The Chairman may authorize investigation. NAB has powers to arrest, search, seize, and freeze assets.
chunks.text: Investigation — NAB may investigate any alleged offence. The Chairman may authorize investigation. NAB has powers to arrest, search, seize, and freeze assets.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Arrest and bail — NAB may arrest without warrant. Bail is not a matter of right for NAB offences. The court may grant bail only if there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and unlikely to commit further offences.
chunks.text: Arrest and bail — NAB may arrest without warrant. Bail is not a matter of right for NAB offences. The court may grant bail only if there are reasonable grounds to believe the accused is not guilty and unlikely to commit further offences.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Trial — Offences under this Ordinance are tried by the Accountability Court, established by the federal government. The court has exclusive jurisdiction. Trial must be concluded within 30 days, extendable up to 90 days.
chunks.text: Trial — Offences under this Ordinance are tried by the Accountability Court, established by the federal government. The court has exclusive jurisdiction. Trial must be concluded within 30 days, extendable up to 90 days.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Burden of proof — Where any property is alleged to be disproportionate to known sources of income, the burden of proving the property was lawfully acquired lies on the accused.
chunks.text: Burden of proof — Where any property is alleged to be disproportionate to known sources of income, the burden of proving the property was lawfully acquired lies on the accused.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Plea bargain — An accused may enter into a plea bargain with NAB, agreeing to return the assets/proceeds of corruption. Upon return, the court may release the accused on such terms as deemed appropriate.
chunks.text: Plea bargain — An accused may enter into a plea bargain with NAB, agreeing to return the assets/proceeds of corruption. Upon return, the court may release the accused on such terms as deemed appropriate.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Appeal — Appeals from the Accountability Court lie to the High Court within 30 days. Further appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
chunks.text: Appeal — Appeals from the Accountability Court lie to the High Court within 30 days. Further appeal to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Voluntary return — A person who has obtained property through corrupt practices may voluntarily return it to NAB before commencement of trial. NAB may close the inquiry.
chunks.text: Voluntary return — A person who has obtained property through corrupt practices may voluntarily return it to NAB before commencement of trial. NAB may close the inquiry.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Protection of witnesses — The court may keep the identity of witnesses confidential, hold in-camera proceedings, and take measures to protect witnesses.
chunks.text: Protection of witnesses — The court may keep the identity of witnesses confidential, hold in-camera proceedings, and take measures to protect witnesses.

chunks.title: National Accountability Bureau Ordinance, 1999 (Ordinance XVIII of 1999)
chunks.chunkTitle: Review of NAB amendments — The Supreme Court of Pakistan has reviewed certain provisions of NAB law. Key amendments by Parliament on various occasions have been subject to judicial scrutiny. Current law reflects amendments.
chunks.text: Review of NAB amendments — The Supreme Court of Pakistan has reviewed certain provisions of NAB law. Key amendments by Parliament on various occasions have been subject to judicial scrutiny. Current law reflects amendments.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: The Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act No. XXVII of 1997) — Provides for the prevention of terrorism, sectarian violence and for the establishment of Anti-Terrorism Courts. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.
chunks.text: The Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act No. XXVII of 1997) — Provides for the prevention of terrorism, sectarian violence and for the establishment of Anti-Terrorism Courts. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Definitions — 'Terrorist act' means any act or threat of action that: (a) involves grievous violence against a person, damage to property, or interference with critical infrastructure; (b) is designed to create a sense of fear in the public, or intimidate the government; (c) is for a political, religious or ideological purpose. 'Terrorist' includes any person who commits, attempts, or abets a terrorist act.
chunks.text: Definitions — 'Terrorist act' means any act or threat of action that: (a) involves grievous violence against a person, damage to property, or interference with critical infrastructure; (b) is designed to create a sense of fear in the public, or intimidate the government; (c) is for a political, religious or ideological purpose. 'Terrorist' includes any person who commits, attempts, or abets a terrorist act.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Punishment for terrorist acts — A person who commits a terrorist act shall be punished with: (a) death or imprisonment for life if the act causes death; (b) imprisonment up to 30 years if the act causes hurt; (c) imprisonment up to 15 years for other cases.
chunks.text: Punishment for terrorist acts — A person who commits a terrorist act shall be punished with: (a) death or imprisonment for life if the act causes death; (b) imprisonment up to 30 years if the act causes hurt; (c) imprisonment up to 15 years for other cases.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Punishment for financing terrorism — Whoever provides, collects or makes available funds for terrorism shall be punished with imprisonment of 10 to 25 years and fine.
chunks.text: Punishment for financing terrorism — Whoever provides, collects or makes available funds for terrorism shall be punished with imprisonment of 10 to 25 years and fine.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Punishment for membership of terrorist groups — Being a member of a proscribed organization or terrorist group: imprisonment up to 10 years.
chunks.text: Punishment for membership of terrorist groups — Being a member of a proscribed organization or terrorist group: imprisonment up to 10 years.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Enhanced penalties — Offences under PPC when committed with terrorist intent attract enhanced penalties as specified in the Schedule to this Act.
chunks.text: Enhanced penalties — Offences under PPC when committed with terrorist intent attract enhanced penalties as specified in the Schedule to this Act.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Proscribed organizations — The federal government may proscribe organizations involved in terrorism. Proscription is notified in the official Gazette and laid before Parliament.
chunks.text: Proscribed organizations — The federal government may proscribe organizations involved in terrorism. Proscription is notified in the official Gazette and laid before Parliament.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Habeas corpus for missing persons — The High Court or Supreme Court may order production of any person alleged to be in illegal custody. Special provisions for terrorism-related detentions.
chunks.text: Habeas corpus for missing persons — The High Court or Supreme Court may order production of any person alleged to be in illegal custody. Special provisions for terrorism-related detentions.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Arrest and detention — A person arrested under this Act may be detained for up to 90 days for investigation. Magistrate must authorize detention beyond 24 hours.
chunks.text: Arrest and detention — A person arrested under this Act may be detained for up to 90 days for investigation. Magistrate must authorize detention beyond 24 hours.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Anti-Terrorism Courts — The federal government may establish Anti-Terrorism Courts (ATC). ATCs have exclusive jurisdiction over offences under this Act and scheduled offences committed with terrorist intent.
chunks.text: Anti-Terrorism Courts — The federal government may establish Anti-Terrorism Courts (ATC). ATCs have exclusive jurisdiction over offences under this Act and scheduled offences committed with terrorist intent.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Trial by ATC — Trials before ATC are conducted summarily. The court must conclude trial within 7 working days, extendable up to 30 days. Adjournments are limited.
chunks.text: Trial by ATC — Trials before ATC are conducted summarily. The court must conclude trial within 7 working days, extendable up to 30 days. Adjournments are limited.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Evidence — Qanun-e-Shahadat Order applies. The court may receive evidence in the absence of the accused if the accused has absconded. Confessions made to police are admissible subject to conditions.
chunks.text: Evidence — Qanun-e-Shahadat Order applies. The court may receive evidence in the absence of the accused if the accused has absconded. Confessions made to police are admissible subject to conditions.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Appeal — Appeals from ATC lie to the High Court within 30 days. Decisions of the High Court may be appealed to the Supreme Court within 30 days.
chunks.text: Appeal — Appeals from ATC lie to the High Court within 30 days. Decisions of the High Court may be appealed to the Supreme Court within 30 days.

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)

chunks.title: Anti-Terrorism Act, 1997 (Act XXVII of 1997)
chunks.chunkTitle: Protection of judges, prosecutors and witnesses — No suit or proceeding shall lie against any judge, prosecutor or authorized officer for acts done in good faith under this Act. Witness protection measures may be ordered.

chunks.chunkTitle: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan — Consolidated coverage of key women's legal protections. Sources: Pakistan Code, Ministry of Human Rights, Provincial Assemblies. Status: VARIOUS (federal + provincial).

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Protection against Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2010 — Applicable to all workplaces, public and private. Every organization must constitute an Inquiry Committee (3 members, majority women, chairperson must be a woman). Complaint procedure: (a) written complaint to Inquiry Committee; (b) inquiry completed within 30 days; (c) extension of 30 days if needed. Punishment: removal from service, fine, or both. Appeals to Ombudsperson.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Criminal Law Amendment (Protection of Women) Act, 2006 — Amended the Hudood Ordinances. Separated zina (adultery/fornication) from PPC provisions. Rape now dealt under PPC Sections 375-376 (not under Hudood). Burden of proof remains with prosecution. False accusation of zina now an offence.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Acid Control and Acid Crime Prevention Act, 2010 — Defines acid throwing as a specific offence under PPC Section 336-B. Punishment: imprisonment for life or 14 years minimum, and fine of PKR 1 million. The court may also order compensation to the victim. Medical treatment must be provided by the state.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Women in Distress and Detention Fund Act, 2011 — Establishes a fund under the Ministry of Human Rights to provide financial assistance, legal aid, medical care, shelter and rehabilitation to women in distress or detention.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Domestic Violence — Provincial legislation: (a) Punjab Protection of Women against Violence Act 2016: protection orders, residence orders, monetary relief, prohibition of violence. (b) Sindh Domestic Violence Act 2013: similar protections. (c) KPK Domestic Violence Act 2021: protection and prevention. Complaints may be made to Protection Officers. Courts may issue interim protection orders.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Women's Right to Inheritance — Muslim Personal Law (Shariat) Application Act 1962 confirms women's right to inheritance. The PPC (Section 498-A) criminalizes depriving a woman of inheritance. Women entitled to specific shares under Islamic inheritance law (Quranic heirs).

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Dowry and Bridal Gifts — Dowry and bridal gifts (Jahez) are the property of the wife. She may recover them through civil suit or family court. Demand for dowry as a consideration for marriage is prohibited.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Nikkah Registration — Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, Section 5: Every marriage solemnized under Muslim law must be registered with the Nikah Registrar. Failure to register is an offence. The Nikah Nama (marriage contract) is a legally binding document.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Women's Right to Maintenance — Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, Section 9: If a husband fails to maintain his wife, the wife may apply to the Family Court which may order maintenance at a rate deemed reasonable.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Protection of Women against Violence — Provincial Domestic Violence laws provide: (a) protection orders preventing the accused from committing violence; (b) residence orders giving the victim exclusive use of shared residence; (c) monetary relief for expenses; (d) custody of minor children to the victim.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Workplace Harassment — The Harassment Act 2010 applies to all employees, interns, patients, students and visitors. Sexual harassment defined broadly including unwelcome advances, requests for sexual favors, verbal/non-verbal conduct. Employers must display the Code of Conduct. Complaint mechanism includes Ombudsperson at provincial level.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Women Prisoners — Special provisions: (a) women prisoners must be kept separate from men; (b) female guards must supervise women prisoners; (c) infants may stay with mothers in prison; (d) pregnant women entitled to special nutrition and medical care.

chunks.title: Women Protection Laws of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Gender-Based Violence Shelters — Provincial governments maintain shelter homes for women in distress. These include: Dar-ul-Amans (Punjab), Women Crisis Centers (Sindh), Shelter Homes (KPK, Balochistan). Services: safe accommodation, legal aid, medical care, counseling, vocational training.

chunks.chunkTitle: Helplines — National Helpline for Women: 1043 (Ministry of Human Rights). Provincial helplines: Punjab Women Helpline 1043, Sindh Women Helpline 1080. Police Women Complaint Cells at every police station. Madadgar 15: emergency police assistance.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Definitions — 'Environment' includes air, water, land, forests, fisheries, wildlife, and the interrelationship between them. 'Environmental pollution' means the contamination of the environment through discharge of emissions, effluents or waste. 'Hazardous waste' includes radioactive waste.

chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency (Pak-EPA) — Pak-EPA is established as the federal regulatory authority. It has powers to: (a) conduct environmental assessment; (b) establish standards for environmental quality; (c) enforce compliance; (d) enter and inspect premises.

chunks.chunkTitle: Provincial EPAs — Each province has established its own Environmental Protection Agency (EPA Punjab, Sindh EPA, KPK EPA, Balochistan EPA) to enforce environmental laws within the province.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Initial Environmental Examination (IEE) — Any project likely to cause adverse environmental effects must submit an IEE to the EPA. The EPA may approve, reject or require an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA).

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) — Major projects must submit a comprehensive EIA to the EPA. The EPA must make the EIA publicly available. Public hearings may be conducted. Approval is required before construction begins.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Prohibition of pollution — No person shall discharge or emit any effluent, emission or waste in excess of the prescribed standards. Non-compliance attracts penalties: imprisonment up to 2 years or fine up to PKR 1 million, or both. Continuing default: additional fine of PKR 100,000 per day.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Handling of hazardous substances — No person shall import, transport, handle or dispose of hazardous substances except in accordance with regulations. Penalty: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to PKR 10 million.
chunks.text: Handling of hazardous substances — No person shall import, transport, handle or dispose of hazardous substances except in accordance with regulations. Penalty: imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to PKR 10 million.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Environmental tribunals — Federal and Provincial Environmental Tribunals are established to adjudicate environmental offences. The tribunal consists of a judicial member and a technical member. Appeals lie to the High Court.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: National Environmental Quality Standards (NEQS) — NEQS have been prescribed for: industrial gaseous emissions, industrial liquid effluents, municipal liquid effluents, ambient air quality, drinking water quality, noise levels, and vehicular emissions.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Climate change — The federal government has established the Ministry of Climate Change. Pakistan is a signatory to the Paris Agreement on climate change. National Climate Change Policy 2012 and National Adaptation Plan guide climate action.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Environmental protection orders — EPA may issue environmental protection orders directing a person to: (a) cease polluting activity; (b) install pollution control equipment; (c) restore the environment; (d) pay compensation.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Forest laws — Provincial forest departments administer forests under the Forest Act 1927 as adapted. Protected forests, reserved forests, and village forests are recognized categories. Deforestation without permission is an offence.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Wildlife protection — Provincial wildlife laws protect endangered species. Hunting, trapping, or trading protected species is prohibited. National parks, wildlife sanctuaries and game reserves are protected areas.

chunks.title: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997 and Related Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Public interest litigation — Courts in Pakistan have recognized environmental rights as part of the right to life under Article 9 of the Constitution. Public interest litigation is an effective tool for environmental protection.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 (Ordinance No. XXII of 2000) — Provides for the protection, treatment and rehabilitation of juvenile offenders. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT (amended by JJSO Amendment Act 2018).
chunks.text: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 (Ordinance No. XXII of 2000) — Provides for the protection, treatment and rehabilitation of juvenile offenders. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT (amended by JJSO Amendment Act 2018).

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Definitions — 'Juvenile' means a person who has not attained the age of 18 years. 'Juvenile offender' means a juvenile who has been charged with or found guilty of an offence. Male juveniles (under 18) and female juveniles (under 18) are covered.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Separation of juveniles — Juvenile offenders must be kept separate from adult offenders in police stations, jails and other custodial facilities. No juvenile shall be kept in a police lockup for more than 24 hours.
chunks.text: Separation of juveniles — Juvenile offenders must be kept separate from adult offenders in police stations, jails and other custodial facilities. No juvenile shall be kept in a police lockup for more than 24 hours.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Arrest procedure — The officer arresting a juvenile must immediately inform the parent or guardian. If no parent/guardian available, the officer must inform the Juvenile Court or probation officer.
chunks.text: Arrest procedure — The officer arresting a juvenile must immediately inform the parent or guardian. If no parent/guardian available, the officer must inform the Juvenile Court or probation officer.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Juvenile Court — Special Juvenile Courts may be established. Where no separate Juvenile Court exists, the District and Sessions Judge or a Magistrate designated by the High Court conducts juvenile proceedings. Proceedings are conducted in camera.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Bail for juveniles — Juveniles charged with bailable or non-bailable offences may be released on bail, unless there are reasonable grounds that release would expose the juvenile to moral or physical danger or defeat the ends of justice.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Disposal of cases — Cases involving juveniles must be disposed of as expeditiously as possible. If not disposed of within 4 months, the court must record reasons for delay.
chunks.text: Disposal of cases — Cases involving juveniles must be disposed of as expeditiously as possible. If not disposed of within 4 months, the court must record reasons for delay.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Probation and supervision — The court may release a juvenile on probation under the supervision of a probation officer. Conditions may include attendance at school, vocational training, or residence at a specified place.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Sentencing of juveniles — No juvenile shall be sentenced to death, life imprisonment, or imprisonment for more than 7 years. The preferred disposition is: (a) release on advice/admonition; (b) release on probation; (c) community service; (d) custody in a juvenile rehabilitation center; (e) fine or compensation.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Rehabilitation centers — The government must establish and maintain juvenile rehabilitation centers. Centers provide education, vocational training, medical care and counseling. Juveniles are segregated by age and gender.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Prohibition of handcuffing — No juvenile shall be handcuffed or chained. Restraint may only be used in extreme circumstances with court permission.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Education and training — Juvenile rehabilitation centers must provide: (a) basic education up to at least middle level; (b) vocational training in trades; (c) religious and moral instruction.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Aftercare — Aftercare programs assist juveniles released from rehabilitation centers to reintegrate into society. Aftercare includes support for employment, continued education, and family reunification.

chunks.title: Juvenile Justice System Ordinance, 2000 and Child Protection Laws
chunks.chunkTitle: Child protection — The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Child Protection and Welfare Act 2010, Punjab Child Protection and Welfare Bureau, and Sindh Child Protection Authority Act provide additional child protection mechanisms.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Police Order, 2002 (Chief Executive's Order No. 22 of 2002) — Reorganizes policing in Pakistan, replacing the Police Act 1861. Source: Pakistan Code (pakistancode.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT (provincial adaptations may vary).

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Fundamental principles — The police shall be a professional, impartial and service-oriented organization. Police functions include: (a) protection of life, liberty and property; (b) prevention and detection of crime; (c) prosecution of offenders; (d) regulation of public assemblies; (e) traffic management.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Duties of police — Every police officer shall: (a) prevent the commission of offences; (b) collect intelligence affecting public peace; (c) register FIR and investigate cognizable offences; (d) arrest offenders; (e) execute warrants; (f) provide assistance in natural disasters; (g) regulate traffic; (h) assist the public in emergencies.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Police stations and jurisdiction — A police station is the basic unit of policing. Each police station has territorial jurisdiction. The Station House Officer (SHO) is in charge. Each police station maintains: station diary, daily diary (Roznamcha), FIR register, case diaries, and property register.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Station House Officer (SHO) — The SHO has overall responsibility for the police station including supervision of investigation, maintenance of law and order, and public service. The SHO must be present at the station or available on communication at all times.

chunks.chunkTitle: Registration of FIR — Section 154 CrPC read with Police Order: The police MUST register FIR for cognizable offences. Refusal to register is a dereliction of duty. Remedies for FIR refusal: (a) complaint to Deputy Superintendent of Police; (b) application to Sessions Judge/Judicial Magistrate under Section 22-A/22-B CrPC; (c) writ petition under Article 199.

Remedies for FIR refusal: (a) complaint to Deputy Superintendent of Police; (b) application to Sessions Judge/Judicial Magistrate under Section 22-A/22-B CrPC; (c) writ petition under Article 199.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Investigation — Investigation includes: visiting the crime scene, collecting evidence, recording statements (Section 161 CrPC), conducting searches, arresting suspects, and preparing charge sheet (challan). Investigation must be completed within 14 days for most offences; extendable up to 90 days with court permission.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Public Safety Commissions — Public Safety Commissions at federal, provincial and district levels oversee police performance and ensure independence from political influence. Commissions review complaints and make recommendations.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Police complaints authority — Citizens may file complaints against police officers for: (a) refusal to register FIR; (b) illegal detention; (c) torture or abuse; (d) corruption; (e) misuse of authority. Complaints may be filed with the District Public Safety Commission or the Provincial Police Officer.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Women police stations — Women police stations exist in major cities. Women police officers handle complaints from women. Staff are specially trained in gender-sensitive investigation and victim support.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Community policing — SHO and police officers are encouraged to engage with local communities through citizen liaison committees, community forums and police-community partnerships.

chunks.title: Police Order, 2002
chunks.chunkTitle: Missing persons — Police must promptly register FIR for missing persons. Investigation must include tracing through mobile data, CCTV footage, hospitals, jails and morgues. Quarterly progress reports must be submitted to the High Court.
