chunks.title: International Travel, Visa & Immigration Basics for Pakistani Citizens
chunks.chunkTitle: A practical, jurisdiction-neutral pre-travel document checklist for a Pakistani traveller: valid Pakistani passport (check expiry vs the destination's required validity); the required visa or residence/work permit for the destination (from the official authority); proof of funds/financial means if the destination requires it; return/onward ticket and accommodation details if required; any invitation or sponsorship letter; travel/medical insurance if required by the destination; and attested supporting documents where the destination demands them. Which of these apply, and in what exact form, is set by the DESTINATION country and can change — always verify on the official government/embassy source. This is general preparation guidance, not a country-specific requirement list. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: International Travel, Visa & Immigration Basics for Pakistani Citizens
chunks.chunkTitle: This knowledge base uses a source-driven approach for foreign countries rather than a fixed hardcoded country list, and it deliberately does not claim to cover every country's law. For any given destination, the authoritative sources are that country's official government portals — typically its Ministry/Department of Foreign Affairs or Immigration (visas), its education ministry or accreditation body (study), and its labour ministry (work permits). INSAaf provides verified Pakistan-facing cross-border guidance for the countries and topics covered by its current official-source corpus, and shows coverage boundaries where information is not verified. Where a specific foreign requirement is not in the verified corpus, the system says so and points to the official source instead of guessing. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: International Travel, Visa & Immigration Basics for Pakistani Citizens
chunks.chunkTitle: For Gulf/GCC countries where many Pakistani workers go (e.g., Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Kuwait), the relevant authorities are typically the country's Ministry/Federal Authority for immigration & visas and its Ministry of Human Resources/Labour (for work permits, wages and labour complaints), each with official national portals that change over time. Because these requirements and portals are updated often and differ per country, INSAaf does not hardcode specific rules; the correct approach is: (a) verify the destination country's official immigration/labour portals for the current visa/work rules; and (b) for Pakistan-side emigration clearance and worker protection, use the Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment (https://beoe.gov.pk) and the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD (https://ophrd.gov.pk), plus the local Pakistani mission. Unpaid wages or passport withholding abroad are primarily foreign labour-law matters with consular support. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: International Travel, Visa & Immigration Basics for Pakistani Citizens
chunks.chunkTitle: For short stays in much of Europe, the Schengen visa framework applies to many (not all) European states; applications are made to the consulate/authorised centre of the country that is the main destination. Rules, fees, required documents and appointment systems are set by the individual Schengen state and change — read them from that country's official embassy/consulate or immigration source. For work or study in a specific European country (e.g., Germany, France, Italy, Netherlands, Türkiye), that country runs its own national visa/residence procedures through its official portals. INSAaf does not fabricate country-specific European requirements; it directs to the relevant official national source and, on the Pakistan side, to document attestation via MOFA. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Some foreign visa/employment/residence processes ask a Pakistani applicant for a Police Character Certificate / good-standing certificate and a medical fitness test from an approved panel. The Police Character Certificate in Pakistan is obtained through the relevant provincial police channels; medical examinations, where required, are usually done at clinics/centres APPROVED BY THE DESTINATION COUNTRY (the list of approved centres is country-specific and changes). Whether these are required, and by which provider, must come from the destination country's official instructions — do not assume a universal rule. On the Pakistan side, such certificates are PAKISTAN-issued documents (may then need attestation for foreign use). Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: International Travel, Visa & Immigration Basics for Pakistani Citizens
chunks.chunkTitle: Remitting money to Pakistan is commonly done through licensed banks and licensed money-transfer/remittance operators operating in the host country. Receiving incentives (such as government remittance schemes on official exchange-rate channels) and any tax treatment are set by Pakistani authorities including the State Bank of Pakistan and the Federal Board of Revenue — these programs and rates change and must be confirmed on official Pakistani sources (e.g., https://www.sbp.org.pk, https://fbr.gov.pk). Using unlicensed informal channels can risk funds and legal compliance. Jurisdiction: sending may be regulated by the host country's rules and receiving by Pakistan's — both sides can apply. This is awareness guidance, not tax or financial advice. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: Overseas employment for Pakistanis involves TWO jurisdictions that must be kept separate: (A) the PAKISTAN side — lawful recruitment, emigration clearance and worker protection regulated by the Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment (BE&OE, https://beoe.gov.pk) under the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & Human Resource Development (https://ophrd.gov.pk), operating under the Emigration Ordinance, 1979; and (B) the DESTINATION-COUNTRY side — that country's work-visa, labour and employment laws, which govern the actual job, contract, wages and working conditions. A Pakistani worker abroad is protected mainly by the host country's labour law, with consular and Pakistan-side emigration channels as support. INSAaf gives Pakistan-facing procedure and directs to the correct authorities; it does not invent job agencies, salaries or "verified" vacancies. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: To seek work abroad lawfully through a recruiter, use only recruitment agents REGISTERED with the Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment. The official online portal for registered recruiters and overseas job listings is the Federal Recruiting Agents / e-Migrate system operated by BE&OE (accessed via https://beoe.gov.pk). Before paying any money to an agent, verify that the agent and the specific job offer are listed/registered on the official BE&OE system. Paying an unregistered agent or an "agent" who promises a job outside the official system is a common route to fraud. Do not rely on WhatsApp/social-media job posts without checking them against the official register. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: For certain categories of overseas employment, an Emigration Clearance Certificate (ECC) from the Protector of Emigrants (an officer of BE&OE) is required before a Pakistani worker can travel on a work visa. Emigration clearance generally requires a properly attested employment contract and verification that the recruitment channel is legitimate; it exists to protect workers from abusive contracts and trafficking. Whether clearance is mandatory depends on the destination and job type, and the process/requirements are set by BE&OE and can change — confirm current rules via https://beoe.gov.pk. Jurisdiction: emigration clearance is a PAKISTAN (federal) requirement applied before departure. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: Before departing for overseas work, the worker should have a clear written employment contract that is properly attested (through the destination country's relevant mission/authority and, for Pakistan-side purposes, verified by BE&OE). Key terms to check: job title, wage amount and currency, working hours, overtime, leave, medical/insurance, accommodation and transport, probation, termination and repatriation. A contract that is vague on wages or that requires the worker to pay excessive "fees" is a red flag. The contract is the primary evidence in any later wage or treatment dispute, so keep signed copies. Details of attestation/clearance requirements change and must be confirmed with BE&OE. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: A Pakistani worker abroad has rights under the HOST COUNTRY'S labour law — including rights to timely payment of wages, to the working conditions stated in the contract, to a safe workplace, and to file a complaint with the local labour authority. Pakistani law does NOT override the foreign country's employment rules for work performed there; instead, Pakistan's role is consular assistance and, for recruitment fraud, action against unregistered agents through BE&OE. To enforce wage or contract claims, the primary route is the destination country's labour ministry/courts, supported where appropriate by the Pakistani mission (find via https://www.mofa.gov.pk). Do not answer an overseas wage dispute with Pakistani labour law alone — jurisdiction matters. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: If an employer abroad does not pay wages: (1) gather evidence — the attested contract, pay records, messages, attendance; (2) file a complaint with the destination country's labour ministry/authority (this is the enforcement body under foreign law); (3) seek consular assistance from the nearest Pakistani mission (https://www.mofa.gov.pk), which can help communicate, refer to local legal aid/lawyers, and, in serious cases, raise welfare with local authorities; (4) for recruitment-related fraud on the Pakistan side, complain to BE&OE (https://beoe.gov.pk). Where a worker needs to return home without funds, the mission may assist with an emergency travel document and, in defined hardship cases, facilitate repatriation support. Outcomes depend on foreign law; no result is guaranteed. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: Withholding a worker's passport is a recognised abuse indicator and, in many countries, is unlawful. If an employer abroad confiscates a Pakistani passport: report it to the local police (foreign jurisdiction) and contact the nearest Pakistani mission (https://www.mofa.gov.pk); the mission can assist in obtaining a replacement/emergency travel document and can raise the welfare concern. Passport confiscation is also a strong indicator of potential trafficking/forced labour — treat it as a safety issue, not merely a contractual dispute. The legal consequences for the employer are determined by the host country's law. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: Potential human-trafficking / forced-labour indicators relevant to overseas Pakistani workers: passport or documents withheld; movement restricted; unpaid or withheld wages; debt bondage ("you owe the agent/employer"); threats, intimidation or violence; forced overtime or work different from the contract; confiscated communication devices; being recruited outside the official BE&OE channel. If trafficking is suspected, prioritise immediate safety, contact the host country's police/helpline and the nearest Pakistani mission (https://www.mofa.gov.pk), and report the recruitment abuse to BE&OE (https://beoe.gov.pk). Pakistan addresses trafficking through its own laws (for example the Prevention and Control of Human Trafficking Act, 2020) on the Pakistan side, while exploitation occurring abroad is prosecuted under the foreign country's law. This is safety guidance, not a legal diagnosis. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Overseas Employment, Emigration Clearance & Migrant Worker Protection
chunks.issuingAuthority: Bureau of Emigration & Overseas Employment / Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD
chunks.chunkTitle: Where an overseas Pakistani is stranded — due to abandonment by an employer, loss of documents, hospitalisation, or destitution — the nearest Pakistani mission (directory via https://www.mofa.gov.pk) is the first point of contact for welfare assistance and can help with emergency travel documents to return to Pakistan. Repatriation support, eligibility and process are determined by the mission and by the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis & HRD / relevant welfare schemes (https://ophrd.gov.pk), and can change. The mission's role is assistance and facilitation; it is not an entitlement to a guaranteed outcome, and it does not substitute for the host country's own legal processes. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Study Abroad, Foreign Universities, Scholarships & HEC Attestation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan / Official Foreign Sources
chunks.chunkTitle: A Pakistani student pursuing education abroad deals with TWO jurisdictions: (A) the PAKISTAN side — recognition/attestation of Pakistani academic credentials, which is handled by the Higher Education Commission (HEC, https://www.hec.gov.pk) for higher-education degrees and by the relevant boards/HPD-type bodies for earlier levels; and (B) the DESTINATION-COUNTRY side — admission to a foreign institution (governed by that institution) and the student visa/residence permit (governed by that country's immigration law). INSAaf explains the Pakistan-facing steps and routes to official foreign sources; it does NOT fabricate any university's admission requirements, deadlines, fees or scholarship criteria. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Study Abroad, Foreign Universities, Scholarships & HEC Attestation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan / Official Foreign Sources
chunks.chunkTitle: For a Pakistani degree to be accepted by a foreign university or employer, the academic documents usually need attestation. HEC Pakistan provides degree/diploma attestation (and an online "Degree Attestation / HEC Digital Attestation" service) at https://www.hec.gov.pk. Depending on the destination country, attested documents may then also need MOFA attestation and the destination mission's legalization (see document attestation). HEC also handles recognition/equivalence questions for foreign qualifications being used in Pakistan. Specific document lists, portals and fees change — always use HEC's official site as the authority. Jurisdiction: HEC attestation is a PAKISTAN-side process. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Study Abroad, Foreign Universities, Scholarships & HEC Attestation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan / Official Foreign Sources
chunks.chunkTitle: A Pakistani who studies abroad and returns may need the FOREIGN degree recognised/evaluated in Pakistan for employment or further study. This recognition/equivalence is dealt with by HEC (for higher education) under its recognition of foreign institutions/degrees framework — see https://www.hec.gov.pk. Whether a particular foreign institution or program is recognised depends on HEC's current lists and criteria, which change. Conversely, a foreign university deciding whether to accept a Pakistani degree applies its OWN admissions rules plus any attestation it requires. Do not assume a specific foreign qualification is or is not recognised in Pakistan without checking HEC's official determination. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Study Abroad, Foreign Universities, Scholarships & HEC Attestation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan / Official Foreign Sources
chunks.chunkTitle: General, jurisdiction-neutral steps to seek admission at a foreign university as a Pakistani applicant: (1) choose an institution and program and read ITS official admissions page (requirements come from the university, not third parties); (2) meet the stated academic prerequisites and any language test the university requires; (3) prepare transcripts/degrees (attested if required); (4) apply through the university's official application portal by its real deadline; (5) once offered a place, use the official acceptance letter for the destination country's student-visa application. Fees, tests (such as language proficiency) and documents vary entirely by institution and country and must be read from the official source. No admission is guaranteed. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Study Abroad, Foreign Universities, Scholarships & HEC Attestation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) Pakistan / Official Foreign Sources
chunks.chunkTitle: A student visa/residence permit is issued by the DESTINATION country under its own immigration law, after (and usually conditional on) acceptance by a recognised institution. Common elements across many countries — to be verified with the specific official source, not assumed — include: a valid offer of admission from an approved institution, proof of sufficient funds/tuition payment, language proficiency, health insurance, and sometimes a medical exam or police clearance. The authoritative rules are on the destination country's official immigration portal (for example GOV.UK for the UK, USCIS/SEVP-linked guidance and travel.state.gov for the USA, IRCC for Canada, Home Affairs for Australia, DAAD/embedded national portals for Germany). INSAaf does not state a single universal student-visa rule. Jurisdiction: FOREIGN. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan's foreign policy is formulated and executed principally by the MINISTRY OF FOREIGN AFFAIRS (MOFA), Government of Pakistan — official portal https://www.mofa.gov.pk. MOFA manages Pakistan's diplomatic relations, its network of embassies/high commissions/consulates abroad, treaty work, and consular policy affecting overseas Pakistanis. Key decision-making on foreign policy involves the federal executive (Prime Minister / Cabinet and the National Security machinery) with Parliament's role on ratification of certain instruments. This entry describes publicly documented institutional structure only; it provides no classified or speculative material and does not turn political opinion into legal guidance. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan's diplomatic missions abroad (embassies in non-Commonwealth capitals, high commissions in Commonwealth capitals, and consulates general in key cities) perform two broad functions: DIPLOMATIC (relations with the host government) and CONSULAR (services to Pakistani citizens and visa/entry facilitation). The heads of mission are accredited under the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations; consular posts operate under the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations. For a citizen's practical purposes, the consular section of the mission covering their area is the contact point (directory: https://www.mofa.gov.pk). Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan is a member of a number of well-documented international and regional organizations relevant to its citizens, including: the United Nations (UN); the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC); the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO); the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC); the Developing-8 (D-8); the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO, as a member); and the Commonwealth of Nations. Membership can affect visas, trade, labour mobility and dispute fora, but the specific rights for an individual depend on each organization's instruments and each state's implementation. This is public, stable, factual membership information; INSAaf does not speculate on policy outcomes. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: A treaty or international agreement binds a state under international law according to its own terms and that state's domestic process for signature/ratification/accession. In Pakistan, the treaty-making and ratification function is coordinated by MOFA, and ratification of treaties that require changes to domestic law involves Parliament. For a user asking what agreement exists between Pakistan and X on topic Y, the correct approach is to consult MOFA's official records / the relevant ministry's publication of the agreement, because treaty status (signed / in force / party reservations) is precise and must not be guessed. INSAaf does not claim any specific agreement exists unless it can be verified from an official source. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan has historically concluded bilateral arrangements on labour/worker recruitment and welfare with several destination countries (particularly in the Gulf and elsewhere). The existence, current status and detailed terms of any specific bilateral workers' agreement are set by the concerned governments and change over time; they are administered on the Pakistan side through the Ministry of Overseas Pakistanis and Human Resource Development / Bureau of Emigration (https://ophrd.gov.pk, https://beoe.gov.pk) and MOFA (https://www.mofa.gov.pk). For a question like "Is there a workers' agreement between Pakistan and country X?", INSAaf explains where the authoritative answer lives and does NOT fabricate the agreement's existence or its terms. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: EXTRADITION (surrendering a person accused/convicted to another state for trial or punishment) and MUTUAL LEGAL ASSISTANCE (MLA: cooperation to gather evidence, serve documents, or enforce certain orders across borders) are governed by a combination of bilateral treaties, multilateral conventions and each country's domestic law. There is no single universal rule: whether Pakistan can extradite to, or provide MLA with, a particular country depends on the specific treaty/arrangement in force between the two states (and, absent a treaty, on domestic legal bases and reciprocity). These relationships are precise and must not be assumed. Authoritative sources: MOFA and the relevant Pakistani legal framework, plus the foreign state's official channels. INSAaf states the concept and the routing, and explicitly declines to confirm any specific extradition arrangement without a verified source. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.title: Pakistan Foreign Policy, Missions, Treaties & International Cooperation
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Government of Pakistan
chunks.chunkTitle: Service of process (formally delivering court documents such as a claim, summons or notice) across borders is regulated by international arrangements (for example the Hague Service Convention among its parties) and/or bilateral treaties and the domestic law of the country where service is to be effected. Whether a particular method of serving a document abroad is valid depends on the law of the country where the case is (foreign), the law of the country where the person is, and any applicable convention between them. A foreign court notice served on a Pakistani is therefore a foreign-jurisdiction matter to be responded to under that foreign country's rules. Do not assume Pakistani service rules validate service abroad, or vice versa. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

For an ordinary citizen's cross-border legal problem, the practical fora are the domestic courts/authorities of the relevant country, supported by consular channels and applicable treaties. INSAaf keeps this section at the level of publicly documented structure and does not represent international fora as a substitute for local legal remedy. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Pakistan's Citizenship Act, 1951 governs Pakistani nationality. Pakistan permits DUAL NATIONALITY only with a defined list of countries announced by the Federal Government, and the list is subject to change by official notification. A Pakistani who acquires a nationality that is NOT on the permitted list may lose Pakistani citizenship by operation of law, and a person ceasing to be a Pakistani has different rights (for example regarding certain property, franchise or government posts). Because the permitted-countries list and the rules change by official notification, the current list must be confirmed from MOFA / the relevant federal notification (https://www.mofa.gov.pk) and NADRA (https://nadra.gov.pk) rather than assumed. A Pakistani passport may only be held/used by a person who is a Pakistani citizen; using another country's passport to enter Pakistan has its own rules. INSAaf does not fabricate the current list of countries. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Whether a marriage validly contracted abroad is recognised in Pakistan (and vice versa) depends on BOTH jurisdictions: the law of the country where the marriage took place (which made it valid there) and Pakistani law on recognition, registration and (for Muslims) the requirements under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961 and registration/NADRA recording. A foreign marriage certificate usually needs to be properly attested/legalised to be used in Pakistan, and registration of the marriage with Pakistani authorities may be required for full recognition for purposes like immigration, inheritance or spousal rights. Recognition is not automatic for every foreign marriage — it turns on the specific facts and applicable Pakistani rules. This is a cross-border matter requiring both the foreign documentation side and the Pakistan recognition side; verify current requirements with NADRA / the relevant mission. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: A divorce obtained abroad is not automatically effective in Pakistan; its recognition depends on Pakistani law and, for Muslims, procedural requirements (such as notice/registration relevant under the Muslim Family Laws framework) and the circumstances of the foreign decree. Conversely, a Pakistani divorce may need recognition abroad under that country's rules. Cross-border divorce frequently raises parallel questions of maintenance, dower, iddat and child custody, each of which may have a Pakistan-side and a foreign-side aspect. Because recognition of foreign decrees is legally technical and can affect remarriage and inheritance, the safe route is to confirm recognition through the proper Pakistani authority/mission and, where needed, obtain advice from a qualified lawyer. INSAaf gives the routing and cautions, not a definitive recognition opinion on facts it lacks. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Child custody / guardianship spanning Pakistan and another country is a genuinely cross-border, jurisdiction-sensitive issue: which court has authority, which country's welfare standard applies, and whether a custody order from one country will be enforced in the other, are all determined by the relevant laws and any applicable international arrangements (for example, abduction/custody conventions as they apply between the specific states — not all countries are parties). International child removal/retention can carry serious legal consequences under the foreign country's law. Such matters should be handled by qualified lawyers in the relevant country or countries, with consular notification where a Pakistani minor is involved (directory via https://www.mofa.gov.pk). INSAaf explains the jurisdiction split and routes to authority; it does not opine on a specific custody outcome. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Owning, buying, selling or transferring property in a FOREIGN country is governed by that country's property, tax and (often) foreign-ownership rules — not Pakistani law. A Pakistani resident dealing with foreign property may need documents (powers of attorney, contracts) executed and attested abroad, and must comply with the foreign country's registration and tax requirements. Repatriating sale proceeds and any Pakistani-side reporting/tax treatment is a separate question governed by Pakistan's rules (State Bank / FBR — https://www.sbp.org.pk, https://fbr.gov.pk) and any applicable double-taxation arrangement. Both jurisdictions can apply to a single transaction. INSAaf does not state a specific country's foreign-ownership rules; it identifies the two layers and points to each side's official authority. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Inheritance where the deceased or heirs are Pakistani but there are assets, or a death, abroad is a cross-border matter engaging (A) the foreign country's succession/probate rules for assets located there and (B) Pakistani succession law (including Muslim personal law of inheritance, and the applicable family/personal law for non-Muslims) for assets in Pakistan, plus recognition of foreign grant-of-probate/letters of administration. Which law applies to which asset often depends on where the asset is situated (immovable property typically follows the law of the country where it is located) and the applicable personal law. Because foreign grants must sometimes be recognised in Pakistan (and vice versa) under the relevant rules, professional assistance and coordination with the Pakistani mission/authorities is usually needed. INSAaf maps the jurisdiction split; it does not compute shares without the verified facts and applicable law. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: A document received FROM a FOREIGN court or authority — such as a U.S. court notice/summons, a foreign claim, an immigration/visa decision letter, a foreign police notice, or a deportation/removal notice — is governed by the ISSUING foreign country's law and procedure, NOT by Pakistani law. The correct response is determined by: (1) what the document actually commands (appear, respond, pay, leave), (2) the deadline it states, (3) the foreign authority/court named, and (4) that country's own procedure — usually requiring a qualified LOCAL lawyer in that country. Pakistani authorities do not adjudicate foreign court proceedings; a Pakistani mission may give consular support (contact list, welfare) via https://www.mofa.gov.pk but cannot act on the foreign case. Ignoring a foreign court deadline can carry real consequences under the foreign legal system. Treat the foreign document on its own terms and never apply Pakistani court procedure to it. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: Enforcing a judgment obtained in one country in another (for example enforcing a foreign money decree in Pakistan, or a Pakistani decree abroad) is not automatic. Pakistan's Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 deals with recognition/enforcement of foreign judgments, distinguishing "reciprocating" territories from others, and enforcement generally requires a court process in the country where enforcement is sought, subject to that country's limits (e.g., public policy, jurisdiction of the original court). The foreign side applies its own enforcement rules. Because this is technical and jurisdiction-pair-specific, professional representation in the enforcing country is normally required. INSAaf identifies the correct framework and the need for local counsel; it does not promise enforcement. Status: CURRENT. Verified: 2026-09-04.

chunks.chunkTitle: A cross-border legal problem should be triaged by jurisdiction before any advice: identify (1) where the person is, (2) where the counterparty/asset/event is, (3) which country's law governs the issue, then use the RIGHT forum for each layer — the foreign country's courts/authorities for foreign-law matters, Pakistani authorities (courts, NADRA, MOFA, BE&OE/FBR) for Pakistan-law matters, and consular channels for citizen welfare. chunks.key: Creation of Pakistan and the retained 1935 Constitution
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Constitutional position at independence
chunks.text:
Title: Constitutional position at independence
After Independence, the first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan, elected in December 1945 in united India, was assigned the task of framing the Constitution of Pakistan.
From 14th August 1947 to 1st March 1956, the Government of India Act, 1935, was retained as the Constitution of Pakistan.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Active

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: First Constituent Assembly and the Objectives Resolution
chunks.text:
Title: First Constituent Assembly and the Objectives Resolution
The first Constituent Assembly of Pakistan passed the Objectives Resolution on 12th March, 1949, laying down principles which later became a substantive part of the Constitution of Pakistan and which still serve as its preamble.
The Assembly was dissolved in October, 1954 before it could accomplish the task of framing the constitution.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Active

chunks.title: Constitutional History of Pakistan - Official Senate Record (1947-2002)
chunks.key: Second Constituent Assembly and the 1956 Constitution
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: The first Constitution of Pakistan, 1956
chunks.text:
Title: The first Constitution of Pakistan, 1956
The Governor General convened the Second Constituent Assembly in May, 1955.
The Second Constituent Assembly framed and passed the first Constitution of Pakistan on 29th February, 1956. That Constitution was promulgated on 23rd March, 1956 and provided for a parliamentary form of Government with a unicameral legislature.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Historical — superseded (abrogated 7 October 1958)

chunks.title: Constitutional History of Pakistan - Official Senate Record (1947-2002)
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Abrogation of 1956 Constitution and the 1962 Constitution
chunks.text:
Title: Abrogation of 1956 Constitution and the 1962 Constitution
On 7th October, 1958, Martial Law was promulgated and the 1956 Constitution was abrogated.
The Military Government appointed a Constitution Commission in February, 1960 which framed the 1962 Constitution. That Constitution provided for a Presidential form of Government with a unicameral legislature.
The 1962 Constitution was abrogated on 25th March, 1969.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Historical — superseded (abrogated 25 March 1969)

chunks.title: Constitutional History of Pakistan - Official Senate Record (1947-2002)
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
chunks.text:
Title: The Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973
The Civil Government, which came to power in December 1971 pursuant to the 1970 elections, gave the nation an interim Constitution in the year 1972.
The 1970 Assembly framed the 1973 Constitution which was passed on 12th April, 1973 and promulgated on 14th August, 1973.
The 1973 Constitution provides for a parliamentary form of Government with a bicameral legislature, comprising the National Assembly and the Senate.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Active — current Constitution of Pakistan

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Growth of the Senate under the 1973 Constitution
chunks.text:

The membership of the Senate, which was originally 45, was raised to 63 in 1977 and to 87 in 1985. The membership of the Senate was again raised from 87 to 100 in 2002.
Source: Senate of Pakistan — History (official parliamentary record)
Source URL: https://senate.gov.pk/en/essence.php?id=1098
Status: Active

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: NADRA identity documents — CNIC and NICOP
chunks.text:
Title: NADRA identity documents — CNIC and NICOP
The National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) issues identity documents under the NADRA Ordinance, 2000. The National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOP) is issued under Section 12 of that Ordinance to Pakistani citizens residing abroad; it is the official proof of identity and nationality for Pakistanis living overseas and allows visa-free entry into Pakistan.
Issued forms of NICOP: (a) NICOP (standard card — NADRA states new standard Teslin-based NICOPs are not currently being issued); (b) Smart NICOP (secure microchip, enhanced security); (c) NICOP with QR-code (machine-readable QR for faster verification); (d) polycarbonate NICOP.
Eligibility: NICOP is issued to Pakistani citizens residing abroad who (a) live or work outside Pakistan; (b) hold dual nationality of a country recognized by the Government of Pakistan; (c) intend to stay abroad for an extended period and need proof of identity and nationality; or (d) are children of Pakistani citizens born abroad who are eligible to be registered as Pakistani citizens.
Document requirements (categories stated by NADRA): identity card number of parent(s) or blood relative(s), or biometric witness by an ID holder with Undertaking "B" where the applicant has no blood relative (system-independent cases); computerized birth certificate (verified) of the Union Council/Municipal Committee/Cantonment, or citizenship/naturalization certificate (intending non-residents); foreign detailed birth certificate, manual birth certificate, or S1 form issued by a Pakistan Embassy/Mission, or citizenship/naturalization certificate (non-residents); Pakistani/foreign passport, residence permit or travel document, or Undertaking "A" attested by a Pakistan Embassy/Mission (non-residents); biometric verification by a parent or blood relative, or attestation of the CNICF as per Regulation 9(a-h) (inland Data Acquisition Units), or verification of the application form by any ID holder (applicants applying from abroad).
Applying: through the PakID application (NADRA's official mobile app: create account, select "New NICOP", fill details, upload documents, visit a NADRA Registration Centre if required, track status) or in person at a NADRA Registration Centre. Biometric verification and photograph may require a visit to a Registration Centre.
Source: National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) — official portal
Source URL: https://www.nadra.gov.pk/identityDocument/nicop?action=new
Status: Active (verified 2026-09-06; fees and timelines on the NADRA fee-structure page)

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Passport application process (Directorate General of Immigration and Passports)
chunks.text:
Title: Passport application process (Directorate General of Immigration and Passports)
The Directorate General of Immigration and Passports (DGIP), Ministry of Interior, is the official passport authority. Two application paths exist: (1) online passport renewal for inland and overseas Pakistanis, including minor modifications and new passports for newborns for overseas Pakistanis; (2) applying in person at a Regional Passport Office in Pakistan or a Pakistan Mission abroad for new, renewal and modification cases.
In-person process steps at a Regional Passport Office: (1) arrival at the customer service counter; (2) photograph capture and QR-code token issuance — original CNIC/Smart Card/NICOP or Children Registration Certificate (CRC)/B-Form (under 18) with copies; (3) biometric (fingerprint) capture — right thumb, right index, left thumb, left index; (4) data entry — the applicant must verify and sign the printed data form; any change must be pointed out at this stage because after the Assistant Director allows "go ahead" no change is possible; a valid mobile number/email is collected for status via SMS 9988 / Email Rabta service; (5) verification against the Exit Control List (ECL) and Black List (BL) — persons on the ECL or BL have their process stopped until removal as per rules/SOP; (6) interview and decision by the Assistant Director/Office In-charge, who may ask for additional documents or refer the case to a security agency; cases of applicants below 18 are deferred for attestation of the data form by a Government Gazetted officer (who writes CNIC/contact and affixes a by-name official stamp); (7) fee payment via QR code through digital payment platforms (e.g., EasyPaisa, JazzCash, online banking); (8) passport delivery — collection at the delivery counter on the given date by the applicant himself/herself or a blood relative, with the original token.
Regional Passport Offices with a One Window facilitation desk process steps 2-5 at one desk.
Source: Directorate General of Immigration and Passports (DGIP), Ministry of Interior — official website
Source URL: https://dgip.gov.pk/passport/process.php
Status: Active (page last modified 22 July 2026)

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Voter enrolment and electoral-roll correction (Election Commission of Pakistan)
chunks.text:
Title: Voter enrolment and electoral-roll correction (Election Commission of Pakistan)
A person is entitled to be enrolled as a voter in an electoral area if he/she: (a) is a citizen of Pakistan; (b) is not less than eighteen years of age; (c) possesses a National Identity Card issued by NADRA at any time till the last day fixed for claims, objections and applications for preparation, revision or correction of electoral rolls; (d) is not declared by a competent court to be of unsound mind; and (e) is, or is deemed under section 27 of the Elections Act 2017 to be, resident in the electoral area. An expired National Identity Card is deemed valid for voter registration and for casting a vote.
To register or transfer a vote, submit the prescribed form with a copy of the CNIC to the District Election Commissioner (DEC), Registration Officer or Assistant Registration Officer of the district where enrolment is sought. Forms are free and available online or from those offices. Voter forms: Form 21 (registration/transfer of vote), Form 22 (objection/deletion of vote), Form 23 (correction of particulars). Enrolment status can be checked by sending the CNIC number by SMS to 8300.
Source: Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) — official website
Source URL: https://ecp.gov.pk/how-to-register
Status: Active (verified 2026-09-06)

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Complaints to the Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib)
chunks.text:
Title: Complaints to the Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib)
The Office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Federal Ombudsman) redresses citizens' complaints against federal government agencies. A complaint written in English or Urdu may be lodged with the Wafaqi Mohtasib Secretariat or any regional office on WMS Form 'A' (downloadable from the official website), or online. If the complaint is not on Form 'A' it must be accompanied by a solemn affirmation that: (1) the allegations are correct and true to the best of the complainant's knowledge and belief; (2) no prior complaint on the subject was filed with the Secretariat or regional offices; (3) no suit, appeal, petition or other judicial proceedings in connection with the subject matter are pending before any court, tribunal or board (and none will be entertained); and (4) a representation to the competent authority of the agency was made but no reply was given within a reasonable time or the representation was unjustly turned down.
Normally the complainant should first approach the higher authorities of the concerned agency to give them an opportunity to redress the grievance. Copies of relevant documents, including the CNIC and latest correspondence with the agency, should be annexed where possible. A receipt is issued immediately when the complaint is presented in person; when submitted by other means, a receipt is issued within 72 hours.
Secretariat: 36 Constitution Avenue, G-5/2, Islamabad. Phones: +92-51-9216762, +92-51-9216763, +92-51-9216764. Child-complaints helpline: 1056.
Source: Office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) — official website

chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Interior / Pakistan Online Visa System (NADRA)
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Visa validity and period of stay
chunks.text:
Title: Visa validity and period of stay
Visa validity is the period during which the visa can be used: all visas are valid for entry into Pakistan for six months from the date of issue, and a visa not utilized within that period becomes invalid. A foreigner may enter Pakistan at any time within the validity of the granted visa. The period of stay is counted from the date of the foreigner's arrival, not from the date of issue of the visa. Stay is governed by the residential permit issued by the foreigner registration office at the time of registration, not by the date of issue of the visa. A stay may be extended by applying for an extension of the relevant visa category.
Source: Pakistan Online Visa System — Important Terms (official)
Source URL: https://visa.nadra.gov.pk/important-terms/

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Police registration of foreigners — exemption rules
chunks.text:
Title: Police registration of foreigners — exemption rules
All foreigners are exempted from registration with the police EXCEPT (a) nationals of: Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Israel, Nigeria, Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) and Somalia; and (b) such other foreign nationals who are directed by the immigration authorities to report to the Foreigner Registration Office (FRO) for registration, in which case a stamp to this effect is affixed on their passports. However, nationals in the managerial category who are issued a Work Permit/Visa from these listed countries are exempted from police registration, except Indians and foreigners of Indian origin.
Source: Pakistan Online Visa System — Important Terms (official)
Source URL: https://visa.nadra.gov.pk/important-terms/

chunks.text:
Title: Pakistan Origin Card (POC) and identity for foreigners
POC means Pakistan Origin Card: the national identity document issued to foreigners with Pakistan origin. It is distinct from the CNIC (Pakistan's Computerized National Identity Card for citizens) and from the NICOP (National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis, issued under Section 12 of the NADRA Ordinance 2000 to Pakistani citizens residing abroad, which allows visa-free entry into Pakistan, as stated on NADRA's official NICOP page). Dual nationality, in the official visa glossary, is a person's citizenship status when he/she is concurrently regarded as a citizen of more than one state.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Official glossary of the Pakistan Online Visa System
chunks.text:
Title: Official glossary of the Pakistan Online Visa System
Official terms used by the visa system: Applicant — the person (or persons) applying for a Pakistan Online Visa. Business Visa List — the list of business-friendly countries identified by the Government of Pakistan. CNIC — Pakistan's Computerized National Identity Card. Complete application — an application providing all information necessary for visa application processing, including all necessary supporting documents. Dependent children — a child or stepchild who has not turned 18 years of age, or, if aged 18 years or over, is a dependent; a dependent child must not have a partner or be engaged to be married. Dual nationality — a person's citizenship status when concurrently regarded as a citizen of more than one state. Deeni Madarris — educational institution for Islamic studies. DCO — District Coordination Officer. DGIP — Directorate General of Immigration and Passport. Extension — extending stay by applying for extension of the relevant visa category. FIA — Federal Investigation Agency. Housemaid — domestic servant. Immediate family — the applicant's partner and dependent children. INGO — registered international non-governmental organization in Pakistan. Journalist — journalists, correspondents or reporters representing overseas news organizations. List of Prohibited Areas — list of prohibited areas identified by the Government of Pakistan. Missionary — person sent on a religious mission in Pakistan. Negative List — the list of names of foreigners or entities developed by the Government of Pakistan to be avoided or distrusted. NGO — registered non-profit organization operating independently of government. NOC — No Objection Certificate, a legal certificate issued by any agency, organization, institute or, in certain cases, an individual. Police Registration — see the exemption rules in the police-registration record above. Tourist Friendly Countries — list of countries defined by the Government of Pakistan. Transit Visa — a visa allowing its holder to pass through a country only, not to stay there. Tabligh — a religious gathering or congregation. Visa — permission to travel to, enter and/or remain in Pakistan for a period of time. Visa on Arrival — visa provided on arrival through immigration counters in Pakistan or at Pakistani borders. Visa Validity — period during which the visa can be used (six months from date of issue for entry).
Source: Pakistan Online Visa System — Important Terms (official)
Source URL: https://visa.nadra.gov.pk/important-terms/
Status: Active (verified 2026-09-06)

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan - Entry, Stay, Police Registration and Residential Permit (Official Visa System Terms)
chunks.issuingAuthority: Ministry of Interior / Pakistan Online Visa System (NADRA)
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Entry controls that apply to foreigners
chunks.text:
Title: Entry controls that apply to foreigners
FIA (Federal Investigation Agency) is the agency of the Government of Pakistan responsible for immigration control at ports of entry; DGIP (Directorate General of Immigration and Passport) is the passport authority; NOC (No Objection Certificate) approvals are required from the competent agency for entry into or activity in notified areas. The Negative List contains names of foreigners or entities to be avoided or distrusted, and the List of Prohibited Areas restricts travel into notified areas. The foreigner registration office (FRO) issues the residential permit that governs the period of stay, and immigration authorities may direct a foreigner to report to the FRO for registration (stamped on the passport). The legal consequence of overstaying a residential permit is governed by the Foreigners Act 1946, which applies to the entry, presence and departure of foreigners in Pakistan (see also case law on bail after arrest under the Foreigners Act 1946 in the case-law records).
Source: Pakistan Online Visa System — Important Terms (official)
Source URL: https://visa.nadra.gov.pk/important-terms/
Status: Active (verified 2026-09-06; overstay consequences are statute-based, see Foreigners Act 1946)

chunks.text:
Public offices of Pakistan — structured records (role / authority / powers / citizen interface / source)
This document is a structured index of public offices a citizen or practitioner may need to approach, from the highest constitutional offices to revenue and police offices at district level. EVERY record states exactly what the indexed corpus and the official government pages verified on 2026-09-06 support. Each record carries a status: FULL (role and powers described by indexed primary text or verified official pages), PARTIAL (only some functions of the office are indexed so far), or GAP (no indexed source yet — the office is named with its covering law so the gap is explicit). No record attributes powers to an office that the cited sources do not state.
Source: Indexed corpus records and official government pages cited per record (all verified 2026-09-06)
Source URL: see each record
Status: Structured index with explicit FULL/PARTIAL/GAP status per office

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: President of Pakistan (Head of State). Role: constitutional head of state. Powers indexed so far: (1) pardon, reprieve and respite powers recorded in the Constitution corpus under Article 45 (constitution.txt); (2) power to make a reference to the Supreme Court on a question of law of public importance — the advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court under Article 186 is recorded in court_hierarchy.txt (Section: 2, Supreme Court). Not yet indexed: election, qualifications and term of office (Articles 41-44), oath (Article 42), and the President's other constitutional functions — the Constitution corpus currently indexes Articles 1, 2, 2A, 4, 5, 8-28, 45, 51, 175, 184, 199 and 251 only. Status: PARTIAL. Provenance: rag/documents/constitution/constitution.txt; rag/documents/court-hierarchy/court_hierarchy.txt.

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: Chief Justice of Pakistan. Role: head of the Supreme Court, the apex court under Article 175. Powers and functions recorded: (a) constitution of benches and the Court's original (Article 184), appellate (185), advisory (186) and review (188) jurisdictions; (b) the established channel by which a citizen's letter complaining of fundamental-rights violations may reach the Court and be converted into suo motu proceedings under Article 184(3) — letters can be addressed directly to the Chief Justice at the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Constitution Avenue, Islamabad, without fee or lawyer. Status: FULL. chunks.chunkTitle: Office: District and Sessions Judge. Role: highest judicial authority in the district; head of the district judiciary. Powers recorded: (a) trial of sessions cases (murder, rape, dacoity, etc.) and original civil jurisdiction above civil-judge pecuniary limits; (b) appellate jurisdiction from civil judges and magistrates; (c) administrative control over the district subordinate judiciary; (d) as ex-officio Justice of Peace, entertaining applications under Section 22A(6) CrPC when police refuse to register an FIR — after a written complaint to the SP/SSP/DPO fails (within 7 days), the citizen applies to the District and Sessions Judge, who calls for the police report and may direct the SHO to register the FIR; (e) weekly prison courts — District and Sessions Judges hold weekly courts visiting prisons, and prisoners may petition the District and Sessions Judge. Status: FULL. Provenance: rag/documents/court-hierarchy/court_hierarchy.txt (Section: 5); rag/documents/court-procedure/procedures.txt (FIR-refusal remedy under Sections 22A/22B); rag/documents/prisons/prisons.txt (Section: 7 grievance mechanism).

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: Civil Judge / Judicial Magistrate (First Class). Role: lowest tier of the regular judiciary. Powers recorded: civil judges try civil suits up to prescribed pecuniary limits; judicial magistrates of the first class try criminal cases punishable with up to about three years' imprisonment (provincial variation); under-trial prisoners must be produced before a magistrate within 24 hours; a private complaint may be filed directly before the Judicial Magistrate under Section 200 CrPC as an alternative when the FIR route fails. Status: FULL. Provenance: rag/documents/court-hierarchy/court_hierarchy.txt (Section: 6); rag/documents/crpc/crpc.txt (Section 200 remedy recorded in procedures digest); rag/documents/prisons/prisons.txt (Section: 6 under-trial prisoners).

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: Election Commission of Pakistan (Chief Election Commissioner and four Members, one from each province). Role: constitutional body under Article 218 of the Constitution. Powers recorded: conducts elections for the National Assembly, Provincial Assemblies, Senate and local government; delimits constituencies after each census; maintains and annually updates voter rolls (every citizen aged 18+ with a NADRA CNIC is entitled to enrolment); prescribes candidate spending limits and receives parties' annual accounts; hears election offences through the law. Citizen interface (verified official page): enrolment/transfer via Form 21, objections via Form 22, corrections via Form 23, filed with the District Election Commissioner, Registration Officer or Assistant Registration Officer; SMS 8300 checks enrolment status. Status: FULL. chunks.chunkTitle: Office: Tehsildar / Naib-Tehsildar (revenue officer). Role: revenue administration at tehsil level. Powers recorded: in the mutation (Inteqal) process — after the buyer applies to the local Patwari following registration of the sale deed, the Revenue Officer (Tehsildar/Naib-Tehsildar) issues notice to the parties; if no objection is filed within the notice period and the transfer is verified, mutation is sanctioned and the new owner's name is recorded in the Fard-e-Malkiat. Status: PARTIAL (only the revenue/mutation function is indexed). Provenance: rag/documents/property/property.txt (SECTION: MUTATION_INTEQAL); sources recorded there: Board of Revenue Punjab/Sindh/KP/Balochistan; Land Revenue Act 1967.

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: Public Prosecutor. Role: prosecuting officer of the State before the Sessions Court and, on direction, the High Court. Powers recorded (CrPC digest): (a) in every trial before a Court of Session initiated upon a police report, the prosecution is conducted by the Public Prosecutor (Section 265A); (b) appeals against acquittal — the Provincial Government may direct the Public Prosecutor to present an appeal to the High Court from an order of acquittal passed by a court other than the High Court, and the Federal Government may do likewise where the offence was investigated by the Federal Investigation Agency (Section 417(1)-(2)); note the corpus also records that an aggrieved person may himself file such an appeal within thirty days (Section 417(2A)). Status: FULL (as recorded in the CrPC digest). Provenance: rag/documents/crpc/crpc.txt (Sections: 265A, 417).

chunks.chunkTitle: Office: District Legal Advisory Committee (DLAC) and District Legal Empowerment Committee (DLEC); Legal Aid and Justice Authority. Role: public legal-aid bodies. Powers recorded: (a) DLACs, established under the Pakistan Bar Council Legal Aid Rules, exist in every district; a person who cannot afford representation applies through the local District Bar Association or District Court, and the DLAC assigns a lawyer for civil or criminal cases; (b) for criminal cases (especially of women and children) the citizen approaches the Legal Aid and Justice Authority, and for civil/general cases the DLEC — through the Deputy Commissioner or the District Judge — by submitting a formal application proving indigency (Zakat certificate or income affidavit); the committee reviews and, if approved, appoints a lawyer from its panel whose fee is paid by the State/committee. Status: FULL. Provenance: rag/documents/legal-aid/aid.txt (SECTION: DLAC); rag/documents/procedure/workflows.txt (legal-aid workflow); Source: Pakistan Bar Council; Legal Practitioners and Bar Councils Act 1973 (as recorded in aid.txt).

chunks.chunkTitle: OFFICE: Prime Minister and the Federal Cabinet. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 90-99.
chunks.text:
OFFICE: Prime Minister and the Federal Cabinet. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 90-99.
JURISDICTION: executive authority of the Federation vests in the Federal Government and is
exercised by the Prime Minister, directly or through federal ministers and officials.
POWERS (summary): the Prime Minister is elected by the majority of the National Assembly
(Article 91); the President appoints federal ministers on the Prime Minister's advice
(Article 92); the Cabinet aids and advises the Prime Minister and is collectively responsible
to the National Assembly (Article 91); the Prime Minister presides over Cabinet, allocates
portfolios, and directs the federal secretariat through secretaries.
LIMITATIONS: the Cabinet answers to Parliament (confidence of the NA majority); ministers
must be members of Parliament (with statutory exceptions); federal legislative and financial
powers remain with Parliament.
SUPERVISION: National Assembly (confidence), Senate (oversight committees), courts (writ
jurisdiction over executive acts).
CITIZEN INTERACTION: policy and departmental heads; grievances to the departments or the
Citizen's Portal; the Prime Minister is not a direct complaint forum.
SOURCE: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 90-99. VERIFICATION: verified (well-established
articles; see the constitution corpus and AMEND_CONST_* records for amendment history).

chunks.chunkTitle: OFFICE: Governor of a Province. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 101-105, 129.
chunks.text:
OFFICE: Governor of a Province. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 101-105, 129.
JURISDICTION: the province; the Governor is appointed by the President (Article 101) and is
the constitutional head of the province.
POWERS (summary): the executive authority of the Province vests in the Governor and is
exercised by him directly or through officers subordinate to him (Article 129); assent to
provincial legislation; appointments in the provincial government on advice where required;
functions under Articles 101-105 including discretionary powers conferred by the Constitution.
LIMITATIONS: most functions are exercised on the advice of the Chief Minister and Cabinet
(Article 129 read with Article 130-131); the Governor cannot act against the provincial
Cabinet's advice where the Constitution requires advice.
SUPERVISION: Provincial Assembly (confidence in the CM/Cabinet); courts (writ jurisdiction).
CITIZEN INTERACTION: through the provincial secretariat; grievances to departments, then the
provincial ombudsman or the courts.
SOURCE: Constitution of Pakistan, Articles 101-105, 129. VERIFICATION: verified.

OFFICE: Chief Minister and Provincial Cabinet. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution, Articles 130-140.
POWERS (summary): the Chief Minister is elected by the majority of the Provincial Assembly
(Article 130); the Governor appoints provincial ministers on the Chief Minister's advice
(Article 132); the Cabinet is collectively responsible to the Provincial Assembly (Article 136);
the Chief Minister presides, allocates portfolios and directs the provincial secretariat.
LIMITATIONS: confidence of the Provincial Assembly; provincial legislative power rests with
the Provincial Assembly.
SUPERVISION: Provincial Assembly; courts.
CITIZEN INTERACTION: provincial departments; complaints to departments, the provincial
ombudsman, or the High Court (Article 199).
SOURCE: Constitution, Articles 130-140. VERIFICATION: verified.

chunks.chunkTitle: OFFICE: Attorney-General for Pakistan. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution, Article 100.
chunks.text:
OFFICE: Attorney-General for Pakistan. LEGAL BASIS: Constitution, Article 100.
POWERS (summary): appointed by the President; must be qualified to be a judge of the Supreme
Court; advises the Federal Government on legal matters, performs such other duties of a legal
character referred to him by the Federal Government, and has the right of audience in all
courts and tribunals in Pakistan.
LIMITATIONS: advice, not decision; does not prosecute (prosecution is the public prosecutor's
function); serves during the President's pleasure.
SUPERVISION: the Federal Government.
CITIZEN INTERACTION: none direct (citizens deal with courts and departments).
SOURCE: Constitution, Article 100. VERIFICATION: verified.

chunks.text:
OFFICES: Sector regulators. LEGAL BASIS: respective enabling statutes.
- SECP (Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan; SECP Act, 1997): regulates companies,
  capital markets, insurance and related corporate services; receives investor complaints.
- State Bank of Pakistan (State Bank of Pakistan Act, 1956): central bank — monetary policy,
  banking regulation and supervision; Banking Mohtasib/banking complaints for consumer
  grievances against banks.
- FBR (Federal Board of Revenue; FBR Act, 2007): federal tax administration (income tax,
  sales tax, customs, FED); Commissioner Appeals/ATIR for tax disputes.
- Telecom (PTA; Pakistan Telecommunication (Re-organization) Act, 1996): telecom licensing,
  consumer protection (complaints against operators).
- Energy: NEPRA (NEPRA Act, 1997) electricity regulation; OGRA (OGRA Ordinance, 2002) oil and
  gas regulation — tariff and consumer complaints.
LIMITATIONS: each regulator's powers are bounded by its statute; tariff/direction powers
subject to judicial review.
SUPERVISION: the Federal Government (policy), Parliament, courts.
CITIZEN INTERACTION: consumer complaint portals of each regulator (verified as to existence;
current portal details per regulator's website).
SOURCE: the enabling statutes listed. VERIFICATION: verified as to the statutory framework.

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: Passport — in-person application at a Regional Passport Office
chunks.text:
Workflow: Passport — in-person application at a Regional Passport Office
Authority: Directorate General of Immigration and Passports (DGIP), Ministry of Interior.
Situation: New passport, renewal or modification applied in person.
Steps: (1) arrival at the customer service counter of the Regional Passport Office; (2) photograph capture and QR-code token — bring original CNIC/Smart Card/NICOP or CRC/B-Form (under 18) with copies; (3) biometric capture — right thumb, right index, left thumb, left index; (4) data entry — verify and sign the printed data form; changes must be raised at this stage because after the Assistant Director allows "go ahead" no change is possible; give a valid mobile number/email for status via SMS 9988 / Email Rabta; (5) verification against the Exit Control List (ECL) and Black List (BL) — persons on the ECL/BL have their process stopped until removal as per rules/SOP; (6) interview and decision by the Assistant Director/Office In-charge, who may ask for more documents or refer the case to a security agency; applicants below 18 are deferred for attestation of the data form by a Government Gazetted officer (who writes CNIC/contact and affixes a by-name official stamp); (7) fee payment via QR code through digital payment platforms (e.g., EasyPaisa, JazzCash, online banking); (8) delivery at the delivery counter on the given date to the applicant personally or a blood relative, with the original token.
Facilitation: Regional Passport Offices with a One Window desk process steps 2-5 at one desk.
Source: Directorate General of Immigration and Passports (DGIP) — official website
Source URL: https://dgip.gov.pk/passport/process.php
Status: Active (page last modified 22 July 2026; verified 2026-09-06)

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: NICOP — application by an overseas Pakistani
chunks.text:
Workflow: NICOP — application by an overseas Pakistani
Authority: NADRA (National Database and Registration Authority), under Section 12 of the NADRA Ordinance 2000.
Situation: A Pakistani citizen residing abroad needs the National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis (NICOP) — proof of identity and nationality allowing visa-free entry into Pakistan.
Routes: (a) PakID application — NADRA's official mobile app: create account, select "New NICOP", fill details, upload documents, visit a NADRA Registration Centre if required, track status; (b) in person at a NADRA Registration Centre (biometric verification and photograph may require a visit).
Document categories (as NADRA states for NICOP): identity card number of parent(s)/blood relative(s), or biometric witness by an ID holder with Undertaking "B" where there is no blood relative; computerized birth certificate (verified) of the Union Council/Municipal Committee/Cantonment, or citizenship/naturalization certificate; foreign detailed/manual birth certificate or S1 form issued by a Pakistan Embassy/Mission, or citizenship/naturalization certificate; Pakistani/foreign passport, residence permit or travel document, or Undertaking "A" attested by a Pakistan Embassy/Mission; biometric verification by a parent or blood relative, or attestation of the CNICF per Regulation 9(a-h), or verification of the application form by any ID holder (for applicants applying from abroad).
Source: National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) — official portal
Source URL: https://www.nadra.gov.pk/identityDocument/nicop?action=new
Status: Active (verified 2026-09-06; fees and timelines on NADRA's fee-structure page)

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: CNIC — applying for the first time (new Computerised National Identity Card)
chunks.text:
Workflow: CNIC — applying for the first time (new Computerised National Identity Card)
Authority: NADRA (National Database and Registration Authority). NADRA's official CNIC page states the CNIC is "an identity document issued by NADRA under Section 9 & 10 of NADRA Ordinance, 2000" and that it "serves as official proof of a citizen's identity, nationality and legal status within Pakistan".
Eligibility: Pakistani citizens in or out of Pakistan who have attained the age of 18 years and have either not been previously registered with NADRA or are a holder of a Child Registration Certificate (CRC) / Juvenile Card.
Requirements: (1) identity card number of parent(s) or blood relative(s), OR biometric witness by an ID holder along with undertaking "B" (as per format) if the applicant has no blood relative — stated by NADRA as applying "for System Independent cases only"; (2) computerised birth certificate (verified) of the Union Council / Municipal Committee / Cantonment, or Citizenship / Naturalization certificate; (3) biometric verification of a parent or blood relative, OR attestation of CNICF as per Regulation 9 (a-h).
Route through PakID (NADRA's official mobile application for identity registration and tracking): (1) download the PakID mobile app; (2) create an account or sign in; (3) select "New CNIC"; (4) fill in personal details; (5) upload required documents; (6) visit a NADRA Registration Centre (if required); (7) track the application status in the app.
Route in person: apply at a NADRA Registration Centre. The official page states that biometric verification and photograph may require a visit to a NADRA Registration Centre.
Card forms named on the official page: CNIC (standard Teslin-based card for adult citizens), Smart CNIC (card with a secure microchip), CNIC with QR-code (machine-readable QR-code for faster verification); the page also lists CNIC (Polycarbonate) and Urdu / Sindhi cards.
Fees and processing time: the official page links to NADRA's fee-structure page instead of stating figures; no fee amount or processing duration is recorded here because none was verified from the source.
Source: National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) — official CNIC page
Source URL: https://www.nadra.gov.pk/identityDocument/cnic
Status: Active (page content read from the live official page on 2026-10-12)

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: CNIC — renewal of an expired card
chunks.text:
Workflow: CNIC — renewal of an expired card
Authority: NADRA (National Database and Registration Authority).
Eligibility: as recorded on NADRA's official CNIC page, "As per Rule 12 of NADRA (NIC) Rules, 2002, a citizen shall at any time but not later than one month after the date of expiry or early termination of validity period, must apply for renewal of his / her card."
Requirements: CNIC number (the only requirement listed in the Renew panel).

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: Which NADRA identity document applies — CNIC, NICOP, CRC / Juvenile Card (B-Form), POC
chunks.text:
Workflow: Which NADRA identity document applies — CNIC, NICOP, CRC / Juvenile Card (B-Form), POC
Authority: NADRA (National Database and Registration Authority).
Distinction as recorded on NADRA's own pages: the CNIC is the identity document for a Pakistani citizen aged 18 or above, issued under Sections 9 & 10 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000, and is the document a citizen moves to from a Child Registration Certificate (CRC) / Juvenile Card — commonly called B-Form — which is the record held before first-time CNIC registration. The NICOP (National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis) is a different document for a citizen residing abroad; NADRA's NICOP page attributes it to Section 12 of the NADRA Ordinance, 2000 and to visa-free entry into Pakistan, so NICOP requirements — foreign birth certificate or S1 form from a Pakistan Mission, residence permit, Undertaking "A" — must not be applied to a domestic first-time CNIC application. NADRA's own description of its credentials lists CNIC, NICOP and POC as separate documents.
Applying the distinction: a question about a new CNIC inside Pakistan is answered from the CNIC records; a question about an overseas Pakistani's identity card is answered from the NICOP records; a question about a child's registration is answered from the CRC / Juvenile Card record.
Source: National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) — official CNIC and NICOP pages
Source URL: https://www.nadra.gov.pk/identityDocument/cnic

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: Voter enrolment, transfer and correction of particulars
chunks.text:
Workflow: Voter enrolment, transfer and correction of particulars
Authority: Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP).
Eligibility: (a) citizen of Pakistan; (b) at least eighteen years of age; (c) possesses a NADRA CNIC issued at any time till the last day fixed for claims/objections/applications for preparation, revision or correction of electoral rolls; (d) not declared by a competent court to be of unsound mind; (e) resident, or deemed resident under Section 27 of the Elections Act 2017, in the electoral area. An expired CNIC is deemed valid for registration and for casting a vote.
Steps: (1) obtain the free prescribed form — Form 21 (registration/transfer of vote), Form 22 (objection/deletion), Form 23 (correction of particulars) — online or from the ECP office; (2) attach a copy of the CNIC; (3) submit to the District Election Commissioner (DEC), Registration Officer or Assistant Registration Officer of the district where enrolment is sought; (4) check enrolment status by sending the CNIC number by SMS to 8300.
Source: Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) — official website
Source URL: https://ecp.gov.pk/how-to-register

chunks.chunkTitle: Workflow: Complaint to the Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib) against a federal agency
chunks.text:
Workflow: Complaint to the Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib) against a federal agency
Authority: Office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Federal Ombudsman).
Steps: (1) obtain WMS Form 'A' (downloadable from the official website) or complain online; (2) if the complaint is not on Form 'A', accompany it with a solemn affirmation that: the allegations are true to the best of the complainant's knowledge and belief; no prior complaint on the subject was filed with the Secretariat or regional offices; no suit/appeal/petition/judicial proceedings on the subject are pending before any court, tribunal or board (and none will be entertained); and a representation to the competent authority of the agency was made but no reply was given within a reasonable time or it was unjustly turned down; (3) annex copies of relevant documents, including the CNIC and latest correspondence with the agency, where possible; (4) present the complaint at the Mohtasib Secretariat (36 Constitution Avenue, G-5/2, Islamabad) or a regional office, or submit by post/other means; (5) obtain the receipt — immediate when presented in person, within 72 hours by other means; (6) track the inquiry; the Mohtasib can direct the agency to rectify the issue (no fee, no lawyer required).
Best practice recorded on the official page: first approach the higher authorities of the concerned agency to give them an opportunity to redress the grievance.
Contacts: phones +92-51-9216762, +92-51-9216763, +92-51-9216764; child-complaints helpline 1056.
Source: Office of the Wafaqi Mohtasib (Ombudsman) — official website
