Stereo HCJDA 38
JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT LAHORE
( JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT)
Writ Petition No.55244 of 2025 Farah Hassan, etc .
V s .
Additional District & Sessions Judge and others.
Petitioners by:- Malik Kashif Raza Awan, Advocate Respondent No.3 by : Ch. Akbar Ali Shad, Advocate Respondent No.4 by: Malik Muhammad Azeem Awan and Mr. Mazhar Ali Haider, Advocates.
Respondent No.6 by: Ch. Fiaz Gujjar, Advocate Date of hearing: - 21.05.2026
JUDGMENT
RAHEEL KAMRAN, J:- Through the instant petition filed under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 (“the Constitution”) , the petitioners have assailed judgment dated
21.02.2025 passed by the Civil Judge, Depalpur, whereby their
application under Section 12(2) of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ( “ CPC ” ) , seeking recall of judgment and decree dated 19.04.2022, was dismissed, as well as judgment dated 02.07.2025 passed by the Additional District Judge, Depalpur, whereby the civil revision preferred by them against the said dismissal was also dismissed.
2 . The facts forming background to the filing of instant petition, precisely, are that respondent No.3 Muhammad Arshad Iqbal instituted a suit for declaration and permanent injunction against the petitioners and respondents No.4 to 7, claiming ownership of agricultural land measuring 450 Kanals, 18 Marlas, situated at Mauza Khairpur, Tehsil Depalpur, District Okara (hereinafter referred to as “the suit W.P.No.55244 of 2026 property”), on the basis of gift mutations, inheritance mutation and other revenue entries. During the proceedings, some of the defendants appeared and conceded the claim of respondent No.3, whereas the remaining defendants were proceeded against ex parte . Vide judgment and decree dated 19.04.2022, the Civil Judge partly decreed the suit to the extent of 258 Kanals, 2 Marlas and 18 Sarsahi, while declining the remaining relief. The petitioners thereafter filed an application under Section 12(2) CPC, seeking recall of the said judgment and decree. After framing of issues and recording of evidence, the Civil Judge dismissed the application vide judgment dated 21.02.2025. The civil revision preferred by the petitioners against the said judgment was also dismissed by the Additional District Judge on 02.07.2025, hence the instant petition.
3 . Heard learned counsel for the parties and file has been perused.
4 . Since the petitioners ’ principal grievance is that they were either not duly served or were otherwise not validly brought before the trial Court, it would be appropriate, before examining the legal objection regarding the remedy invoked by them, to first examine the manner in which the proceedings were conducted and the defendants were proceeded against.
5 . The suit was instituted by respondent No.3 on 25.11.2019.
On 28.11.2019, summons were ordered to be issued to defendants No.2 to 8, whereas service upon the public at large/defendant No.1 was ordered through publication in the newspaper. On 20.12.2019, on receipt of publication, the public at large was proceeded against ex parte . The matter was thereafter adjourned to 06.01.2020, on which date defendant No.2, Mst. Fehmeeda Begum and defendant No.5, Mst. Razia Begum, appeared before the trial Court and their statements conceding the claim of respondent No.3/plaintiff were recorded on the order sheet. The case was then adjourned to 18.02.2020 for summoning of the remaining defendants.
W.P.No.55244 of 2026 6 . On 18.02.2020, a power of attorney on behalf of defendant No.3 Mst. Rasheeda Begum and defendant No.4, Mst. Safia Begum was submitted before the trial Court. Significantly, the order passed on that date does not record the personal appearance of either defendant No.3 or defendant No.4, nor does it record that any statement on their behalf was made or recorded. Rather, the case was adjourned to
25.02.2020 specifically for submission of written statement and for
summoning of the remaining defendants. The order dated 18.02.2020 reads as under:
- 18-02-2020 کونسل فریقین حبضر۔
مدعب علیہم 3 ، 4 کب وکبلت نبمہ داخل شد۔ ملتوی ہو کر برائے ادخبل جواة و طلبی بقیہ مدعب علیہم
بتقرر 0202 - 20 - 05 کے لئے پیش ہووے۔
However, in the documents annexed with the petition, there is available a page whereupon statements of defendants No.3 and 4 are shown to have been recorded on 18.02.2020 whereby they are shown to have conceded the claim of the plaintiff/respondent No.3.
7. The above order dated 18.02.2020 is of considerable
significance. Had defendants No.3 and 4 personally appeared and conceded the claim of respondent No.3 on 18.02.2020, there would hardly have been any occasion for the trial Court to adjourn the matter for submission of written statement on their behalf. The contemporaneous order sheet, therefore, does not support the subsequent position reflected in the record that statements of the said defendants conceding the plaintiff ’ s claim had already been recorded on that date.
8. The matter becomes more significant because separate
statements attributed to defendants No.3 and 4 do not bear the signatures of the Presiding Officer contemporaneously with the proceedings dated
18.02.2020. The signatures of the Presiding Officer appearing thereon are
dated 25.01.2022 and have been made by way of takmeel . Thus, there is a material discrepancy between the contemporaneous order sheet dated
18.02.2020 and the separate statements subsequently forming part of the
record. The former records submission of power of attorney and W.P.No.55244 of 2026 adjournment for filing of written statement, whereas the latter purport to show that the defendants had already appeared and conceded the claim.
Such discrepancy, at the very least, casts serious doubt upon the manner in which the said statements came to be incorporated into the judicial record and their evidentiary worth could not have been determined merely by noticing their existence.
9. The Civil Judge, while dealing with this aspect, appears to
have proceeded on the premise that the existence of the statements itself established the appearance of defendants No.3 and 4 before the Court.
Such approach overlooks the significance of the contemporaneous order sheet and the subsequent date appearing with the signatures of the Presiding Officer on the statements. Where two parts of the same judicial record disclose materially different positions regarding the appearance and conduct of a defendant, the Court is required to reconcile the discrepancy before placing reliance upon one version to the prejudice of the other. In the present case, no satisfactory reconciliation of the two has been brought to notice of this Court.
10. The question of service of the remaining defendants also
presents a serious procedural infirmity. On 11.09.2020, the report of the Ahlmad appearing on the margin of the order sheet recorded that Majida Begum had died, that Aqsa Bibi had been personally served, whereas no service had been effected upon the remaining defendants. Yet, on the subsequent date, i.e. 26.10.2020, the trial Court made no determination regarding service of the defendants and instead directed the plaintiff to file an amended plaint. Thereafter, on 18.05.2021, the earlier direction regarding the amended plaint was recalled and defendant No.6 and the legal heirs of defendant No.7 were ordered to be summoned through summons/notices along with registered envelope A.D. and courier for
08.06.2021.
11. On 08.06.2021, the trial Court again directed that
defendant No.6 and the legal heirs of defendant No.7 be summoned through registered envelope A.D., courier service and affixation, subject W.P.No.55244 of 2026 to deposit of process fee, besides publication in the newspaper. The margin of the same order, however, contains the report of the Ahlmad that the requisite process fee had not been deposited, although the proclamation had been received. Thus, the specific direction of the trial Court regarding issuance of summons through the prescribed modes had admittedly not been complied with.
12. Despite the above position, on 15.07.2021 the trial Court
proceeded against defendant No.6 and the legal heirs of defendant No.7 ex parte , apparently relying upon the publication in the newspaper. What is conspicuously absent from the order is any reason as to why the earlier direction for service through registered post, courier and affixation was not complied with, or how publication alone came to be regarded as sufficient service in the circumstances. The Court, having itself directed service through particular modes, could not simply dispense with compliance thereof without recording a judicial satisfaction, supported by reasons, that such modes had failed or could not reasonably be adopted and that substituted service had consequently become necessary.
13. This defect assumes importance because the requirement
of service is not an empty procedural formality. Its purpose is to secure the attendance of a defendant and to afford him an effective opportunity of defending the claim. Where a defendant is proceeded against ex parte without first ensuring compliance with the Court ’ s own directions concerning service, the resulting proceedings are rendered vulnerable, particularly where the defendant subsequently asserts that he had no knowledge of the proceedings.
14. The position is further reinforced by the judgment of the
Supreme Court in the case of “Messrs Mobiserve Palistan (Pvt. Limited. V. Messrs V- Tech and others” (2025 SCMR 1936) . In the said case, the Supreme Court examined the legality of substituted service and found that the trial Court had resorted to publication without first satisfying the mandatory requirements relating to ordinary service. It was emphasized in the said judgment that substituted service can be resorted to only when W.P.No.55244 of 2026 the Court is satisfied that ordinary service cannot be effected or that the defendant is deliberately avoiding service, and that the prescribed procedure must be followed before such mode of service is adopted. The Court further underscored the fundamental principle that a person should not be condemned unheard and that procedural technicalities should not be allowed to defeat a litigant ’ s right to a fair opportunity of hearing.
15. The facts noticed above cannot, therefore, be
characterized as isolated or inconsequential irregularities. On one hand, the contemporaneous order dated 18.02.2020 does not record the personal appearance or any concession by defendants No.3 and 4, while separate statements attributed to them appear on the record with the signatures of the Presiding Officer subsequently made by way of takmeel .
On the other hand, in respect of defendant No.6 and the legal heirs of defendant No.7, the specific directions for service through registered post, courier and affixation were not complied with, yet the defendants were subsequently proceeded against ex parte on the basis of newspaper publication without recording reasons for dispensing with the earlier modes of service. These circumstances, when considered cumulatively, materially undermine the regularity of the proceedings through which the defendants were brought within the process of the Court and ultimately deprived of an opportunity to contest the suit.
16. It is at this stage that the objection raised by learned
counsel for the respondents assumes significance. Considerable emphasis was placed upon the fact that the petitioners had invoked Section 12(2), CPC, and had not independently sought the remedy provided under Order IX Rule 13 CPC. Learned counsel relied upon the reasoning adopted by the Civil Judge, who, while dismissing the petitioners’ application under Section 12(2) CPC also observed that the petitioners had not claimed relief under Order IX Rule 13 CPC and that such remedy could not be extended to them by the Court itself. The said objection, therefore, requires examination.
W.P.No.55244 of 2026
17. There is no cavil with the proposition that Section 12(2)
and Order IX Rule 13 CPC operate in distinct fields. Section 12(2) provides a remedy where the validity of a judgment, decree or order is challenged on the ground of fraud, misrepresentation or want of jurisdiction, whereas Order IX Rule 13 provides a specific remedy to a defendant against an ex parte decree where the summons was not duly served or the defendant was prevented by sufficient cause from appearing when the suit was called for hearing. The two provisions should not ordinarily be treated as interchangeable merely because the facts of a particular case may overlap.
18. The distinction, however, does not mean that a Court
should disregard the substance of an application merely because the applicant has invoked one provision while his pleaded case also discloses circumstances attracting the other. In the present case, the petitioners ’ application under Section 12(2) CPC was not confined to a bare assertion that they had not been served. They specifically alleged that respondent No.3 had procured the ex parte proceedings through fraud and misrepresentation, including furnishing incorrect addresses, fraudulently obtaining signatures and thumb impressions, and relying upon a fictitious or unauthorized power of attorney. Non-service and the consequent ex parte proceedings were pleaded as part of a broader challenge to the manner in which the decree had allegedly been procured.
19. The judgment of the Supreme Court in Mobiserve
Pakistan (Pvt.) Limited (supra) is instructive in this regard. The Supreme Court was confronted with an application styled under Section 12(2) CPC in circumstances where the grievance substantially concerned defective service and an ex parte decree. After examining the respective scopes of Section 12(2) and Order IX Rule 13 CPC, the Supreme Court did not permit the technical description of the application to defeat the substantive grievance. Having found from the record that the prescribed procedure for service had not been followed, the Court treated the matter in accordance with the remedy warranted by the facts and ultimately accepted the application by treating it as one under Order IX Rule 13 W.P.No.55244 of 2026 CPC. The judgment thus makes it clear that where the record establishes that a party was deprived of an opportunity of hearing because of defective or legally insufficient service, the Court should not allow procedural nomenclature to stand in the way of doing substantial justice.
20. The case in hand stands on an even more significant
footing inasmuch as the petitioners did not merely allege non-service in the abstract. Their application specifically questioned the manner in which the ex parte proceedings were procured and alleged fraud and misrepresentation as the basis for invoking Section 12(2) CPC. The record examined above, moreover, independently discloses material procedural defects concerning service and the manner in which the proceedings were conducted. In such circumstances, the application could not have been rejected merely on the ground that the petitioners had not separately invoked Order IX Rule 13 CPC.
21. This Court is conscious that allegations of fraud or
misrepresentation cannot be accepted merely because they have been pleaded, and that the person invoking Section 12(2) CPC bears the burden of establishing such allegations in accordance with law. So it is not considered necessary, in the present proceedings, to record a definitive finding upon each allegation of fraudulent procurement of signatures, thumb impressions or the alleged power of attorney. The conclusion reached by this Court does not rest solely upon those allegations. Rather, the conclusion is independently supported by the deficiencies apparent from the judicial record itself, particularly the failure to ensure compliance with the Court ’ s own orders concerning service before proceeding against the concerned defendants ex parte .
22. The cumulative effect of the circumstances discussed
above is that the ex parte proceedings culminating in judgment and decree dated 19.04.2022 cannot safely be sustained. The Civil Judge, while deciding the application under Section 12(2) CPC, failed to properly appreciate the material discrepancies appearing from the original record and placed undue reliance upon the mere existence of the W.P.No.55244 of 2026 disputed statements, while also failing to adequately address the noncompliance with the orders passed for service of the remaining defendants. The Additional District Judge, while dismissing the civil revision, did not cure these material defects.
23. For the foregoing reasons, the petition in hand is allowed.
The impugned judgment dated 21.02.2025 passed by the Civil Judge, Depalpur, and judgment dated 02.07.2025 passed by the Additional District Judge, Depalpur, are set aside. Consequently, the petitioners’ application under Section 12(2) CPC is allowed and the judgment and decree dated 19.04.2022 passed by the Civil Judge are also set aside. The matter is remanded to the trial Court for decision afresh in accordance with law, after affording the petitioners an opportunity to file their written statements, framing appropriate issues and recording evidence of the parties. The trial Court shall decide the suit strictly on its own merits, uninfluenced by any observation made herein. Parties are directed to appear before the trial court on 25.09.2026.
(RAHEEL KAMRAN)

JUDGE

Court: Lahore High Court, Lahore. Case No: Misc. Writ 30572/26. Title: Misc. Writ 30572/26 (Hafiz Ghazanfar Ali Vs Province of Punjab etc). Official Ref: 2026LHC5456. Author Judge: Mr. Justice Raheel Kamran. Judgment Date (as displayed): 02-09-2026. Record Type: FULL_TEXT_VERBATIM (complete judgment text extracted from the official court PDF). Source URL: https://sys.lhc.gov.pk/appjudgments/2026LHC5456.pdf. Verified: 2026-09-06 against the official court repository.
VERBATIM JUDGMENT TEXT (extracted from the official PDF at the Source URL; 17 pages; spelling, punctuation and lineation as in the PDF):
Stereo. H C J D A 38.
JUDGMENT SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT, LAHORE.
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 Hafiz Ghazanfar Ali Versus Province of Punjab and others
JUDGMENT
DATE OF HEARING 10.07.2026
PETITIONER BY Ch. Ishtiaq A. Khan, M/s Jahangir Ahmed Bhatti and Adnan Ahmed Chaudhary, Advocates.
RESPONDENTS BY Mr. Mohammad Osman Khan, Assistant Advocate General, Punjab assisted by Mr. Ahsan Ashraf, Junior Legal Consultant at the office of the Advocate General, Punjab.
Mr. Muhammad Adil Chattha, Advocate for respondent No.7.
RAHEEL KAMRAN, J. – Through this petition under Article 199 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, (“the Constitution”), the petitioner has challenged the Notification No.SOR- III(S&GAD)1-25/2025 dated 30.10.2025 issued by the Secretary (Regulations), Services and General Administration Department, Government of the Punjab, Lahore, whereby the Tourism, Archaeology and Museums Department (Tourist Services) Rules, 2025 have been framed while exercising powers under section 23 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974. The prayer clause of the petition reads as under:
In view of above submissions it is very humbly prayed that the instant petition may very kindly be allowed and the impugned Rules made through notification dated 30-10-2025 only for the post of Controller Tourism, Archaeology and Museums Department (Tourist Services), Punjab in negation to Federal Statute, and without statue by Provincial Government may Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 2 very kindly be set aside by declaring it ultra vires to the statue and constitution and illegal/ unlawful, biased, discriminatory, void ab-initio and unconstitutional.
It is further prayed that the in the mean while the operation of the impugned rules for the post of Controller may very kindly be suspended in the interest of justice and the respondents may very kindly be refrained to proceed further upon the impugned rules till the final decision of the Honorable Court on the instant petition.
It is further prayed that any other relief which this honorable court deems fit may very kindly be awarded to meet the ends of justice.
2. The petitioner, a Deputy Controller in the Department of
Tourist Services, challenges the Tourism, Archaeology and Museums Department (Tourist Services) Rules, 2025 on the ground that after the Eighteenth Constitutional Amendment the Federal statutory regime governing the Department continues to remain in force by virtue of Articles 268 and 270AA of the Constitution until altered or repealed by the competent legislature. It is alleged that, without first enacting or adopting the requisite Provincial legislation, the Provincial Government framed the impugned Rules under section 23 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974, replacing the existing promotional channel for the post of Controller with posting of a PAS/PMS Officer. According to the petitioner, the Rules were framed to validate the transfer/posting of a particular officer whose appointment had already been suspended by this Court, thereby defeating the petitioner’s legitimate expectation of promotion and diluting the requirement of technical experience considered essential for heading the Department of Tourist Services.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the
impugned rules are ultra vires the Pakistan Hotels and Restaurants Act, 1976, the Travel Agencies Act, 1976 and the Pakistan Tourist Guides Act, 1976. According to him, in view of Articles 268 and 270AA(6) of the Constitution, the aforesaid Federal statu tes and the rules framed thereunder continue to remain in force until altered, amended or repealed by the competent legislature. He submitted that although the Provincial Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 3 Legislature was competent to enact a law governing the devolved subject and to confer rule-making power upon the Provincial Government, no such legislation has been enacted. Consequently, the Provincial Government lacked the authority to frame the impugned Rules in exercise of powers under section 23 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act,
1974. He further argued that the impugned Rules are also inconsistent
with Article 148 of the Constitution as the Province cannot, through subordinate legislation, override the rules framed by the Federation under the aforesaid enactments, the operation whereof continues to be protected under the Constitution. Learned counsel further submitted that the impugned Rules fundamentally alter the existing method of recruitment to the post of Controller by providing for appointment through posting of a PAS/PMS Officer, contrary to the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1973, as amended vide Notification dated 14.01.2004 (S.R.O.128(I)/2004). Under the said notification, the post of Controller (BS-19) was required to be filled 100% by promotion, subject to prescribed academic qualifications and twelve years ’ supervisory experience in the field of tourism, hotel management or travel agency. According to him, the impugned Rules dispense with these essential eligibility requirements and thereby undermine the specialized and technical character of the office. He further contended that the impugned Rules are arbitrary and discriminatory as they permit appointment of the head of the Department through posting of a PAS/PMS Officer, without insisting upon the specialized experience considered indispensable for the efficient administration of the Department of Tourist Services. In support of his contentions, reliance has been placed on “ Contempt Proceedings against Chief Secretary, Sindh and others” (2013 SCM R 1752) and “ General Post Office, Islamabad and others v. Muhammad Jalal” (PLD 2024 SC 1276) .
4. Notice under Order XXVIIA of the Code of Civil
Procedure, 1908, was issued to the Advocate General, Punjab, in response to which parawise comments have been submitted.
Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 4 5 . Learned Assistant Advocate General, Punjab, assisted by the learned counsel for respondent No.7, raised a preliminary objection to the maintainability of the instant petition. He submitted that the controversy essentially pertains to the terms and conditions of service of the petitioner, who admittedly is a civil servant governed by the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974 and the rules framed thereunder. Referring to paragraph No.8 of the writ petition as well as the relief claimed therein, he argued that the grievance falls within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Punjab Service Tribunal and, therefore, the constitutional jurisdiction of this Court is barred by Article 212 of the Constitution. He maintained that the exclusive jurisdiction of the Service Tribunal extends even to cases involving the vires of statutory rules or notifications or allegations regarding violation of Fundamental Rights, provided the controversy, in substance, relates to the terms and conditions of service. In support of the said objection, reliance has been placed upon the judgments in the case of “Muhammad Hassanullah (OMG/B -18), Acting Additional Secretary, Health Department, Balochistan v. Chief Secretary, Government of Balochistan, Quetta and another” (2025 SCMR 134) and “Ahmad Ullah and others v. District Education Officer (Male), Buner and others” (2024
SCMR 2004) .
On merits, learned Assistant Advocate General submitted that the impugned Notification has validly been issued in exercise of the rulemaking power conferred by section 23 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act,
1974. He further argued that the petitioner has adopted inconsistent and
mutually destructive positions by questioning the competence of the Provincial Government to frame the impugned Rules while himself having been appointed under the Punjab Youth Affairs, Sports, Archaeology and Tourism Department (Tourist Services Dying Cadre) Employees Service Rules, 2017, framed by the Provincial Government under the very same statutory provision through notification dated
27.04.2017. According to him, having accepted appointment under the
Provincial Rules, the petitioner cannot now challenge the Province’s Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 5 competence to frame similar rules regulating appointment to the post of Controller. To substantiate his contention, reliance has been placed upon “ Asrar Ahmed and others v. Chairman Pakistan Aeronactuical Complex Board, Kamra and others” (2023 SCMR 1427) . Learned Assistant Advocate General further submitted that prior to the Eighteenth Constitutional Amendment, the subject of tourism formed part of Entry No.42 of the Concurrent Legislative List. Although the post of Controller was governed by the Federal service rules framed under the Civil Servants Act, 1973 and the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1973, the devolution brought about through Article 270AA of the Constitution conferred legislative competence upon the Province to regulate the service structure relating to the devolved subject. According to him, Articles 268 and 270AA do not freeze the pre-existing Federal legal regime, rather, they merely preserve the continuity of existing laws until altered, amended or repealed by the competent Provincial authority. In support of this proposition, reliance has been placed upon “ Taisei Corporation and another v. A.M. Construction Company (Pvt.) Ltd and another” (2024 SCMR 640), “Messrs Azfar Laboratories Private Limited through Directors and others v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Ministry of National Health Services and 4 others ” (PLD 2018 Sindh 448), “ Syed Imran Ali Shah v. Government of Pakistan ” (2013 PLC 143) , “ Salim Javed Baig and others v. Federal Ombudsman and others ” (PLD 2016 Lahore 433) and “ Kamil Khan Mumtaz and others v. Province of Punjab ” (PLD 2016 Lahore 699) . Learned Assistant Advocate General lastly contended that the determination of qualifications, eligibility criteria and the mode of recruitment for a particular post falls within the policy domain of the Government and the competent Service Rules Committee. Such matters, being administrative in nature, are ordinarily not amenable to judicial review unless shown to be contrary to law. He submitted that no Government servant possesses a vested right either to promotion or to insist upon the continuance of a particular promotion channel and that Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 6 the Government is competent to amend the service rules in the interest of administrative exigency or to remove anomalies. To support his contention, reliance has been placed upon “ Government of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa through Chief Secretary, Peshawar and others v. Hayat Hussain and others ” (2016 SCMR 1021) , “ The Central Board of Revenue, Government of Pakistan v. Asad Ahmad Khan ” (PLD 1960 SC 81) .
6. In rebuttal, learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that
the objection r egarding maintainability proceeds on an erroneous characterization of the controversy as an individual service dispute. He contended that the petitioner does not dispute the general competence of the Provincial Government under the Punjab Civil Servants Ac t, 1974 to regulate the provincial services or to frame rules in that regard.
According to him, the petitioner had accepted his appointment under the 2017 Rules, which regulated the subordinate posts and preserved the then existing promotional structure; h is challenge is confined to the impugned Rules of 2025, whereby the established promotion channel from the feeder cadre to the post of Controller has been eliminated and the post has instead been made available for appointment through posting of a PAS/PMS Officer without the prescribed academic qualifications and relevant experience in the field of tourism. He maintained that the present challenge is, therefore, directed against the constitutional validity, arbitrariness and discriminatory character of the 2025 Rules themselves and not against the general rule - making competence of the Provincial Government. He further submitted that acceptance of the earlier 2017 Rules, which according to him were consistent with the statutory and constitutional framework an d did not disturb the existing promotional structure, could not amount to waiver of the right to challenge a subsequent rule which alters that structure in violation of constitutional and statutory requirements. He, therefore, contended that the authoritie s relied upon by the learned Law Officer, concerning disputes founded upon the individual terms and conditions of service of civil servants, are distinguishable from the present case.
Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 7
7. Arguments heard.
8 . It is trite law that the question of jurisdi ction goes to the root of the matter and must be decided at the very outset, for unless a Court is satisfied that it possesses the requisite jurisdiction, it cannot proceed to examine the merits of the dispute. In this regard, the Supreme Court of Pakistan in the case of “ Muslim Commercial Bank Limited v.
Muhammad Anwar Mandokhel” (2024 SCMR 298) has reiterated that every Court, before taking cognizance of and adjudicating upon any controversy, is under a legal obligation to first satisfy itself regarding t he assumption of jurisdiction and only upon recording an affirmative conclusion in that behalf can it proceed to determine the issues raised before it. So, before adverting to the merits of the controversy, it is imperative to determine the preliminary obj ection raised by the learned Assistant Advocate General regarding the maintainability of this constitutional petition. It has been contended by the learned Law Officer that the petitioner admittedly is a civil servant and the impugned Rules directly regula te the method of appointment to the promotional post of Controller, thereby affecting his terms and conditions of service.
According to him, notwithstanding the constitutional grounds urged in the petition, the controversy essentially pertains to a service matter falling within the exclusive jurisdiction of the Punjab Service Tribunal, thus attracting the constitutional bar contained in Article 212 of the Constitution. However, the l earned counsel for the petitioner has argued that the instant petition is m aintainable under Article 199 of the Constitution as it calls in question the constitutional validity of the impugned Rules.
9 . The jurisdictional question has to be determined with reference to the true nature of the controversy and the relief sought. The Federal Constitutional Court, in its recent pronouncement in the case titled “ Province of Sindh through Chief Secretary, Government of Sindh, Karachi & others v . Zulfiqar Khushk & others” ( C.P.L.A No.2799 of
2023) has observed that “A Service Tribunal do es not have the
Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 8 jurisdiction to determine the constitutionality of a Rule framed by a competent authority, if the terms and conditions of a Civil Servant are not disputed .” 10 . In the case in hand, the petitioner, while serving as Deputy Controller, was given only the additional charge of Controller for some time when the post fell vacant. He does not claim an accrued or vested right to promotion to the post of Controller, nor is any individual order denying him promotion under challenge. His substantive challenge is directed against the impugned Rules themselves, whereby the method of appointment to the post of Controller has been altered, extinguishing the promotional avenue from Deputy Controller to Controller. The relief sought is to declare the impugned Rules ultra vires the statute and the Constitution and to set them aside. Such relief, if granted, would not be confined to the petitioner but would operate upon the rule itself and, consequently, upon all persons presently serving or who may hereafter serve as Deputy Controller and otherwise be eligible for consideration for appointment to the post of Controller. The controversy, therefore, is not confined to the petitioner’s individual terms and conditions of service but essentially concerns the validity and legality of the impugned Rules.
11 . In these circumstances, the case falls within the principle enunciated by the Federal Constitutional Court that where the terms and conditions of the civil servant are not themselves in dispute, the Service Tribunal lacks jurisdiction to determine the constitutionality of the Rule.
The objection raised by the learned Law Officer is, therefore, repelled, and the petition is held to be maintainable under Article 199 of the Constitution.
12 . T he controversy may now b e examined on merits. The first question is whether the impugned Rules were made by an authority competent to frame them ? Undeniably, prior to the Constitution ( Eighteenth Amendment ) Act, 2010 the subject of tourism formed part of Entry No.42 of the Concur rent Legislative List. Although the post of Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 9 Controller was governed by the Federal service rules framed under the Civil Servants Act, 1973 and the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1973, the devolution brought about through Article 270AA of the Constitution conferred legislative competence upon the Province to regulate the service structure relating to the devolved subject. Co-extensive with such legislative power is the executive authority of the Province in terms of Article 137 of the Constitution. Articles 268 and 270AA of the Constitution do not freeze the pre-existing Federal legislative authority, rather, they merely preserve the continuance in force of existing laws until altered, amended or repealed by the provincial authority. Reliance in this regard is placed on the judgment of this Court in the case of “Salim Javed Baig and others v. Federal Ombudsman and others” (PLD 2016 Lahore 433) .
Additionally, learned counsel for the petitioner, in rebuttal to the objection regarding approbation and reprobation, has conceded the general competence of the Provincial Government to regulate the provincial service and to frame rules in that behalf. Section 23 of the said Act empowers the competent authority to make such rules as may be necessary or expedient for carrying out the purposes of the Act. The impugned notification having been issued by the Government of the Punjab in exercise of the rule-making power available under the Act, there is no substance in the challenge to its competence as such.
13 . The determination of the method of appointment to a civil post, including the choice between initial appointment, promotion, transfer or posting, is ordinarily a matter of governmental policy and administrative judgment. Guidance is drawn from the cases of “ Lt.-Col.
Farzand Ali and others v. Province of West Pakistan through the Secretary, Department of Agriculture, Government of West Pakistan, Lahore ” (PLD 1970 SC 98) , “ Syed Muhammad Arif and others v. University of Balochistan and others ” (PLD 2006 SC 564) , “ Wattan Party and another v. Federation of Pakistan and others ” (PLD 2013 SC 167) . Judicial review, however, is not excluded merely because the impugned measure is described as a Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 10 matter of policy. Where the manner in which the policy has been translated into a statutory rule is shown to be arbitrary, discriminatory, unguided or unrelated to the object sought to be achieved, the rule remains subject to constitutional scrutiny. Reliance may be placed on the cases of “Messrs Al -Raham Travels and Tours (Pvt.) Ltd. and others v.
Ministry of Religious Affairs, Hajj, Zakat and Ushr through Secretary and others” (2011 SCMR 1621) , “ Dossani Travels (Pvt.) Ltd. v. Messrs Travels Shop (Pvt.) Ltd.” ( PLD 2014 SC 1 ), “Syed Azam Shah v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Cabinet Secretariat, Islamabad and another ” (2022 SCMR 201) and “Sikandar Hayat Maken v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Establishment Division Government of Pakistan and others ” (2021 PLC (C.S.) 1450).
14 . The post of Controller is not an ordinary generaladministration post. It is the apex post in the Department of Tourist Services and carries statutory and regulatory responsibilities in relation to a specialized field involving, inter alia , tourism, hotels and restaurants, travel agencies and tourist guides. The legislative and regulatory scheme itself demonstrates that the functions performed within this field require familiarity with its technical and professional dimensions. This is also borne out by the service structure which existed before the impugned Rules. Through Notification dated 14.01.2004, issued by the Federal Government in exercise of the powers conferred by sub-rule (2) of rule 3 of the Civil Servants (Appointment, Promotion & Transfer) Rules, 1973, the post of Controller (BS-19) was prescribed to be filled 100% by promotion and the eligible officers were required to possess the prescribed academic qualifications together with twelve years’ supervisory experience in tourism, hotel management or travel agency. The significance of this requirement is not that the Provincial Government is forever bound by the earlier federal rule, but that it furnishes an objective indication of the nature of the office and the relevance which the rule-making authorities have historically attached to specialized experience for appointment to it.
Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 11 15 . The significance of specialized education and experience assumes even greater importance because the Controller is not merely required to perform routine administrative or coordinating functions; as the head of the Department, he is expected to provide its professional leadership, formulate and implement its vision, guide its direction and exercise informed judgment in matters falling within its specialized domain. Officers belonging to PAS/PMS are undoubtedly qualified public administrators and may possess substantial experience in general administration; however, such general administrative competence cannot, by itself, be regarded as a substitute for substantive knowledge and practical experience in the field which the officer is required to lead and regulate. Administrative competence may complement specialized expertise, but where the office carries responsibility for the overall direction of a specialized Department, relevant academic qualification and practical experience bear a direct and rational relationship to the effective discharge of its functions and, therefore, cannot reasonably be treated as irrelevant to the suitability of the incumbent.
16 . The same consideration is reflected in the service structure below the post of Controller, where experience has been treated as an essential eligibility criterion for progression within the Tourist Services cadre. Under the Punjab Youth Affairs, Sports, Archaeology & Tourism Department (Tourist Service Dying Cadre) Employees Service Rules, 2017, framed in exercise of the powers conferred by section 23 of the Punjab Civil Servants Act, 1974, the post of Deputy Controller (BS-18), which is immediately below the post of Controller, requires, in addition to the prescribed academic qualification, five years’ experience as a supervisor in the field of tourism, hotel management or travel agency.
The same Rules also provide for appointment by promotion against 50% of the posts of Deputy Controller from amongst Assistant Controllers (BS- 17) having five years’ service in BS -17. In this statutory context, the complete dispensation with any requirement of relevant experience for appointment to the higher and functionally more significant post of Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 12 Controller is difficult to reconcile with the service structure devised by the Provincial Government itself. If the rule-making authority considered five years’ relevant experience necessary even for appointment to the post of Deputy Controller, there appears to be no discernible rational basis for treating experience as wholly irrelevant to appointment as Controller, who heads the specialized Department. The executive’s power to reform the service structure cannot be equated with an unfettered and unbridled power to dispense with all rational criteria for appointment to a specialized statutory office.
17 . The authority of the Government to regulate its services and determine the method of appointment to a civil post, though broad, is subject to the constitutional guarantees governing equality, fairness and opportunity in public employment. In this regard, Article 27 of the Constitution is required to be read in conjunction with, inter alia , Articles 2A, 18 and 25. In the case of “Mushtaq Ahmad Mohal and others v. The Honourable Lahore High Court, Lahore and others” (1997 SCMR
1043) , the Supreme Court observed:
“We may observe that Article 27 of the Constitution is to be read in conjunction with inter alia Articles 2A, 18 and 25 of the Constitution. Aforesaid Articles 2A and 18 of the Constitution have already been referred to hereinabove.
Whereas above Article 25 of the Constitution guarantees that all citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection and that they shall not be discriminated on the basis of sex alone. Inter alia the above Articles of the Constitution are designed, intended and directed to bring about an egalitarian society based on Islamic concept of social justice.” The same constitutional conception has more recently been reaffirmed by the Supreme Court in “General Post Office, Islamabad and others v.
Muhammad Jalal” (PLD 2024 SC 1276) . While examining the validity of rules and policies governing appointments in the public service, the Supreme Court observed that “The Government and public sector employment cannot be allowed to be parceled out to the functionaries of the Sta te” and that the Constitution stipulates that equal employment and Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 13 economic opportunities must be provided to all citizens; economic justice, being a component of social justice, focuses on creating equal opportunities for all within society. The Supreme Court further held that appointments which obstruct qualified citizens from competing for entry into the service of Pakistan according to their ability and eligibility negate equality of opportunity, competition and merit and defeat the object of good governance. It was also emphasized that good governance cannot be achieved by exercising discretionary powers unreasonably or arbitrarily and that a law, policy or rule which is manifestly inconsistent with constitutional commands and discriminatory is subject to judicial review. Significantly, applying these constitutional principles, the Supreme Court in the said case declared the policies and rules providing appointments without open advertisement, competition and merit to be discriminatory and ultra vires Articles 3, 4, 5(2), 18, 25(1) and 27 of the Constitution, while emphasizing that equal employment opportunities, transparency and merit are essential to good governance and that discretionary powers cannot be exercised unreasonably or arbitrarily.
18 . The foregoing principles make it clear that although the Government possesses considerable latitude in structuring its services and determining the method of appointment to a civil post, such power is not unconfined. The framework of public employment remains subject to the constitutional requirements of equality, fairness, merit and nondiscrimination. The impugned Rule must, therefore, be tested against these constitutional standards.
19 . Within this constitutional framework, Article 25 does not prohibit the State from making classifications. It does, however, require that any differential treatment rest upon a reasonable basis. The Supreme Court in “I.A. Sherwani and others v. Government of Pakistan and others” (1991 SCMR 1041) authoritatively held that equal protection of law does not envisage that every person must be treated alike in all circumstances; persons similarly situated or similarly placed are required to be treated alike, while classification is permissible where it is founded Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 14 upon a reasonable distinction or basis. The same principle has been reiterated in “Syed Azam Shah v. Federation of Pakistan through Secretary Cabinet Division, Cabinet Secretariat, Islamabad and another” (2022 SCMR 201) and “Hadayat Ullah and others v. Federation of Pakistan and others” (2022 SCMR 1691) . In Syed Azam Shah case it was explained that the concept of “intelligible differentia” connotes a comprehensible dissimilarity between those grouped together and those left out, and that such differentiation or categorization must have a logical and commonsensical nexus with the object sought to be achieved. Thus, the constitutional requirement of equality does not prevent the Government from prescribing different eligibility criteria for different posts or classes of officers; what it prohibits is a classification which is arbitrary, lacks an intelligible basis or bears no rational nexus with the object sought to be achieved.
20 . No such rational nexus is discernible from the impugned Rule. It does not require the officer proposed to be posted as Controller to possess any relevant academic qualification, specialized training or experience. Nor does it prescribe any objective yardstick by which the suitability of an otherwise eligible PAS/PMS officer is to be assessed with reference to the specialized functions of the office. Consequently, an officer may be selected solely by reason of belonging to the specified service and grade, irrespective of whether he possesses any knowledge or practical experience of the field which he would be required to administer. Conversely, an officer possessing the relevant academic qualification and experience considered significant by the earlier service regimes is excluded from meaningful consideration merely because of his service affiliation. The distinction is thus founded upon service identity rather than upon any characteristic bearing a rational relationship with the functions of the post. Indeed, the very considerations which are objectively relevant to the performance of the office have been excluded from the eligibility framework, while an otherwise unrelated characteristic has been made the decisive basis for Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 15 eligibility. Such a classification cannot be regarded as reasonable merely because it has been incorporated in a statutory rule or is sought to be justified as an administrative policy. A rule governing public employment cannot, consistently with the constitutional guarantees of equality of opportunity, merit and fairness, confer an exclusive advantage upon a particular class of officers without prescribing objective criteria having a rational nexus with the duties of the post.
21 . The conclusion is further reinforced by the nature of the statutory functions attached to the office. If the rule-making authority itself considered five y ears’ relevant supervisory experience necessary for appointment to the immediately subordinate post of Deputy Controller and the earlier service regime considered twelve years’ supervisory experience in the relevant field necessary for appointment as Controller, there must be some rational explanation for dispensing altogether with relevant experience and qualification when prescribing the eligibility of the Controller who is to head the specialized Department. No such basis is disclosed by the impugned Rule. The defect, therefore, does not lie in the Government’s decision to depart from the earlier promotional arrangement; rather, it lies in the manner in which that policy has been translated into a rule which confers eligibility upon one class of officers solely on account of their service affiliation while excluding persons possessing qualifications and experience directly relevant to the functions of the post. The rule consequently substitutes an objective and functionally relevant eligibility framework with a discretion which is not guided by any discernible standard relating to the suitability of the incumbent for the specialized office. As observed by the Supreme Court in General Post Office case (supra), good governance cannot be achieved by exercising discretionary powers unreasonably or arbitrarily; rather, constitutional requirements of justness, fairness and openness must govern the exercise of such discretion. The discretion conferred by the impugned Rule, being unsupported by intelligible standards and lacking a rational nexus with Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 16 the object sought to be achieved, therefore suffers from the vice of arbitrariness and discriminatory classification in violation of Article 25 of the Constitution and is inconsistent with the constitutional requirement of equality of opportunity in public employment.
22 . This Court is conscious that it cannot substitute its own administrative preference for that of the Executive. The constitutional issue is not whether a Controller ought necessarily to be appointed by promotion rather than posting, nor whether an officer belonging to PAS/PMS is incapable of performing the functions of the post. Those are matters falling within the executive domain. The narrower and decisive question is whether, while exercising its rule-making power, the Government could lawfully confine eligibility to PAS/PMS officers without prescribing any educational qualification, specialized training or relevant experience commensurate with the functions of a specialized statutory office. The Constitution does not require the Government to perpetuate a particular method of recruitment, but it does require that the method ultimately prescribed for public employment operate within the bounds of equality, merit, fairness and non-discrimination. For the reasons recorded above, the answer is in the negative. The impugned Rule, to that extent, is arbitrary and discriminatory and cannot be allowed to stand.
23 . For the foregoing reasons, the Tourism, Archaeology and Museums Department (Tourist Services) Rules, 2025, issued through Notification No.SOR-III(S&GAD)1-25/2025 dated 30.10.2025, to the extent they govern appointment to the post of Controller, are hereby set aside. The competent authority is directed to reframe the relevant provision governing appointment to the post of Controller in accordance with the constitutional requirements discussed hereinabove, by prescribing reasonable, objective and functionally relevant educational qualifications and experience and by providing an intelligible criterion for selection. Upon reframing of the said provision, the appointment to the post of Controller shall thereafter be made afresh in accordance with Writ Petition No.30572 of 2026 17 the duly reframed Rules. The aforesaid exercise, including the making of fresh appointment, shall be completed as expeditiously as possible and preferably within three months from the receipt of a copy of this judgment. A compliance report shall be submitted before this Court through the Deputy Registrar (Judicial) within the aforesaid period.
24 . The petition in hand is allowed in the above terms.
(RAHEEL KAMRAN)
JUDGE
Announced in the Open Court on 01.09.2026.
JUDGE
Approved for reporting.
JUDGE
Azhar*

Case: Crl. Misc-Post-arrest Bail-PPC 2598-B-26 (MUHAMMAD SHAKEEL VS STATE ETC ).
Court: Lahore High Court, Lahore. Case No: Crl. Misc-Post-arrest Bail-PPC 2598-B-26. Title: Crl. Misc-Post-arrest Bail-PPC 2598-B-26 (MUHAMMAD SHAKEEL VS STATE ETC ). Official Ref: 2026LHC5453. Author Judge: Mr. Justice Khalid Ibn-i-Aziz. Judgment Date (as displayed): 02-09-2026. Record Type: FULL_TEXT_VERBATIM (complete judgment text extracted from the official court PDF). Source URL: https://sys.lhc.gov.pk/appjudgments/2026LHC5453.pdf. Verified: 2026-09-06 against the official court repository.
VERBATIM JUDGMENT TEXT (extracted from the official PDF at the Source URL; 3 pages; spelling, punctuation and lineation as in the PDF):
Form No. HCJD/C - 121.
ORDER SHEET
IN THE LAHORE HIGH COURT ,
RAWALPINDI BENCH, RAWALPINDI
JUDICIAL DEPARTMENT.
Crl. Misc. No . 25 9 8 - B of 202 6 .
Muhammad Shakeel V s . The State etc .
S.No. Of order/ Proceeding Date of order/ Proceeding Order with signature of judge, and that of parties or counsel, where necessary, 25 . 08 .202 6 . Mr. Khadim Hussain Malik , Advocate for the petitioner.
M alik Rafaqat Ali , DP G for the State with Amir S.I. Muhammad Shakeel , petitioner through instant petition seeks pos t arrest bail in case FIR No . 01 , dated 02 . 0 1 .202 6 , offence s under Section s 322, 320, 337 - G, 279, 427 PPC, registered at Police Station City Hassan Abd a l , District Attock .
2. As per allegations leveled in the FIR , on 02.01.2026 at
about 03.15 P.M., a dumper No.9722/D.I. Khan, came on G.T. Road from Peshawar side , was being driven by some unknown person rashly and negligently, who hit the motorcycle of Mudassar (son of the complainant) from back side , due to which his son was severely injured and later on succumbed to injuries.
3 . Arguments h eard . Record perused .
4 . This Court has observed that initially F.I.R. was lodged against an unknown accused person and later on complainant got recorded his supplementary statement on 04.01.2026 , wherein, he nominated one Tariq Mehmood s/o Muhammad Maskeen as accused, whose pre - arrest bail was confirmed by the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Hassan Abd al , Attock vide order dated 22.01.2026 . Thereafter on
22.06.2026, the present petitioner Muhammad Shakeel was
nominated in this case by the prosecution on the basis of C.D.R. i.e. after a period of more than five months . Moreover , t he offence under Section 320 PPC has been deleted vide zimni No.6 dated 22.06.2026 and offenc e under Section 322 PPC has been added (which is non - bailable), whereas, the Crl. Misc. No. 25 9 8 - B of 20 2 6 .
remaining offences i.e. under Section s 279, 337 - G and 427 PPC are bailable. The punishment provided for the offence under Section 322 PPC is only Diyat . Although the offence under Section 322 PPC is non - bailable yet no punishment of imprisonment is provided for the said offence. If , an accused charged under Section 322 PPC, upon pleading his guilty or after his trial is convicted, he can only be kept in confinement in case he commi ts default in the payment of Diyat amount, a t moment , incarceration of the petitioner pending trial would amount to double jeopardy and i t is settled law that where the criminal liability of an offence is Diyat only , th at offence does not fall within the p rohibitory clause and where an offen c e does not fall within the prohibitory clause, the acceptance of bail is the rule and the rejection is an exception. Reliance has been placed on the case s of Tariq Bashir and others v. The State ( PLD 1995 Supreme Court 34 ) and Muhammad Zahid versus The State and another ( 2021 YLR 1959 ). Moreover , the complainant has not mentioned the name of even a single witness in the F.I.R. who has seen the accused while committing the occurrence. In the instant ca se, present petitioner has been nominated on the basis of mere C.D.R data and the admissibility of the same would be determined by the learned trial Court, which has not yet concluded . In the case of Naveed Sattar versus The State and others (202 4 S CMR 205 ) , the Hon’ble Supreme Court has observed as under: - “… So far as the Call Data Record (CDR) is concerned, this Court in a number of cases has held that in absence of any concrete material the CDR is not a conclusive piece of evidence to ascertain the guilt or otherwise of an accused .” In the case of Shameem Bibi versus The State and others (202 2 S CMR 2077 ) , the Hon’ble Supreme Court has observed as under: - “ We have specifically asked the learned Law Officer and the learned counsel for the Crl. Misc. No. 25 9 8 - B of 20 2 6 .
complainant to sh ow us from record any material, which could prima facie connect the petitioner with the commission of crime but except the Call Data Record (CDR), they could not show us anything. This court in a number of cases has held that in absence of any concrete mat erial the Call Data Record is not a conclusive piece of evidence to ascertain the guilt or otherwise of an accused. On our query, learned Law Officer admitted that as yet there is no evidence that the mobile phone belonged to the petitioner and the SIM was in her name. In these circumstances, the (Call Data Record) CDR in isolation does not advance the prosecution’s case unless and until some credible material in this regard has been collected.” Besides, the liability of the present petitioner or charge leveled against him could only be determined by the trial court after recording and evaluating the evidence.
5 . The petitioner is behind the bars since 22 . 06 .202 6 . The investigation of the case is complete and person of the petitioner is no more required by the police for the purpose of further investigation, therefore, his further detention in jail would serve no useful purpose to the prosecution.
6 . For what has been discussed above , this petition is accepted and the petitioner is allowed post - arrest bail subject to his furnishing bail bonds in the sum of Rs. 10 ,00,000/ - with two suret ies in the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned trial court. It is further observe d that the observatio ns made hereinabove are tentative in nature and shall have no bearing on any of the other proceeding s connected to this case.
( Khalid Ibn - i - Aziz )
JUDGE
Approved for reporting .
Judge This order has been dictated, pronounced, prepared and signed on 25 .08.2026.
Umar Hayat *

Official Ref: 2025LHC8715. Author Judge: Mr. Justice Tariq Saleem Sheikh. Judgment Date (as displayed): 02-09-2026. Record Type: FULL_TEXT_VERBATIM (complete judgment text extracted from the official court PDF). Source URL: https://sys.lhc.gov.pk/appjudgments/2025LHC8715.pdf.
