MUHAMMAD KAMRAN KHAN MULAKHAIL, J: This Civil Misc A ppeal No. 15 of 2020 filed under Section 21 (4) of the Trade Organization Act 2013, against the order Notification No. F. No. 3 (08)/2017 dated 20 th April 2018 issued by Director General of Trade Organization (Office of Regulator of Trade Organization) and order dated 06 th November 2020, passed by the Secretary Commerce, Government of Pakistan, whereby the appeals filed by the appellant was dismissed; similarly, the connected appeal Nos.
16 to 22, 25 of 2020 & 82 of 2019, against the order of the Regulator and Appellat e Authority have also been filed . Since common question of law and facts have been raised, therefore, I propose to dispose of these appeals through this common judgment.
2. C ivil Misc Appeal No. 1 5 of 2020
C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 5 - Brief facts of the case are that the appellant w as lawful license holder bearing No. 247, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice No.
F.No.12(02)/2017 - TO dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sh aring the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No.
18(08)/2017 - TO, dated 15 th March 2018 issued to the appellant , in response whereof, the appellant’s legal attorney visited the office of responde nt No.2, but he was not allowed to represent the case, meanwhile, the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No.
F.NO3(08)/2017 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ) , against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court , but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 16 of 20 20 Succinct facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 232, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 , duly obtained after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under R ule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly replied, but C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 6 thereafter, a show cause No. 18( 13 )/201 6 - TO, dated 09 th March 2018 i ssued to the appellant, however, due to minimum time given to the appellant, he was not able to appear and defend his case before the DGTO , meanwhile, the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No. F.NO3( 13 )/201 6 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned noti fication ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 17 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 249, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 , having been obtained after ful filling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, which notice w as duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 1 7 ( 04)/2017 - TO, dated 13 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, however, without extending an adequate opportunity of hearing to the appellant, his license was cancelled vide letter No. F.N o .3( 04 )/201 7 - TO da ted 2 5 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 7 the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismis sed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 18 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 241, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 20 13 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, wh ich notice was duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 18(13)/2016 - TO, dated 09 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, however, due to minimum time given to the appellant, he was not able to appear and represent his case before the DGTO, meanwhile, t he appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No.
F.NO.3(22)/2016 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was remanded to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th Novembe r 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 19 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful lice nse holder bearing No. 236, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 8 requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 18(15)/2016 - TO, dated 13 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, however, due to minimum time given to the appellant, he was not able to appear and represent his case before the DGTO, meanwhile, the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No.
F.NO.3(15)/2016 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matte r was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 20 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 24 8 , issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 18( 05 )/201 7 - TO, dated 09 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, but on the date fixed for hearing of the matter, the appellant was not allowed to appear and represent his case before C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 9 the respondent No.2 , meanwhile, the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No. F.NO. 305 2)/201 7 dated 2 3 rd April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide o rder dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 21 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 238, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling a ll legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for sharing the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly r eplied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 18(16)/2016 - TO, dated 13 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, however, due to minimum time given to the appellant, he was not able to appear and represent his case before the DGTO, meanwhile, the appellant’s licens e was cancelled vide letter No.
F.NO.3(16)/2016 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 10 - No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 22 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No . 237, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that the appellant was issued a notice under Rule 6 (1) (k) of the Trade Organization Rules, 2013, dated 01 st August 2018, by the respondent No.2 for s haring the post registration codal formalities, which notice was duly replied, but thereafter, a show cause No. 18(1 4 )/2016 - TO, dated 09 th March 2018 issued to the appellant, however, due to minimum time given to the appellant, he was not able to appear an d represent his case before the DGTO, meanwhile, the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No.
F.NO.3( 14 )/2016 dated 20 th April 2018 ( impugned notification ), against which a constitutional petition was preferred, but, the matter was referred to the concerned authority vide order dated 12 th November 2019 by this court, but the relevant forum viz respondent No.3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
Civil Misc Appeal No. 25 of 2020 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 145, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements; that since the appellant was working primarily for C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 11 promoting interests of women business community of the province, but was restricted by the respondent from functioning its work; that the appellant was issued a show cause No. 1 2 ( 01 )/201 8 - TO, dated 03th October 2018 , which was duly replied explaining the delay in filing the applicati on for renewal of the license, but the appellant’s license was cancelled vide letter No. F.NO. 04 ( 07 )/201 3 - TO dated 2 8 th March 201 9 ( impugned notification ), however, after lapse of 18 months of direction issued by this court in Civil Appeal No. 23 of 2019 v ide order dated 24 th April 2019, the respondent No. 3 dismissed the appeal vide order dated 06 th November 2020 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
C ivil Misc Appeal No. 82 of 20 19 Brief facts of the case are that the appellant was lawful license holder bearing No. 185, issued under the Trade Organization Act, 2013 after fulfilling all legal and formal requirements and was incorporated with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan under Companies Ordinance, 1984 and was allotted Universal Identi fication No. 0094621 and was also registered with Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce & Industry (FPCCI) as a trade body; that on 02 nd May 2019, the appellant was called for personal hearing in the office of respondent No.2 in response to complaint filed by the respondent No.3 , but on 14 th June 2019 the appellant’s license was cancelled , against which an appeal was preferred, but the same was also C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 12 declined vide order dated 01 st July 2019 ( impugned order ), hence this appeal.
3. During pendency of the appeals, the
applicant/intervener Jamal - ud - Din, filed applications in each appeal with request to be arrayed as party to the appeal on the ground that on his application, the licenses of the appellants were cancelled.
The said applications were contested by the appellants on legal as well as factual grounds, by filing separate rejoinders to the same.
4 . D r. Pervaiz Khan, learned counsel for the appellant in Civil Misc Appeal No s . 15, 17, 16, 18, 19, 21, 20, 22 & 25 of 2020 contended that the impugned or ders are outcome of certain illegalities and irregularities manifesting malafide on part of the respondent No.2; that without adhering to the relevant provision of law and rules the respondent No.2 has ordered for cancellation of the appellant’s license th at too on the strength of not fulfilling post license conditions, whereas no opportunity of hearing was afforded to the appellants to explain their position in pursuance of explanation letters and show cause issued by the respondent No.2; that as per law a nd Rules the Director General Trade Organization was appointed as Regulator , but in the instant case the impugned notifications/orders have been passed by the respondent No.2 ( Depu ty Director, Trade Organization , but there is nothing on record with regard to appointment of respondent No.2 nor any power has been delegated by the Regulator to the respondent, thus, C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 13 the impugned notifications are not sustainable and liable to be set aside .
Mr. Munir Ahmed Kakar, Muhammad Nazeer Tareen and Muhammad Asif Reki, a ppearing for appellants in Civil Misc Appeal Nos. 16, 18 & 20 of 2020, while relying on the arguments advanced by the Dr. P e rvaiz Khan , added that the impugned orders have been passed without having any authority in the matter, thus, are not sustainable; that even otherwise the post license conditions were satisfactor il y fulfilled by the license holders, while the minor deficiencies, if any, could have been met with or dealt with by at least imposing minor fine , thus, the impugned orders besides being passed without any authority are also harsh in nature; he therefore, urged for setting aside of the impugned orders/notifications.
Conversely, Mr. Tahir Iqbal Khatak , Assistant Attorney General.
Mr. Naseer - ud - Din Mengal , Assistant Advocate General, assisted b y Mr.
Zain - ul - Abidin, GSP Officer Ministry of Commerce Learned Additional Advocate General submitted that the appellants failed to fulfill the conditions of post license requirements despite lapse of one year period and the thus, the impugned orders were p assed by the respondent No.2 that too with the approval of the Regulator; that the entire proceedings were carried put in accordance with the prevailing Act and Rules and with the approval of the Regulator of Trade Organization ; he therefore, urged for dis missal of the appeals.
C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 14 - Mr. Muhammad Amir Nawaz Rana , Advocate appearing for the intervener, contended that the intervener/ applicant was/ is necessary party to the appeal as on his complain t the license s of the appellants were cancelled, but the appellants intentionally failed to array the applicant as party to the appeal; that the appeals are filed beyond the stipulated period, therefore, the same being time barred are not sustainable; that the instant appeals are filed just to disturb the forthcoming election of Chamber of Commerce ; the learned counsel requested for arraying the applicant as necessary party to the petition and also urged for dismissal of the petition.
In rebuttal, the learned counsel for the appellants contended that the intervener/appli cant has nothing to do with the these appeals as the matter is in between the appellants and the Trade Organization, thus, the applicant/intervener is neither necessary party nor he has any locus standi to file the instant application; therefore, the appli cation merits dismissal.
5 . I have heard learned counsel for the parties and the learned Advocate General at reasonable length and have also gone through the record of the case with theirable assistance. However, before dilating upon the merits of case, it would be apt to reproduce the sections 22(1) of Trade Organization Act 2013 :
Section 22. Delegation of Powers. — (1) The Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette , direct that all or any of its powers under this Act shall, in relati on to such matters or subject C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 15 to such conditions as may be specified therein, also be exercisable by the Regulator.
(2) The Regulator may, by order in writing, authorise the Administrator or any other officer to exercise and perform any of his powers and f unctions under this Act .” 6 . The afore quoted provision unequivocally reveal s that the Federal Government may delegate its power to the Regulator to exercise its powers under the Act, while sub - Section (2) of the Section 22 speaks that the Regulator may further delegate its powers to any other subordinate officer. In the case in hand the Government of Pakistan vide Notification dated 06 th March 2013, appointed the Director General Trade Organization as Regulator to perform the functions and exercise the p owers vested in the “ Regulator ” under the Act 2013 . In order to ascertain the legality of appointment of Regulator and delegation of powers to him, this court vide order dated 27 th August 2021, directed the official respondents to produce the documents whe reby the Regulator was appointed. The order runs as under :
“Mr. Irshad Ahmed, Director, representative of Trade Organization, Islamabad is in attendance along with Mr. Tahir Iqbal Khattak, Assistant Attorney General, who apprised the court about the relev ant provisions of Section 12 & 22 of Trade Organization Act, 2013.
After perusal of referred to provisions, he is directed to produce the relevant notification/summary and order in writing with C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 16 regard to delegation of powers initially to the Regulator a nd thereafter to any other officer of the Directorate of Trade Organization.
Mr. Jamaluddin, intervener requests for adjournment on account of non - availability of his counsel, while one Mr. Daroo Khan, entered appearance and submitted an application unde r Order 1 Rule 10 CPC filed in Civil Misc: Appeal No.15 of 2020. Copy whereof has been delivered to the counsel for the appellant, who seeks time to go through the same and file a reply, if so advised.
To come up on 17.09.2021.
In compliance, the Direct or General, Trade Organization appeared and submitted details, however, expressed his inability to file the requisite summary with regard to appointment of Regulator of the Organization and requested for direction to the Ministry of Commerce for submi tting the requisite details, and thus the learned Deputy Attorney General was directed to file the requisite summary . But despite clear direction of this court the relevant documents pertaining to appointment of Regulator, followed by order of delegation of pow ers to him was not filed .
7 . Section 22 (2) of Trade Organizations Act, 2013, deals with the delegation of powers to the Regulator and in compliance, the Federal Government vide Notification dated 06 th March 2013 appointed the Director General Trade Organ izations as Regulator to perform the functions and exercise the powers vested in the Act
2013. Though , as per Notification dated 06
th March 2013 the powers were delegated, however, due to non - filing of the requisite C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 17 documents pertaining to delegation of po wers to the Regulator, whether the powers were duly exercised by the Federal Government . In order to elucidate the meaning of the term 'Federal Government' as well as the concept of 'executive powers', the Hon’ble A pex court conducted a detailed exposition of Pakistan's constitutional and political history , in case of “ Mustafa Impex, Karachi vs The Government of Pakistan through Secretary Finance, Islamabad ( PLD 2016 Supreme Court 808 ), whereby it was held that:
“ 84. We may now summarize our conclusions: -
(i) The Rules of Business, 1973 are
binding on the Government and a failure to follow them would lead to an order lacking any legal validity.
(ii) The Federal Government is the
collective entity described as the Cabinet constituting the Prime Minister and Federal Ministers.
(iii) Neither a Secretary, nor a Minister and
nor the Prime Minister are the Federal Government and the exercise, or purported exercise, of a statutory power exercisable by the Federal Government by any of them, especially, in relation to fiscal matters, is constitutionally invalid and a nullity in the eyes of the law. Similarly budgetary expenditure, or discretionary governmental expenditure can only be authorized by the Federal Government i.e. the Cabinet, and not C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 18 the Prime Minister o n his own.
(iv) Any Act, or statutory instrument (e.g.
the Telecommunication (Re - Organisation) Act, 1996) purporting to describe any entity or organization other than the Cabinet as the Federal Government is ultra vires and a nullity.
(v) The ordinance making power can only
be exercised after a prior consideration by the Cabinet. An ordinance issued without the prior approval of the Cabinet is not valid.
Similarly, no bill can be moved in Parliament on behalf of the Federal Government without having bee n approved in advance by the Cabinet. The Cabinet has to be given a reasonable opportunity to consider, deliberate on and take decisions in relation to all proposed legislation, including the Finance Bill or Ordinance or Act. Actions by the Prime Minister on his own, in this regard, are not valid and are declared ultra vires.
(vi) Rule 16(2) which apparently enables
the Prime Minister to bypass the Cabinet is ultra vires and is so declared.
(vii) Fiscal notifications enhancing the levy
of tax issued by the Secretary, Revenue Division, or the Minister, are ultra vires. (it is clarified, in passing, that this court has in the past consistently held that a greater latitude is allowed in relation to beneficial notifications and that principle still applies).
(viii) In consequence of the above findings the
C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 19 impugned notifications are declared ultra vires and are struck down. ” In the case in hand though, Notification No. F. No.
12(1)/2012 - TO dated 06 th March 2013 for appointment of Director General Trade Or ganization as “Regulator” and Notification of even number of even date for delegation of powers to the Regulator w ere placed on record , purporting to have be en issued by the Federal Government, but nothing has been placed on record to show that whether the approval of the cabinet was sought or otherwise?
Through separate notifications, but of even number and even date the Regulator has been appointed and has also been delegated the powers, however, I am unable to reconcile that whether the notification of a ppointment was issued earlier or the powers were delegated at first instance , whatever the case may be, both these exercises appears to have not been taken place with the authority of the cabinet. And thus, it cannot be concluded that the Notification s dat ed 06 th March 2013, are in line with guidelines framed by the Hon’ble Supreme Court in case of Mustafa Impex supra.
8 . The record is indicative of the fact that initially notice s under Section 6 (k) of the Rules 2 0 13 w ere issued to the appellants by the Deputy Director and thereafter show cause notice was also issued to the appellants by the said Deputy Director and finally the impugned orders followed by the impugned Notifications, whereby the license (s) of the appellant ( s ) was/were cancelled were issue d C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 20 by the Deputy Director, but it is evident that no powers were delegated to the Deputy Director by the Regulator under sub - Section (2) of Section 22 of the Act . Albeit, it was contended that the entire proceedings were carried out with the approval of the Regulator , but the record is silent about any order in writing of the Regulator, either authorizing the respondent No.2 or delegating any such power to her to perform any powers or functions. The law is also silent to the effect that the proceedings are t o be conducted with the approval of the Regulator , but it is clear enough that the powers are to be delegated to any officer and without issuing any order to the effect and nominating any officer, the proceedings carried out by the Deputy Director, Trader Organization, cannot be termed as legal proceedings . Thus, the entire proceedings carried out by the respondent No.2 commencing from issuance of notice, and finalizing with the passing of impugned order and issuance of impugned notification, are carried ou t without having any authority in the matter and without being empowered to exercise such powers. The learned appellate authority while deciding the appeals filed by the appellants also overlooked , rather ignored this legal aspect of the case and wrongly u pheld the impugned orders of the respondent No.2.
9 . As regards the right of the appellants for having protected right of business and trade, Article 18 of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan protects the right of every citizen to C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 21 have freedo m of business and trade. The provisions of Article 18 ibid are reproduced below for ease of reference: -
18. Freedom of trade, business or profession.
Subject to such qualifications, if any, as may be prescribed by law, every citizen shall have the right t o enter upon any lawful profession or occupation, and to conduct any lawful trade or business:
Provided that nothing in this Article shall prevent:
(a) the regulation of any trade or profession
by a licensing system; or
(b) the regulation of trade, comm erce or
industry in the interest of free competition therein; or
(c) the carrying on, by the Federal
Government or a Provincial Government, or by a corporation controlled by any such Government, of any trade, business, industry or service, to the exclusio n, complete or partial, of other persons. ” [Emphasis supplied] 10 . Likewise, Article 25 of the Constitution provides equal protection of law to the citizens, thus, no restriction can be imposed upon a citizen relating to the freedom of trade, business o r profession and if the same is imposed, it will be subject to Article 18 ibid, which does not confer on any individual or association, the monopoly right to carry on trade or business without competition from other eligible persons rather it prohibits the same. Article 25, while ensuring equality of all citizens, covers the entire field of C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 22 - State action, it would extend not only when a citizen is discriminated against in the matter of exercise of his rights, but also in matter of granting privileges vis - a - v is giving jobs by the State granting permits or licenses, inviting tenders for Government contracts or issuing quotas. Article 25 of the Constitution of Pakistan 1973 stipulates as follows: - "25. Equality of citizens. (1) All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law.
(2) There shall be no discrimination on the basis of sex.
(3) Nothing in this Article shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the protection of women and children." 1 1 . A rule of procedu re also cannot be excluded from Article 25 of the Constitution as every citizen is entitled to availability of same procedural venues as are provided to others including the State institutions, in like circumstances. Any discrimination in the procedure whi le dealing with the citizen shall offend Article 25 of the Constitution, whereas, the aforesaid action taken by the respondents resulting into cancellation of the license of appellants are highly discriminatory in nature while jeopardizing the rights of the appellants . Article 25 not only protects the petitioner against discriminatory procedural laws, but equally applies against the discriminatory substantive actions, especially in the present scenario, when the country more particularly the province is fac ing the financial constraint s, and therefore, the citizens are also facing financial fixes, but instead of providing C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 23 them fair and free opportunity of trade and business, they are being restrained from carrying out their businesses , that too , on mere techn ical basis and without adopting the due course of law .
12 . As far as, the application filed under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC by the intervener is concerned, admittedly the matter is in between the appellants and the respondent Department , and the applicant has f ailed to show his locus standi to be arrayed as party to the appeals . The parties can either be classified as a necessary party or a proper party. A person, who ought to have been joined, is a necessary party, and a person whose presence is necessary to ef fectually and completely adjudicate upon and settle all points involved in the lis , is a proper property. Parties cannot be added in any other case. In the instant case no relief is sought against the intervener and thus he is not a necessary party and sim ilarly, his presence is also not necessary , as the decision can be made in his absence , and thus, he also does not fall within the definition of proper party. The matter might have been reported and initiated on the complaint of the intervener, but it does not entitle the applicant to be arrayed as necessary party, therefore, the applications filed by the intervener under Order 1 Rule X CPC are dismissed.
However, without rendering any observation on merit s and demerit s of the case, we deem it appropriate to set aside the impugned orders and notifications, whereby the license of the appellants were cancelled, consequently, the licenses of the C ivil Misc Appeal Nos. 1 5 to 2 2 , 25 of 2020 & 82 of 20 1 9 . - 24 appellants are restored and the matter is remanded to the Regulator , Trade Organization , with the direction to ensur e the appointment and delegation of powers as per law and dictum laid down by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, It’s further directed that at least two months’ (60 days) time be extended in favour of the appellants to make - up the deficiencies in their post licensing documents and thereafter, their cases be decided afresh, but strictly in accordance with law and keeping in view the observations made herein above, with an opportunity of hearing to the appellants.
Order accordingly.
These details shall co nstitute the reasons of short order dated th October 2021.
Quetta, Reasons drawn : Sd/xxxxx On 11 th November , 2021. JUDGE

Muhammad Kamran Khan Mulakhail, J. By this common judgment, we propose to d ispose of the Service Judicial Appeal Nos. 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 0 7 , 09 and 1 0 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 , as common question of law and facts are i nvolved in all these appeals.
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 6
2. These service appeals are preferred by the appellants /
judicial officers of the District Judiciary in their respective capacity, being aggrieved of Notification No. 1207/120 - Estt: dated th March 2017 ( ‘impugned Notification ’ ), whereby on recommendation of Promotion Committee of the High Court , the Administration Committee granted antedated pr omotion to the respondents, who, according to the appellants’ perception, were otherwise junior to the m, resultantly, the appellant s were superseded by means of impugned Notification , whereas , through Service Appeal Nos. 07, 09 and 10 of 2019, the seniority list issued by the High Court has been assailed on entirely different grounds to each other . Thus, in order to better understandi ng of controversy raised and challenged thrown upon the impugned Notification , a brief resume of each appeal is reproduced herein below :
I. Service Judicial Appeal No.1 of 2017 . This appeal has been presented by appellant Abdul Hafeez , (civil Judge), bei ng aggrieved of impugned Notification mainly on averments that he w as appointed as Civil Judge/Judicial Magistrate by the High Court of Balochistan on recommendation of Balochistan Public Service Commission (“ BPSC ” ) , vide Notification dated 28 th May 2001, whereas respondents herein ( judicial officers ) were appointed respectively in 1997, 1998 & 1999, on ad - hoc basis, but their services were regularized vide Notification dated 10 th December 2001; that the Notification of regularization of ad - hoc appointees w as challenged before Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 7 this tribunal through service appeal No s . 1 of 2002, 6, 7, 8 & 9 of 2015 , which were accepted vide judgment dated th April 2016, ( “Tribunal’s Judgment” ) thereby , declaring the appellant and other non - appealing judicial officers appoi nted on regular basis on the recommendations of the BPSC to be senior to that of the ad - hoc appointees . Consequently, the matter was referred to the Administrative Committee of the High Court, and thereafte r, the Administrative Committee, on recommendation s of the Promotion Committee , granted antedated promotion to the respondents by superseding the appellant, despite the fact that he w as / is perfor ming his dut ies with utmost diligence and required standard of satisfaction.
II. Service Judicial Appeal No s .2 & 3 of 2017 . Appellants Bashir Ahmed Badini and Muhammad Jamshed Khan jointly , the appellant Nauroz Khan Hoth, ( Service Appeal No.3 of 2017 ) District & Sessions Judges, have separately called in question the impugned Notification , based on a contention tha t most junior and inexperience d judicial officers have been granted antedated promotions and placed senior to them, despite the fact that they , by rendering the services were more experience d , whereas the respondents, without even having the qualifying min imum length of service were granted antedated promotion and placed higher in the seniority list, thereby caused serious Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 8 prejudice to them, thus, the impugned Notification has been sought to be withdrawn .
III. Service Judicial Appeal Nos. 04 & 05 of 2017 .
A ppellants Inayatullah and Najeebullah , have called in question the impugned Notification mainly on a strength that they were appointed as Civil Judge/Judicial Magistrate vide Notification No.983/148 - Sadd/Admn dated 05 th April 2000, by the High Court of Bal ochistan on recommendation of BPSC , wherein , the appellant Inayatullah was at serial No.3 and the appellant Najeebullah was at serial No. 6 of the merit list . Whereas, the respondent No.4 Imran Siddique also appointed , vide same Notification was at serial No.4 of the merit list. The respondent No. 5 to 7 were also appointed by the High Court of Balochistan on the recommendation of BPSC on th May 2001; that some of the judicial officers were also appointed in 1997, 1998 & 1999, on ad - hoc basis, though thei r services were regularized vide Notification dated 10 th December 2001 from the respective date(s) of their appointment(s); that vide Tribunal’s judgment the Administrative Committee on recommendation of the Promotion Committee granted antedated promotion to the respondents by superseding the appellants against the prevailing rules, precedents and principles of natural justice .
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 9 IV. Service Judicial Appeal Nos. 9 and 10 of 2017 .
Appellants namely Najeebullah and Inayatullah, also separately challenged anoth er Notification No.3051/120 - Estt: dated 13 th June 2017 (second Notification ) , whereby , though they were promoted as Additional District and Sessions Judges (BPS - 20) on regular basis , but with immediate effect, wh en their other associates were granted anted ated promotion as AD&SJ w.e.f. 31.03.2010, wh ile earlier they were superseded by promoting the junior judicial officers, without even communicating any reason for not considering them , and their such right of promotion is/was protected under the Constituti on of Pakistan and they have been dealt with arbitrary and discriminative manner .
V. Service Judicial Appeal No. 10 & 11 of 2020 . Appellant Rahim Dad , (Additional District & Sessions Judge) and the appellant Abdul Ali Jalalzai (Senior Civil Judge) have sep arately expressed their grievances against the impugned Notification on the averments that they were appointed as Civil Judge s /Judicial Magistrate s (BPS - 17) by the High Court of Balochistan on recommendations of the BPSC ; that by means of Tribunal’s judgme nt they alongwith other judicial officers were declared senior to the judicial officers appointed by the High Court of Balochistan on ad - hoc basis , respectively in the year 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2000, who se services were regularized Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 10 vide Notification dated 10 th December 2001, but the Promotion Committee of the High Court through the impugned Notification granted antedated promotion to the junior judicial officers by superseding the senior judicial officers, while the back benefit was also denied to the appel lants; it was finally urged that the impugned Notification be recalled/set aside and a fresh Notification was sought to be issued , thereby , implementing the Tribunal’s judgment dated 25 th April 2016 in its letter and spirit, beside s awarding back benefits to them.
VI. Service Judicial Appeal Nos. 07, 09 & 10 of 2019 .
Appellants Nasir Khan Yousafzai, Nazir Ahmed Khajak and Zafarullah Bazai , (District & Sessions Judges), have seperetaly called in question the impugned seniority list issued by the High Court of Balochistan, whereby the judicial officers , when granted antedated promotion on the strength of Tribunal’s judgment , were placed higher to them in the seniority list and they were placed junior, mainly on a strength that they were directly appointed by the High Court of Balochistan , vide Notification dated 19 th May 2015, whereas the respondents were given antedated promotion as District & Sessions Judges vide Notification dated 27 th March 2017, but w.e.f. 15 th May 2015; that they were appointed prior to the Tribunal’s judgment , on basis whereof, the impugned Notification of antedated promotion was issued. Thus they cannot be placed junior Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 11 to those who have been granted antedated promotion subsequent to the appellants’ appointment(s) on regular basis ; tha t they filed objections against the provisional seniority list, but so far, no decision was rendered and without deciding their objections , the impugned seniority list was issued, a ffecting their legal right; they finally prayed for rectification of the im pugned seniority list , by declaring them senior to that of the antedated promoted respondents .
3 . Mr. Gul Hassan , learned counsel for the appellants Najeebullah and Inayatullah (in Service Appeals No.04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017) , argued that the appellants being entitled for promotion and senior to the respondents as per the Tribunal ’s judgment , were required to be granted antedated promotion, but contrarily and in utter violation of the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court on a strength whereof , this Tribu nal’s judgment attained finality and has become a binding force, the appellants were superseded, however, no reason for deferring or superseding the appellants’ promotion was communicated to them, nor any reason was assigned in the minutes of meeting; that there is /was no allegation of legal or moral misconduct against the appellants, nor any adverse remarks are /were available against the m in their respective ACRs, but by means of impugned Notification , the appellants have been condemned unheard; that it wa s declared by the Tribunal that the appellants are senior (s) to the judicial officers appointed on ad - hoc basis, but the promotion committee while promoting the respondents, still placed Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 12 the appellants below then the ad - hoc appointees in violation of the T ribunal’s judgment; that on the one hand the ad - hoc appointees have been declared junior to them, but on the other , the appellants have been denied promotion, that too, without any explicit reasons or if any, same have never been conveyed to them. He final ly urged for setting aside the impugned Notification with further request to remit the matter to the promotion committee for de - novo consideration of the ir promotion in similar manner as their other counterparts and the ad - hoc judicial officers were treate d . He placed reliance on following citations :
i. ( 2002 SCMR 1056) Zafar ullah Baloch v Government of Balochistan and others ii. ( 1997 PLC (CS) 167) Secretary, Narcotics Control Division, Government of Pakistan Islamabad v Muhammad Sajjad and 4 others iii. Since, the judgment rendered by the Tribunal was in rem, therefore, all the judicial of ficers declared senior by the Tribunal were considered by the promotion committee, whereby , on scrutinizing the judicial record and performance, evaluating the conduct and examining the personal files of the aspirant judicial officers, recommendations were made to the extent of only those judicial officers, who were found fit for promotion by the committee, whereas the remaining judicial officers were superseded on the ground that they were not fit.
Before we proceed to examine the legality and proprietar y of the recommendations and Notification in question, it would be beneficial to Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 19 refer to the legal framework pertaining to the promotion of the civil servants and its procedure. It is section 9 of the Balochistan Civil Servants Act, 1973 that stipulated f or and deals with the promotion of a civil servant in the following terms:
"9. Promotion . --- (1) A civil servant possessing such minimum qualification as may be prescribed shall be eligible for promotion to a higher post for the time being reserved under the rules of departmental promotion in the service or cadre to which he belongs:
(2) A post referred to in subsection (1) may either be a selection post or a non - selection post to which promotions shall be made as may be prescribed.
(a) In the case of a se lection post, on the basis of
selection on merit ; and
(b) In the case of a non - selection post, on the basis of
seniority - cum - fitness . (emphasis provided).
The afore - quoted section provides that a promotion in a case of selection post shall be made on the basis of selection on merit , i.e.
fitness - cum - seniority, and in case of a non - selection post, on the basis of seniority - cum - fitness, whereas the ‘ Balochistan Additional District and Sessions Judges and District and Sessions Judges Service Rules, 2002 ’ , p rovides the appointment against the post of Additional District and Sessions Judges and against the post of District and Sessions Judge on the basis of seniority - cum - fitness. There is no denial of the fact that the posts carrying B - 19 and above are selection posts , thus the promotion to these posts shall be made on the basis of selection on merit. The seniority in the cases of promotion is merely one of factors, whereas, the basic factor is the merit and fitness of the candidate and in Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 20 case the promotion c ommittee reaches to the conclusion that the two or more than two candidates secure equal marks in merit/fitness, then the seniority would have a decisive role in deciding the case(s) of promotion between equally placed officers .
11. During course of hearing of these appeals, and on perusal
of the relevant Law, Rules, Notifications and record, it further transpired that initially ‘ Balochistan Additional District and Sessions Judges and District and Sessions Judges Service Rules, 1980 (“ Rules 1980 ” ) were fr amed and notified vide Notification No. SOR(2)62/S & GAD - 79, dated 03 rd April 1980 , whereas in sub - Rule (1) & (2) of Rule (5), the method of recruitment was also stipulated . Where in , promotion to the post of Additional District & Sessions Judge from amongst the Senior Civil Judges and the Judicial Magistrates was stipulated at the ratio of 50:50 , and similarly , for promotion to the post of District & Sessions Judge , 50% promotion quota was stipulated for the senior Additional District & Sessions Judge, 25% q uota was granted to the officers belonging to the Central and Provincial Governments , and 25% quota was reserved for initial appointment. The said rules were reframed and notified vide Notification No.
SOR(2)62/S & GAD - 79/8181 - 981, dated 15 th November, 200 2, wherein the Rule ( 5 ), relating to method of recruitment , in case of appointment to the post of Additional District & Sessions Judge, 50% quota was reserved for initial recruitment, 40% promotion quota was reserved from amongst the Senior Civil Judges on basis of seniority cum - fitness and 10% quota was allocated for the officers belonging to the Central and Provincial Governments. Similarly for the post of Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 21 District & Sessions Judges 80% posts were reserved for promotion quota, 15% for direct recruitment a nd 5% quota was reserved by transfer from the officers belonging to Central or Provincial Governments.
In view of above scenario, we have sent a query to the Registrar office, so as to d i g out the reason beyond reframing of af o re - referred rules and there fore, we were eagerly anxious to go through the minutes of the meeting, in which the afore cited changes in the afore referred Rules were either discussed or decided, but with our utmost surprise, neither any minutes of meeting a re available on record, nor even the statement of reason s and object s does exist, on basis whereof , the principle of seniority - cum - fitness was inserted in the Rules. It appea r s that the principle of fitness - cum - seniority for promotion against the selection grade was changed without any explicit reason , thus, due to non - availability of the minutes of meeting, in which the subject decision might had taken , coupled with non - availability of statement of reasons and object s amendment made in the afore - referred Rules is of no legal effect, having be en introduced without any lawful authority and against the principles of service Laws and Rules framed thereunder .

The grievance of the appellants is with regard to granting antedated promotions to the respondents , which resulted in appellan ts’ supersession, or they though being granted antedated promotion, but their seniority is /was disturbed by placing junior judicial officers higher in seniority list. For promotion of the officer s either antedated or regular promotion to the selection post, the first criteria is fitness and then seniority. As far as the seniority of the appellants is concerned, there was no dispute with regard to their seniority, who were appointed directly on the recommendation of the BPSC; however, the appellants ’ seniority was interchanged after granting antedated promotions.

14. However, in these appeals antedated promotion granted
to the regular appointees/respondents has also been assailed, on the strength that the regular appointees were also not entitled for promotion for lacking quali fying minimum length of service under the relevant Rules. Be that as it may, but the antedated promotions cannot be considered as an ordinary promotion, but being distinct in nature will have entirely different implication. Although the promotion granted u nder the prevailing Rules, is stipulating minimum length of service for promotion in next grade. But this tribunal’s judgment while granting the relief to the respondents, was upheld by the Hon’ble Supreme Court of Pakistan, which under Articles 189 & 201 of the Constitution is binding upon all organs of the State. Thus the promotion granted on the strength of judgment of the court, will have a force of law and any condition stipulated under the procedural Rule will have no application on the cases of Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 24 anted ated promoted judicial officers. Thus, this contention being misconceived is also not sustainable.
The appe l lants in these appeals are judicial officers, and therefore, are supposed to be well cognizant of legal position and are expected to act prudently, justly and fairly being part of judicial service, but , they did not give up their endeavors , when despite declaration of Hon’ble Apex Court, once again the seniority of regular appointees has been challenged, which amounts to challenge the judgment of thi s tribunal again before the same tribunal and relief has been sought against the judgment of the Hon’ble Supreme Court . This tendency developed by the appellants being judicial officers is highly disapproved and we despite being dismayed do not impos e any fine , however, while showing our displeasure on the appellants’ behavior for not accepting the verdict of competent court of law , is absolutely im proper and unfortunate, at least to say. Thus, these appeals being misconceived and frivolous are not maintainable.
1 5 . In Judicial Service Appeal Nos. 10 & 11 of 2020, the appellants Rahim Dad Khilji and Abdul Ali Jalalzai in addition to assailing the impugned Notification upto the extent of their supersession , have also claimed for payment of back benefits on t he strength of their promotion from Senior Civil Judge to Additional District & Sessions Judges. It is worthwhile to mention here that in the impugned Notification through which the appellants were promoted, it was mentioned in clear terms that ‘ the office rs granted antedated promotions would not be entitled to claim any back benefit ’ . However, Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 25 though it is by now well settled that the officer who has been restrained or refrained to perform in a higher position, on getting antedated promotion would also be entitled to get back benefits, but this principle has been laid down in a peculiar circumstances of each case, particularly, when a a ffected judicial officer was either not gainfully employed anywhere else or remained jobless, or having been remained out o f service, for no fault of officer concern . But in the appellants’ case , though they were juniors but were still performing duties according to their respective grades and thus neither remained unemployed or jobless nor question of their seniority was deci ded yet.
Similarly, the higher post on which the appellants have been promote d now, were neither vacant during the entire period , but were manned by others and those incumbents working on the higher posts had been paid emoluments of those positions respec tively held by them . Thus, the normal rule of law “ No work , no pay ” would be applicable in the appellants’ cases. Another aspect which must be kept in mind that when the higher positions were manned by other officers, they were also being paid their respec tive emoluments according to their grade, and thus, the posts were not vacant so as to presume that deprivation of appellants for any reason has infact saved the revenue and the public exchequer was parked in surplus. While the appellants have never served or worked on the higher positions, thus, granting them back benefits would not only cause losses to the public exchequer , but the taxpayer would be penalized indirectly , who in that case would share the burden of these back benefits on two counts, firstly the emoluments paid to the officers already worked on the higher positions and last but Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 26 not the least, the appellants would also get benefit of a work which they have never performed . Needless to add here that on this principle a service judicial appeal No. 06 of 201 7 of Mr. Tahir Hamayun , whereby the claim of back benefit was turned down, who is also another antedated promoted officer/District & Sessions Judge , but his appeal for these added reasons has already been dismissed , vide this Tribunal’s judgme nt dated 30 th June 2020 ,therefore, following the principle of equity, which stipulates that “ alike shall be treated alike” , and for the afore - discussed added reasons, the appellants are also not entitled for any back benefit.
1 6 . A point to ponder before us was a criterion followed by the promotion committee at the time of granting antedated promotions to the respondents and superseding the appellants. Though the minutes of meeting of the promotion committee dated 09 th November 2016, contain the fact that the personal file of each judicial officer was perused and on scrutinizing their judicial record and the judgments rendered by the m , the respondents were found fit for antedated promotions, whereas the appellants’ performance was not found satisfactory, th us their cases were deferred. Admittedly, the fitness of a civil servant to hold a 'next higher post depends upon his performance which he had been showing during the period prescribed for promotion to next grade and it is to be determined on the basis of material placed before competent authority including Annual Confidential Reports etc.
The performance of a judicial officer is to be evaluated on quantifying the marks secured by him as per the in vogue formula, on perusing the judgments delivered by him, his skills of writing judgments, his legal Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 27 approach. When a question of supersession has been raised on the strength of arguments that he has been superseded in violation of the Promotion Policy or in violation of the judgment rendered by the tribunal decl aring him/them senior to those appointed on ad - hoc basis, this Tribunal can examine the question of their fitness. Eligibility for promotion and fitness , there are two separate criteria s, which are judicially recognized in a number of decisions viz ‘ Muham mad Anis and others v. Abdul Haseeb and others’ ( PLD 1994 SC 539 ).
Eligibility relates primarily to the terms and conditions of service and their applicability to the concerned civil servants, the question of fitness is a subjective evaluation on the basis of objective criteria and hence is not justiciable. However having observed as much it would also be seen that the discretion so given to the promotion committee in the matter of fitness of a judicial officer for promotion, has to be exercised in a fair, open and just manner which should be based on reasonable assessment of the concerned judicial officer’s performance at judicial side, especially when he is going to be considered for the next higher post, his judicial record viz judgments so delivered, conduct in judicial and official work, behavior with superiors, litigants, Advocates and staff is to be kept in sight, whereas most of these requirements are also mentioned in the Annual Confidential Report of the judicial officer.
1 7 . Albeit in case of pr omotion of any judicial officer, when his performance is found satisfactory and the judicial officer is found fit, in such case, the reasons for promoting an officer might not be as much necessary, except in a case where the judicial officer(s) is/ar e Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 28 superseded or deferred, in such case , it would be the requirement and legal duty to assess the material of each judicial officer individually and thereafter comparatively with the one, who has been considered and recommended for promotion. The perception for giving reason in case of superseding is that the entire process is done with due care and caution on assessment of the entire service record and no tyranny is done to anyone. One’s fitness cannot be adjudged, unless the basic ingredients for promotion viz efficiency, performance, quantification, integrity and professional output are evaluated or scrutinized. The term 'fitness' includes all the qualities of an employee such like academic qualification as distinction in education matters, integrity, devotion of duty and the manner in which a person discharges his duties, beside s determining some other factors including the punctuality in work, the work done by him, the manner and behaviour of such officer with superior and subordinate and with general pub lic, have to be considered. The seniority may be considered as one of the factors for determination of merit and if all other qualities are equal then seniority may be a deci sive factor of merit.
1 8 . In the case in hand, on perusal of the minutes of meeting and the record , it is noted that on evaluating the judicial performance and scrutinizing the appellants’ personal files, reasons might have been recorded separately in case of each superseded officer, but these reasons were not included in the minutes of the promotion committee ’s meeting , showing that they were either unfit or their performance was not satisfactory to grant them antedated promotion as given to the respondents and this missing aspect of the case has infact can be termed Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 29 as main grievance of the appellants . Although the promotion is not a vested right of a civil servant, however, each deserving and eligible candidate is to be considered for promotion and the promotion committee has to evaluate his fitness for the promoted post as held by t he Hon’ble Supreme Court in case of ‘ Muhammad Rahim Khan v. The Chief Secretary, N. - W.F.P. and 4 others’ ( 1999 SCMR 1605 ) , and it is instructive to reproduce the relevant passage therefrom, which stipulates as under : - "However, even in the matter involving fitness to be appointed or promoted to a particular post or grade there has to be necessary material on the basis of which an opinion, one way or the other, is to be formed. If, therefore, either all the necessary material is not put up before the Authori ty deliberating upon the matter of appointment or promotion or obviously misleading material is put up or manifest acts of commission or omission, as regards vital data, are involved the subjective exercise may not qualify as such and may irretrievably be conditioned by objective factors, wanting in due process. Such aspects, probably, would be more akin to consideration of eligibility than of fitness and all things being equal, be opened for scrutiny before a legal forum. In the instant proceedings, the ob jective factors were the working paper etc. and the recommendations of the Board. On such material, another had to determine the fitness and while such determination may be beyond judicial scrutiny, the necessary steps leading to the same i.e. the objectiv e factors may not always be so, see, inter alia, Muhammad Anwar v. Secretary, Establishment Division, PLD 1992 SC 144, Federation of Pakistan v.
Muhammad Qaiser Hayat Khan, 1994 SCMR 544, Walayat Ali Mir. v. Pakistan International Airlines 1995 Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 30 SCMR 650, S ecretary, Narcotics Control Division v.
Muhammad Sajjad, 1997 PLC (C.S.) 167, Pakistan Broadcasting Corporation v. Nasiruddin 1997 PLC (C.S.) 931, S.T. Rehman v. Government of Pakistan,
1997 PLC (C.S.) 1207."
Admittedly, the appellants were eligible for t he promotion in view of the Tribunal’s judgment , but it is also a settled principle that mere eligibility does not qualify a civil servant for the promotion, as the next criteria for the promotion is fitness. But as stated supra, the fitness of a candidate is to be adjudged from his personal record of service on assessing each and every aspect, and thereby, there must be reason, in case he/she is not found fit for promotion. For promotion to the higher post, especially when it is a selection post, the entr ies under "quality and output of work" and "integrity" in all the ACRs recorded during his service as an officer are be quantified. Furthermore the quantification of the "quality and output of work" and "integrity", are a crucial factor in determining comp arative merit of the officers for promotion to the selection post. The significance of the service record as a source/basis of the above evaluation/quantification was so great and crucial.
1 9 . With regard to the contention of the learned counsel that by means of granting antedated promotion to the respondents in view of the Tribunal’s judgment through impugned Notification dated 27 th March 2017, they have been superseded and their right have been infringed, a s can be seen from the foregoing, though all the officers declared to be senior to those ad - hoc appointees by means of referred to judgment have been considered for promotion on evaluating their performance, personal record and on perusing their personal file s , but Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 31 the appellants in these appeals have been either superseded in promotion or in seniority, but since the reasons , if so recorded have not been included or made part of the minutes of the meeting of the Promotion Committee , for ignoring the quantification in the service record, nor we could fin d anything adverse against the appellants from their personal file s showing that either they were incompetent in their judicial work or their performance, behavior, integrity and punctuality a ffecting their fitness for promotion w as either pointed out in t heir record or any adverse observation at administrative and judicial side were stated to comprehend for overriding the evaluation on the basis of the service dossier of the officer covering the entire spectrum of their performance and conduct, spread over long years of their service, which could suggest their supersession. Supersession of any officer without recording any reason for such supersession amounts to not only violation of the requirement of adequate disclosure, but also to offend the principle o f fairness, due process and procedural propriety.
20 . The promotion committee might have well scrutinized the personal dossier of each judicial officer and have tried to conduct the process in reasonable manner to eradicate any chance of arbitrariness, a mbiguity and a whimsical approach, instead of placing reliance on undefined personal opinion, but since the law of proprietary demands that the process conducted by the promotion committee must appear to have been done in a reasonable and justifiable manne r, therefore, it would have been of much credence, if the minutes of meeting would have flowed the fact that the dossier of each judicial officer was Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 32 scrutinized individually and thereafter comparatively , with the dossier of other judicial officers.
21 . T hrough the instant appeals the question of seniority was also raised by the appellants that their seniority was disturbed. It is also settled principle of law that "seniority" in the grade to which a civil servant is promoted is to take effect from the dat e of regular appointment to a post in the grade. It is also settled principle of law qua the question of conferring seniority with retrospective effect that cannot be done unless such right was established. Reliance is placed on “ Director General Intellige nce Bureau, I s lamabad and others v Amir Mujahid Khan and others” ( 2011 SCMR 389). As far as the contention s of the appellants Nasir Khan Yousafzai, Nazir Ahmed Khajak and Zafarullah Bazai are concerned , that they were senior to the judicial officers who we re granted antedated promotion to the post of District & Sessions Judge . It is an admitted fact that the appellants were appointed prior to the Tribunal’s judgment dated 25 th April 2016 followed by issuance of the impugned Notification dated 27 th March 201 7, but the antedated promotion was granted to the respondents w.e.f 15 th May 2015, just four (4) days prior to the appointment of the appellants, and they have been declared and placed junior to the promoted judicial officers. The appellants were appointed on 19 th May 2015, by the High Court of Balochistan after due process of law and they are performing their jobs since then, whereas the respondents (newly promoted District & Sessions Judges) have been granted antedated promotion , vide Notification dated 2 7 th March 2017 but w.e.f 15 th May 2015 .
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 33 It would be apt to observe here that in the case of seniority of the appellants of afore - referred appeals, and to consider the question, which involves their seniority, these cases can be classified with three cate gories. The first category was of those officers, who were granted antedated promotions, second category was, who were directly appointed before granting antedated promotions to other officers and the third category was of the officers who being ad - hoc app ointees were declared junior to the directly and regularly appointed officers .
2 2 . In the comparison criterion of the afore - mentioned three categories the provision of Civil Servant (seniority) Rules 1993 and Balochistan Civil Servant (Seniority) Rules 2 008 become applicable , which are absolutely analogues in nature to each other and both Rules carry equitable provisions . While the Section ( 8 ) of Civil Servant Act 1973 is also relevant, which stipulates a criterion of seniority and its sub - section (4) pro vides “ seniority in a post, service or cadre to which a civil serv a nt is promoted shall take effect from the date of regular appointment to that post” while Rule ( 6 ) of Rules 1973 , stipulates that departmental promotees shall always regarded senior to dire ct recruites of same year.
Admittedly, neither the appellants and antedated promoted officers were appointees and promotees of same year, nor the appellants who were appointed on 19 th May 2015 against the regular posts , were party in the service appeal N o. 01 of 2002 . The Tribunal’s judgment though has also granted benefit to the non - appealing judicial officers, but this prin ciple cannot be extended in case of the appellants Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 34 of instant appeals. Similarly, the Tribunal’s judgment was announced on 25 th Apri l 2016, after about one year of appointment of the appellants, while antedated promotions were granted vide Notification dated 27 th March 2017 , thus at the cost of repetition, it is reiterated that “ seniority in grade to which office r is promoted is to ta ke effect from the date of regular appointment to a post in the grade ” . Meaning thereby that the appellants were entitled to acquire seniority from the date of their regular appointment, while the antedated promoted officers would become entitled to acquir e the seniority from the date of their regular appointment . However, only the cases of promoted officers was considered retrospectively for antedated promotions, but the Tribunal’s judgment was not retrospectively applicable on the appellants’ seniority. T hus, for the aforesaid reasons the impugned seniority list, whereby the appellants were declared junior to the antedated promoted officers was also not sustainable.
2 3 . Before parting with this judgment, we are cognizant of the fact that the irregularitie s or for that matter, anomalies emerged in the service matters of the judicial officers of this court have been surfaced, and t h is tribulation was mainly exposed for certain obvious reasons .
Such as, in the backdrop of promulgation of Presidents’ Order No. 01 of 1970 (“ P.O - 1 of 1970 ” ) , the Province of West of Pakistan was dissolved on 30 th March 1970 , wh ereby its Article 14 stipulated as under:
“High Court. - (1)There shall be established a High Court for each of the new Provinces consisting of the Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 35 Chief Ju stice and such other Judges as the President may appoint:
Provided that the Provincial Government of two or more Provinces (herein referred to as a “group”) may agree that either: -
(a) There should be a common High Court for
the group; or
(b) That the High Court of one of the Provinces
in the group shall be the High Court for all the Provinces in the group, and High Court for all the Provinces in the group, and The President may, on a request being made in this behalf, if he thinks fit, make an order accordingl y.
(2) . …….
The Presidents’ Order No. 08 of 1970 (“ P.O - 8 of 1970 ”) was notified on 16 th June 1970 by ordering the establishment of Provincial High Court s in pursuance of Article 14 of P.O - I of 1970 for establishment of High Courts for new provinces, the c lause - 3 (c) established “ a High Court for Provinces of Balochistan and Sindh to be called the Sindh and Balochistan High Court with its principle seat at Karachi ” . The P.O - 6 of 1976 (“ P.O - 6 of 1976 ”), namely , Balochistan and Sind (High Courts) Order 1976 d eclared the establishment of two separate High Courts by virtue of Clause (2) of Article 192 of the Constitution . Whereas, subject to Article 270 (1) of the Constitution of Islamic Republic of Pakistan 1973, while extending validation to certain laws state s as follows:
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 36 “ 270. Temporary v alidation of certain laws, etc.
{(1) Majlis - e - Shoora (Parliament)} may by law made in the manner prescribed for legislations for a matter in Part 1 of the Federal Legislative List validate all Proclamations, President’s Orde rs, Martial Law Regulations, Martial Law Orders and other laws made between the twenty - fifth day March, one thousand nine hundred and sixty nine and the nineteenth day of December, one thousand nine hundred and seventy - one (both days inclusive).
Thus, in view of afore - quoted validation stipulated in Article 2 70 of the Constitution , the High Court of Balochistan was established by the President of Pakistan by virtue of Clause (2) of Article 192 of the Constitution and despite mandate of Constitution no sep arate enactment was promulgated for establishment of High Court of Balochistan, while the referred to P.O - 6 of 1976 was/is silent about conferring any powers to the High Court for framing the Rules for regulating its ordinary businesses and functions . Howe ver , the provision s of Article 202 , 203 & 208 of the Constitution defines powers of High Court , which for the ease of reference and being relevant are reproduced here under:
“202. Rules of Procedure . Subject to the Constitution and law, a High Court may ma ke rules regulating the practice and procedure to the Court or of any Court subordinate to it.
203. High Court to Superintendent subordinate
Courts. Each High Court shall supervise all courts subordinate to it.
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 37
208. Officers and servants of Courts . The Sup reme
Court [and the Federal Shariat Court], with the approval of the President and a High Court, with the approval of the Governor concerned, may make rules providing for the appointment by the Court of officers and servants of the Court and for their term s and conditions of employment.
With great concern , it is painfully observed here that though initially by virtue of P.O - 8 of 1970, named as, High Courts (Establishment) Order, 1970 by virtue of Clause (1) of Article 14 of P.O - 1 of 1970 “ a High Court for the Provinces of Balochistan and Sind to be called the Sind and Balochistan High Court with its principle seat at Karachi ” was established, and by virtue P.O - 6 197 6 the common High Court of the two Provinces was ceased to function as a common High Court , but unfortunately, neither the High Court of Balochistan framed its own Administrative, Establishment and Procedural Rules, nor adopted the already framed Rules of the High Court of Sind. Thus, since establishment of High Court of Balochistan w.e.f. 29 th November 1976, was/is being regu lated without any set Rules, by - Rules and necessary Notifications. To our utmost surprise, it has been revealed that due to non - framing and non - availability of any relevant Rules, the High Court was being run on basis of Ru les framed by the other High Courts. Thus, wherever, it was felt convenient, either the Rules framed by the Lahore High Court or by the High Court of Sind were being followed, but that too without any proper Notification of adoption or adaption of the Rul es of any of the High Court(s).
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 38 2 4 . In view of above narrated facts followed by a recurring scenario of dilemma, it was high time when it acutely required to frame its own Administrative, Establishment and Procedural Rules .
Therefore, on recommendation of the Judges Committee of the High Court, the High Court Establishment (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules 2020 were framed and after the approval of the Hon’ble Governor Balochistan , have been notified vide Notification No.
GAZ.01/Rules/Admn date d 10 th February, 2020 .
Similarly, in order to streamline the Rules of Procedure and to supervise and control all the courts subordinate to it a proposed draft bill of Balochistan District Judiciary Act, 2020 has also been forwarded to the concerned gover nment for its onward placement before the Provincial Assembly of Balochistan for enactment . Thus, after approval of the provincial assembly and receiving the assent of the Hon’ble Governor , followed by issuance of necessary Notification , the required servi ce Rules of District Judiciary and the sub - ordinate staff of the District Judiciary will also be framed and notified in due course. The above exercise after completion will enable the High Court of Balochistan to regulate its business on the strength of the legislative instruments and Rules to be framed thereunder .
25. Again, reverting to the fate of these pending appeals, since
we being the members of this Tribunal, and being integral part of Administration of the High Court of Balochistan are well aware about afore - narrated anomalies created during the afflux of time for which no one can be held responsible in his/her individual capacity. Similarly, in Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 39 case of completely setting aside the impugned Notification or impugned seniority list, would also create an absurd situation, which will ultimately lead to an endless chaos, and would further create an uncertain state of confusion and dilemma. Therefore, for these obvious reasons, we , while without setting aside the impugned Notification No.
1207/120 - Estt: d ated 27 th March 2017 and the impugned seniority list , hereby declare as under:
i. This Tribunal’s judgment dated 25 th April 2016 passed in Service Judicial Appeal No.01 of 2002 , being re m in nature, shall be implemented in letter and spirit.
ii. S er vice Judicial Appeal Nos. 02 & 03 of 2017, respectively filed by the appellants viz Bas h ir Ahmed Badini, Muhammad Jamshed and Nouroz Khan Hoth are dismissed being frivolous and misconceived.
iii. Service Judicial Appeal Nos. 10 & 11 of 2020, respectively filed by the appell ants , Rahim Dad Khilji and Abdul Ali Jalalzai are partly dismissed upto the extent of claim for back benefits. However, upto the extent of supersession are partly accepted and remanded for de novo consideration by the Promotion Committee.
iv. Service Judicial Appeal Nos.0 1 , 0 4 , 0 5 , 09 & 10 of 2017 and 09 of 2020 filed by the appellants , Abdul Hafeez , Inayatullah, Najeebullah , and Muhammad Afzal are partly accepted and their cases are remanded back to the Promotion Committee for de novo consideration.
Service Appeal No s . 01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 09 & 10 of 2017, 07, 09 & 10 of 2019, 09, 10 & 11 of 2020 . 40 v. The servic e appeal Nos. 07, 09 & 10 of 2019 field by the appellants, Nasir Khan Yousafzai, Nazir Ahmed Khajak and Zafarullah Bazai are accepted.
vi. Till final decision on this declaration, the Judicial Officers irrespective of their grade, seniority on basis of already granted antedated promotions, supersession of the a ffected judicial officers, shall neither be changed, nor should any representation either pending or already filed be decided.
These appeals, are therefore, disposed of in the above terms.
Quetta.
Anno unced in open Court: Member - I th November 2020.
Member - II
