chunks.text:
WING: FIA Anti-Human Trafficking. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
SUBSTANCE: investigates offences under the Prevention of Trafficking in Persons Act, 2018 and the
Emigration Ordinance, 1979 — human trafficking, migrant smuggling, illegal recruitment of
workers for overseas employment, forged travel documents; complaints can be made at FIA
anti-human-trafficking circles/zones.
SOURCE: PACHTO 2018; Emigration Ordinance 1979. VERIFICATION: verified as to the framework.

chunks.title: Federal Investigation Agency Act, 1974 — Jurisdiction, Complaint Procedure, Cyber & Trafficking
chunks.chunkTitle: LIMITS: FIA powers are investigation powers, not adjudication; trials take place in courts.
chunks.text:
LIMITS: FIA powers are investigation powers, not adjudication; trials take place in courts.
FIA cannot register provincial offences; do not advise FIA complaints for ordinary police
matters. FIA jurisdictional notifications change — verify the current Schedule.

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: Administrative law governs how public authorities and civil servants must act, and what a
chunks.text:
Administrative law governs how public authorities and civil servants must act, and what a
citizen can do when an authority acts unlawfully. The two strands are: (1) service law (terms
of employment and discipline of civil servants) and (2) judicial review (courts checking
administrative decisions for legality under the Constitution).

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Civil Servants Act, 1973. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
LAW: Civil Servants Act, 1973. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY PROVISIONS (summary of the operative framework):
- Applies to civil servants in federal service (provincial civil servants are governed by
  provincial civil servants acts modelled on the same scheme).
- Terms and conditions: appointment, probation, seniority, promotion, transfer and posting are
  regulated under the Act and rules.
- Termination of service: termination, removal from service and compulsory retirement are
  distinct penalties with different legal consequences; removal from service imposed after
  departmental proceedings is a major penalty.
- Grounds of dismissal: misconduct and inefficiency are dealt with under the Efficiency and
  Discipline Rules.
SOURCE: Civil Servants Act, 1973. VERIFICATION: verified as to framework.

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 (and provincial equivalents).
chunks.text:
LAW: Government Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 (and provincial equivalents).
COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY PROVISIONS (summary):
- Show-cause notice: before imposing a major penalty (reduction to lower post, removal,
  dismissal), the authority must issue a show-cause notice stating the charges and the basis
  of the charge and give a reasonable opportunity to reply.
- Inquiry: where the reply is unsatisfactory, a factual inquiry may be conducted; the accused
  officer can defend, produce evidence and cross-examine (subject to the rules).
- Penalties: minor (censure, withholding of promotion) and major (reduction, removal, dismissal).
- Appeal/review: orders are appealable to the appellate authority under the rules.
SOURCE: E&D Rules, 1973. VERIFICATION: verified as to the show-cause/inquiry/appeal structure.

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Service Tribunals Act, 1973 (Federal Service Tribunal; provincial service tribunals).
chunks.text:
LAW: Service Tribunals Act, 1973 (Federal Service Tribunal; provincial service tribunals).
COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY PROVISIONS (summary):
- The Federal Service Tribunal hears appeals of federal civil servants against departmental
  orders (dismissal, removal, reduction etc.); provincial tribunals for provincial servants.
- Aggrieved civil servants must exhaust the departmental appeal before the Tribunal where
  required, then appeal to the Tribunal within the limitation period.
- Tribunal decisions are final subject to the Supreme Court's jurisdiction; the High Court's
  jurisdiction over service matters is barred by the Act, leaving the Supreme Court as the
  superior forum.
SOURCE: Service Tribunals Act, 1973. VERIFICATION: verified as to framework.

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Constitution of Pakistan, Article 199 (High Courts) and Article 184(3) (Supreme Court
chunks.text:
LAW: Constitution of Pakistan, Article 199 (High Courts) and Article 184(3) (Supreme Court
original jurisdiction). COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY PROVISIONS (close paraphrase):
- The High Court may, on application of an aggrieved person, direct a person performing
  functions in connection with the affairs of the Federation, a Province or a local authority
  to refrain from doing an act not permitted by law, or to do an act required by law, or declare
  an act done without lawful authority void — the constitutional writ jurisdiction
  (mandamus, prohibition, certiorari, quo warranto and habeas corpus).
- Habeas corpus: for release of a person illegally detained.
- Grounds of review include: lack of jurisdiction, error of law apparent on the record, breach
  of natural justice (audi alteram partem — right to be heard; rule against bias), and mala
  fides (bad faith).
SOURCE: Constitution of Pakistan, Article 199. VERIFICATION: verified (writ framework is
well-established; see the rights-corpus for the fundamental-rights provisions).

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: PRINCIPLES (summary of the settled position in Pakistani administrative law):
chunks.text:
PRINCIPLES (summary of the settled position in Pakistani administrative law):
- Audi alteram partem: no person may be condemned unheard; before an order adverse to a person
  (removal from service, cancellation of licence, blacklisting), that person must be given
  notice and an opportunity to be heard.
- Rule against bias: a decision-maker with a personal interest in the matter must not decide it
  (nemo judex in causa sua).
- Reasoned orders: administrative orders affecting rights should state reasons where required.
- These principles are judicially recognized; breach makes the order liable to be set aside in
  writ jurisdiction.
SOURCE: settled case law. VERIFICATION: verified as settled principles.

chunks.title: Administrative Law & Public Service — Civil Servants Act 1973, E&D Rules, Service Tribunals, Judicial Review
chunks.chunkTitle: CITIZEN REMEDY ROUTES (summary):
chunks.text:
CITIZEN REMEDY ROUTES (summary):
- Departmental complaint: written complaint to the head of the department/authority first.
- Ombudsman: Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib) for maladministration in federal agencies;
  provincial ombudsmen for provincial agencies (see civic-services records).
- Writ petition: where the administrative action is unlawful, a constitutional petition to the
  High Court (Article 199) or a civil suit where a private right is affected.
- Regulatory complaints: sector regulators (DRAP, healthcare commissions, food authorities,
  PTA, NEPRA, OGRA etc.) for sector-specific grievances.
SOURCE: Constitution and ombudsman legislation. VERIFICATION: verified as to routes.

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: A tort is a civil wrong (not a breach of contract or trust) for which the law provides damages.
chunks.text:
A tort is a civil wrong (not a breach of contract or trust) for which the law provides damages.
Pakistani courts apply the common-law tort framework as modified by statute (defamation) and by
the Constitution (fundamental rights can support claims against the State). Tort claims are
brought in civil courts; criminal remedies (e.g., criminal defamation under the PPC) are
separate.

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Defamation Ordinance, 2002 (civil defamation); Pakistan Penal Code, Section 499-501
chunks.text:
LAW: Defamation Ordinance, 2002 (civil defamation); Pakistan Penal Code, Section 499-501
(criminal defamation). COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY PROVISIONS (summary):
- Defamation is publication of a false statement that injures a person's reputation.
- Civil: under the Defamation Ordinance 2002, an aggrieved person may sue for damages; defences
  include truth (justification), fair comment on a matter of public interest, and privilege
  (absolute for judicial/parliamentary proceedings; qualified for fair and accurate reports).
- Criminal: PPC Section 499 defines defamation; Section 500 prescribes punishment (imprisonment
  up to two years or fine or both — check the current text for the exact range); defences in
  Section 499's explanations (truth for public good, fair comment, etc.).
- Defamation through electronic systems is also punishable under PECA 2016 (online defamation).
SOURCE: Defamation Ordinance, 2002; PPC ss.499-501; PECA 2016. VERIFICATION: verified as to the
framework (exact penalty text should be checked against the current statute).

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: common-law negligence as applied in Pakistan. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
LAW: common-law negligence as applied in Pakistan. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
ELEMENTS (summary of the settled test):
- Duty of care: the defendant owed the plaintiff a duty to take reasonable care (the
  neighbour principle — persons so closely affected by one's acts that one ought reasonably to
  have them in contemplation).
- Breach: the defendant's conduct fell below the standard of a reasonable person in the
  circumstances (professional negligence judged by professional standards).
- Causation: the breach caused the plaintiff's loss (cause-in-fact and proximate cause).
- Damage: the plaintiff suffered recoverable loss (personal injury, property damage, economic
  loss in recognized cases).
- Medical negligence: judged by the standard of the ordinary skilled practitioner of the
  relevant specialty (Bolam-type standard as applied in Pakistan), and also actionable before
  healthcare commissions as establishment-level negligence.
SOURCE: settled case law. VERIFICATION: verified as settled principles.

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: common law. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
chunks.text:
LAW: common law. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
- Private nuisance: substantial and unreasonable interference with a person's use or enjoyment
  of land (noise, fumes, encroaching structures, blocked passages); remedies: injunction
  and/or damages. Public nuisance affects the public at large and is also a PPC offence
  (Section 268).
- Trespass to land: unauthorized entry on another's land; trespass to goods: unauthorized
  interference with goods. Remedies: damages, injunction, recovery of possession.
SOURCE: common law; PPC s.268. VERIFICATION: verified as settled principles.

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: common law. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
chunks.text:
LAW: common law. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
ELEMENTS (summary): the defendant prosecuted the plaintiff without reasonable and probable
cause, actuated by malice, and the prosecution ended in the plaintiff's favour (acquittal or
discharge), causing damage. Applies to criminal proceedings; suits for malicious prosecution
must plead and prove these elements.
SOURCE: settled case law. VERIFICATION: verified as settled principles.

chunks.title: Law of Torts — Defamation, Negligence, Nuisance/Trespass, Malicious Prosecution, Damages
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: common-law damages; Limitation Act, 1908. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
chunks.text:
LAW: common-law damages; Limitation Act, 1908. COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
- Damages: compensatory (to put the plaintiff in the position before the wrong) and, in
  exceptional cases, exemplary/punitive damages; aggravated damages for injury to feelings in
  defamation.
- Limitation: tort suits (defamation, negligence etc.) are barred after the limitation period
  applicable to the wrong under the Limitation Act, 1908 (defamation suits are subject to a
  short limitation period — check the current Schedule); delay can defeat an otherwise valid
  claim.
SOURCE: Limitation Act, 1908. VERIFICATION: verified as to the general framework (exact periods
for each tort should be checked against the Schedule).

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Birth registration (CRC/Form-B basis)
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Birth registration (CRC/Form-B basis)
WHO: Union Council / local government office (and NADRA for the Child Registration
Certificate after registration).
WHERE: union council of the child's area; NADRA centres for CRC (Form-B).
DOCUMENTS: birth certificate/hospital record or affidavit of witnesses, parents' CNICs,
parent nikahnama (where required).
STEPS: (1) obtain the birth report/hospital slip; (2) submit at the union council within the
prescribed period with parents' identity; (3) receive the union council birth certificate;
(4) apply to NADRA for the CRC (B-Form) using the certificate.
FEES: union council registration fee NOT VERIFIED (local by-laws); NADRA CRC fee per the
current NADRA schedule.
TIME: union council registration usually days; CRC per NADRA's current processing time.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: for refusal/delay, complaint to the secretary union council / district
administration, then the provincial local government department or ombudsman.
SOURCE: local government registration framework; NADRA CRC procedure.
VERIFICATION: metadata-verified (steps well-established; fees/time vary).

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Death registration and death certificate
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Death registration and death certificate
WHO: Union Council / local government office (death registration); NADRA for cancellation
of CNIC of the deceased and death certificate where issued.
WHERE: union council of the area of death/residence.
DOCUMENTS: medical cause-of-death certificate (hospital) or witnesses' affidavits, CNIC of
the deceased and of the informant, graveyard/burial proof where required.
STEPS: (1) obtain medical certificate or witnesses; (2) register the death at the union
council; (3) obtain the death certificate; (4) notify NADRA for CNIC cancellation and
succession documentation.
FEES: NOT VERIFIED (local by-laws).
APPEAL/ESCALATION: complaint to the district administration / local government department.
SOURCE: local government registration framework. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Marriage registration (nikahnama) and NADRA marriage record
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Marriage registration (nikahnama) and NADRA marriage record
WHO: nikah registrar (union council) for the nikahnama; NADRA for updating the family record.
WHERE: union council of the bride's area (registrar's jurisdiction) and NADRA centres.
DOCUMENTS: CNICs of bride, groom and witnesses, and any documents the registrar requires
(guardians' CNICs where applicable).
STEPS: (1) nikah performed; (2) nikahnama registered with the nikah registrar (union
council) with prescribed fee stamps where required; (3) obtain the registered nikahnama
copy; (4) optionally update NADRA family records (CRC of children later uses it).
FEES: nikah registration fee per the local government schedule (NOT VERIFIED here).
APPEAL/ESCALATION: disputes over registration to the union council secretary / local
government department; failure to register is an offence under the Muslim Family Laws
Ordinance, 1961 framework.
SOURCE: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance, 1961; union council registration practice.
VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Domicile certificate
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Domicile certificate
WHO: Deputy Commissioner / district administration.
WHERE: DC office of the district of residence.
DOCUMENTS: CNIC (and family members' where required), proof of residence (utility bill,
rent agreement, property documents), educational certificates where applying on
education/profession basis, passport-size photographs, affidavit where required.
STEPS: (1) fill the prescribed domicile application; (2) attach proofs; (3) submit at the
DC office (or online where the district portal exists); (4) verification by the local
police/revenue staff; (5) collect the domicile certificate.
FEES: nominal provincial fee (NOT VERIFIED here).
TIME: usually weeks (verification-dependent).
APPEAL/ESCALATION: for refusal/delay, complaint to the Commissioner's office, then the
provincial home/services department; courts can be approached where the refusal is unlawful.
SOURCE: provincial domicile rules. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Police complaint for non-cognizable matters and police misconduct
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Police complaint for non-cognizable matters and police misconduct
WHO: SHO (police station) for complaints; complaint cells for misconduct.
WHERE: local police station; district SP/DSP complaint cell; police complaint authorities
(e.g., Police Complaints Authority where established); online portals where available.
DOCUMENTS: written complaint with facts, dates, witnesses, evidence, CNIC copy.
STEPS: (1) submit written complaint at the station (receipt obtained); (2) if not
entertained for a cognizable offence, demand FIR registration (CrPC s.154) and escalate
under s.22-A/22-B; (3) for police misconduct, complaint to the district complaint cell
or provincial complaint authority; (4) judicial remedy (writ, private complaint under
s.200 CrPC) where police refuse.
FEES: none (complaint registration is free).
APPEAL/ESCALATION: SP/DSP complaint cell -> CPO/IG complaint cell -> provincial complaint
authority -> court (s.22-A/22-B application or writ petition).
SOURCE: CrPC 1898 ss.154, 22-A, 22-B, 200; Police Order 2002 complaint provisions.
VERIFICATION: verified as to the legal routes.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Complaint against a government department (service delivery failure)
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Complaint against a government department (service delivery failure)
WHO: the department itself, then grievance mechanisms, then the ombudsman.
WHERE: department's complaint cell / Pakistan Citizen's Portal (Prime Minister's
performance delivery portal) / provincial citizens' portals.
DOCUMENTS: written complaint, reference numbers, receipts, evidence of the grievance.
STEPS: (1) complain to the department (keep record); (2) escalate to the department head;
(3) use the Citizen's Portal / provincial portal; (4) file with the Federal Ombudsman
(Wafaqi Mohtasib) or provincial ombudsman for maladministration; (5) writ petition to the
High Court where the action is unlawful.
FEES: none.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: ombudsman -> representation against ombudsman order -> court.
SOURCE: ombudsman legislation (Federal Ombudsman); Citizen's Portal practice.
VERIFICATION: verified as to routes.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Public information requests
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Public information requests
WHO: public bodies under federal/provincial transparency laws (e.g., the federal access
to information framework and provincial RTI acts — Punjab Transparency and Right to
Information Act 2013; Sindh Transparency and Right to Information Act 2016; KP Right to
Information Act 2013; Balochistan equivalent — verify current titles).
WHERE: the public information officer of the relevant body; provincial information
commissions for appeals.
DOCUMENTS: written request describing the information sought.
STEPS: (1) submit the request to the designated officer; (2) the body must respond within
the statutory period (check the applicable act); (3) on refusal/delay, appeal to the
provincial information commission or the designated appellate forum.
FEES: nominal copying fee where applicable.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: information commission -> courts.
SOURCE: federal/provincial right-to-information legislation. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified
(acts exist; exact procedures vary by province).

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Free legal aid
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Free legal aid
WHO: Legal aid authorities (provincial legal aid agencies / district legal empowerment
committees), bar association free-legal-aid cells, and courts' appointed counsel for
indigent accused in criminal cases.
WHERE: district legal aid offices, bar associations, courts (application for state
counsel under CrPC where indigent).
DOCUMENTS: proof of identity, proof of income/indigence, case documents.
STEPS: (1) apply to the legal aid authority/committee with case details; (2) eligibility
determined (indigence, nature of case); (3) lawyer assigned; (4) for accused persons
facing serious charges, courts may provide counsel at state expense.
FEES: free for eligible applicants.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: refusal to the head of the legal aid agency, then the courts.
SOURCE: legal aid legislation and court practice (see legal-aid corpus).
VERIFICATION: verified as to framework.

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Emergency services
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Emergency services
WHO/WHERE: Rescue 1122 (emergency ambulance/fire/rescue — provincial); police emergency
15 (varies by province); Edhi and other voluntary ambulance services; hospital
emergencies.
STEPS: (1) call the emergency number of the province (1122 for rescue; 15 police where
applicable); (2) give location and nature of emergency; (3) for medical emergencies,
hospital emergency departments treat first.
FEES: Rescue 1122 service is free; private ambulance services charge.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: complaints about emergency response to the district administration
or provincial emergency service.
SOURCE: provincial emergency services practice. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified
(numbers/services can change — advise checking the province's current emergency numbers).

chunks.title: Pakistan Civic Services — Citizen Workflows (registration, domicile, complaints, legal aid, emergency)
chunks.chunkTitle: WORKFLOW: Voter enrolment and electoral complaints
chunks.text:
WORKFLOW: Voter enrolment and electoral complaints
WHO: Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) for enrolment; ECP district offices for
complaints; courts (election tribunals) for election disputes.
WHERE: ECP district election office / ECP online services.
DOCUMENTS: CNIC, address proof for registration/transfer of vote.
STEPS: (1) apply for voter enrolment/transfer at the ECP office or online (elections
framework); (2) verification; (3) electoral roll entry; (4) complaints on rolls to the
ECP; (5) election disputes to election tribunals under the Elections Act 2017.
FEES: enrolment free.
APPEAL/ESCALATION: ECP -> election tribunals -> Supreme Court.
SOURCE: Elections Act, 2017. VERIFICATION: verified as to framework.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: A power of attorney (mukhtar-nama) is a written instrument by which one person (the
chunks.text:
A power of attorney (mukhtar-nama) is a written instrument by which one person (the
principal/donor) authorizes another (the attorney/agent) to act on his behalf. Pakistani
law governing POAs: the Powers of Attorney Act, 1882 (definition and general effect), the
Registration Act, 1908 (when registration is compulsory), and the Stamp Act, 1899 (stamp
duty). Requirements below state the settled position; where a figure (stamp duty, fee) is
not verified it is marked NOT VERIFIED.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: TYPES (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882 framework):
chunks.text:
TYPES (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882 framework):
- General POA: authorizes the attorney to do all acts the principal could do, or a wide
  class of acts (property dealings, litigation, banking, representation before offices).
- Special POA: confined to a specific act or matter (e.g., to execute one sale deed, to
  represent in one case, to collect one specific payment).
- Property POA: authorizes dealings with immovable property (sale, purchase, mortgage,
  mutation). Registration considerations apply (see POA_REGISTRATION).
- Overseas POA: executed by a Pakistani abroad for use in Pakistan, or executed in Pakistan
  for use abroad — requires notarization and consular attestation (see POA_OVERSEAS).
SOURCE: Powers of Attorney Act, 1882, Section 2 definition framework. VERIFICATION: verified.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Registration Act, 1908, Sections 17 and 18; settled case law. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
LAW: Registration Act, 1908, Sections 17 and 18; settled case law. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY POSITION (summary):
- A POA that CREATES or ASSIGNS an interest in immovable property, or that empowers the
  attorney to sell, mortgage or otherwise transfer immovable property, requires compulsory
  registration under Section 17 (read with Section 49: an unregistered instrument of that
  class cannot affect immovable property and is inadmissible as evidence of the transaction).
- A POA for general representation (appearing in offices, litigation, filing documents) or
  for acts not transferring immovable property does not require compulsory registration.
- A power coupled with an interest (where the attorney has an interest in the subject
  matter) is irrevocable during that interest.
SOURCE: Registration Act, 1908, ss.17/49; settled case law. VERIFICATION: verified as to the
settled position (the sale/mortgage POA registration requirement is well-established).

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: LAW: Stamp Act, 1899 (Article 48 POA schedule, as amended provincially). COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
chunks.text:
LAW: Stamp Act, 1899 (Article 48 POA schedule, as amended provincially). COVERAGE: SUMMARY.
KEY POSITION: a POA must be stamped with the prescribed stamp duty (general vs special POA
rates differ; provincial amendments vary). Understamped documents cannot be received in
evidence (subject to the penalty/validation procedure). AMOUNT: NOT VERIFIED — check the
current provincial stamp schedule.
SOURCE: Stamp Act, 1899. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: EXECUTION AND ATTESTATION (settled practice):
chunks.text:
EXECUTION AND ATTESTATION (settled practice):
- The principal signs (or thumb-impresses if illiterate) in the presence of witnesses.
- Two witnesses attest the principal's signature/thumb impression; for an illiterate
  principal the thumb impression must be attested with the attestation recording that the
  contents were read over and understood.
- Attestation before a Notary Public (notarized POA) is standard for use in offices, banks
  and abroad.
- For court/pleading POAs (vakalatnama for lawyers) the court rules apply.
SOURCE: settled notarial and stamping practice. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: OVERSEAS POA (Pakistani abroad or foreign POA for use in Pakistan):
chunks.text:
OVERSEAS POA (Pakistani abroad or foreign POA for use in Pakistan):
- Execute before a Notary Public in the country of execution (as per that country's law —
  home-country step).
- Then attestation: the Pakistani Embassy/Consulate in that country attests the notarized
  POA (consular attestation) for use in Pakistan; where the foreign country is a party to
  the Apostille Convention and Pakistan accepts the channel, an apostille may apply —
  verify the current channel with the Pakistani mission.
- After attestation, the POA is submitted/registered in Pakistan where registration is
  required (property POAs).
- Consular use abroad of a POA executed in Pakistan: notarize in Pakistan, then attest from
  the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the foreign mission in Pakistan as required by the
  destination country (destination-country requirement).
SOURCE: MOFA consular attestation practice. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: REVOCATION (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882, Section 201-208 framework):
chunks.text:
REVOCATION (Powers of Attorney Act, 1882, Section 201-208 framework):
- The principal may revoke the POA at any time (unless it is coupled with an interest).
- Revocation by: a revocation deed (registered where the POA was registered), or written
  notice to the attorney, and public notice to persons dealing with the attorney.
- Termination: POA also terminates on the death, insolvency or incapacity of the principal
  (subject to the law), or on completion of the specified act (special POA).
- Until notice of revocation reaches them, third parties who deal with the attorney in good
  faith may be protected.
SOURCE: Powers of Attorney Act, 1882. VERIFICATION: verified as to the framework.

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: DRAFTING STRUCTURE — GENERAL POA (English formal document skeleton):
chunks.text:
DRAFTING STRUCTURE — GENERAL POA (English formal document skeleton):
1. Heading: "GENERAL POWER OF ATTORNEY"
2. Preamble: donor identification — "I, [NAME], son/daughter of [PARENT], holder of CNIC
 [CNIC NUMBER], resident of [ADDRESS], do hereby appoint ..."
3. Attorney identification: "Mr./Ms. [NAME], son/daughter of [PARENT], holder of CNIC
 [CNIC NUMBER], resident of [ADDRESS], as my true and lawful attorney."
4. Scope clause: "to do and execute all or any of the following acts, deeds and things on
 my behalf: (a) to manage, sell, mortgage, lease or otherwise deal with my movable and
 immovable property; (b) to appear, act and represent me before all courts, offices,
 banks and authorities; (c) to sign, execute and register all deeds, documents and
 applications; (d) to receive and recover monies due to me and to give valid receipts;
 (e) to do all other acts incidental or necessary to the above."
5. Ratification clause: "I hereby ratify and confirm all acts lawfully done by my attorney
 in pursuance of this power."
6. Date and place; 7. Signature of the donor; 8. Attestation of two witnesses (name,
 CNIC, signature); 9. Notarial attestation where required.
NOTE: for a SPECIAL POA, replace the scope clause with the single specified act (e.g.,
"to execute the sale deed of property described as ... in favour of ...").
VERIFICATION: drafting structure (not statutory form — adapt to the matter and local
requirements).

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: DRAFTING STRUCTURE — GENERAL POA (Urdu Script formal document skeleton):
chunks.text:
DRAFTING STRUCTURE — GENERAL POA (Urdu Script formal document skeleton):
1. سرخی: "مختار نامہ عام"
2. تمہید: "میں، [نام] ولد [والد کا نام]، شناختی کارڈ نمبر [شناختی کارڈ]، ساکن [پتہ]، بذریعہ
 اس تحریر مقرر کرتا/کرتی ہوں ..."
3. مختار کی شناخت: "جناب [نام] ولد [والد کا نام]، شناختی کارڈ نمبر [شناختی کارڈ]، ساکن
 [پتہ] کو اپنا قانونی مختار مقرر کرتا/کرتی ہوں۔"
4. اختیارات کی شق: "کہ وہ میری طرف سے درج ذیل امور انجام دے: (الف) میری منقولہ و غیر منقولہ
 جائیداد کا انتظام، فروخت، رہن، کرایہ یا دیگر معاملات؛ (ب) تمام عدالتوں، دفاتر، بینکوں اور
 حکام کے سامنے حاضری اور نمائندگی؛ (ج) تمام دستاویزات، درخواستوں اور ہنڈیوں پر دستخط اور
 اندراج؛ (د) میرے واجبات کی وصولی اور رسیدیں دینا؛ (ہ) مذکورہ بالا امور سے متعلق تمام
 ضروری کارروائیاں۔"
5. توثیق کی شق: "میں اپنے مختار کے اس اختیار کے تحت کیے گئے تمام جائز اعمال کی توثیق کرتا/کرتی ہوں۔"
6. تاریخ اور مقام؛ 7. مؤکل کے دستخط؛ 8. دو گواہوں کی تصدیق (نام، شناختی کارڈ، دستخط)؛
 9. ضرورت کے مطابق ناظرِ عام کی تصدیق۔
VERIFICATION: drafting structure (Urdu Script formal document skeleton; adapt wording to the
matter).

chunks.title: Power of Attorney — Law, Registration, Execution & Drafting Structures (English/Urdu Script)
chunks.chunkTitle: LIMITS: stamp-duty figures, exact registration-office fees and consular attestation fees are
chunks.text:
LIMITS: stamp-duty figures, exact registration-office fees and consular attestation fees are

For foreign-law execution requirements (notarization abroad), the destination rules control;

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: PAKISTAN LAW: Foreigners Act, 1946 (as applicable) and the Ministry of Interior's visa and
chunks.text:
PAKISTAN LAW: Foreigners Act, 1946 (as applicable) and the Ministry of Interior's visa and
residence framework. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY FRAMEWORK (summary):
- Entry: foreigners enter on a valid visa (Pakistan Online Visa System) or visa-free
  arrangements; the visa states duration of stay and number of entries.
- Registration: foreigners staying beyond the visa-free period may be required to register
  with the police under the Foreigners Act, 1946 framework (Foreigners Registration
  requirement) — check current MoI practice.
- Residence permit: long-stay foreigners (work/study/business) obtain a Residence Permit
  from the Ministry of Interior; the permit evidences lawful residence and is renewable.
- Pakistan Origin Card (POC): available to foreign nationals of Pakistani origin (including
  former citizens) for visa-free entry and indefinite stay, subject to the POC Rules.
SOURCE: Foreigners Act, 1946; MoI visa/residence practice. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified
(exact current registration and permit procedures change; check MoI's official pages).

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: PAKISTAN LAW: visa extension and re-entry. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
PAKISTAN LAW: visa extension and re-entry. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY FRAMEWORK (summary):
- Extensions: visa extensions are applied to the Ministry of Interior (visa extension
  process) before expiry; overstay without extension is an immigration offence (fine,
  detention and/or deportation exposure).
- Exit/re-entry: a single-entry visa does not permit re-entry; multi-entry visas state the
  re-entry conditions; departure before expiry and re-entry on a fresh visa is the standard
  route; exit permits may be required in specific cases (e.g., where an exit permit is
  endorsed).
- Documentation to carry: passport with valid visa/stamp, residence permit where issued,
  and proof of registration where required.
SOURCE: MoI visa rules. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: PAKISTAN LAW: work, study and business categories under the Online Visa System. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
PAKISTAN LAW: work, study and business categories under the Online Visa System. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY FRAMEWORK (summary):
- Work: a work visa requires a sponsoring Pakistani employer/invitation letter and sectoral
  clearance where required (e.g., Board of Investment recommendation for employment);
  the visa is tied to the employer and period of employment.
- Business: business visas for investors/entrepreneurs with the prescribed invitation and
  documentation; long-stay business activity may require the residence permit route.
- Study: study visas for students enrolled at HEC-recognized institutions, with admission
  letter and, where required, No-Objection Certificate; age/eligibility per the current
  rules.
- Each category has its own document list in the Online Visa System — always use the
  official checklist for the category.
SOURCE: Pakistan Online Visa System categories. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified (category
checklists change; the visa portal is the authoritative source).

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: PAKISTAN LAW: interaction with police and immigration authorities. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
PAKISTAN LAW: interaction with police and immigration authorities. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY FRAMEWORK (summary):
- Routine checks: foreigners may be asked to show passport, visa and registration documents
  by police/immigration officials; carrying the passport or attested copies with the visa
  page is advisable.
- Offences: overstay, breach of visa conditions (unauthorized work on a study visa etc.) and
  entry without valid documents are immigration offences; remedies include fine,
  imprisonment for serious cases, and deportation.
- Arrest/detention: a detained foreigner has the right to legal representation under
  Pakistani law and to consular notification — the foreigner's embassy/consulate is
  contacted (home-country consular channel, not a Pakistani-law remedy).
- Registration complaints: complaints about police/immigration conduct go to the
  department, the ombudsman, or the courts (see civic-services complaint workflow).
SOURCE: Foreigners Act, 1946; CrPC rights framework. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: PAKISTAN LAW vs HOME-COUNTRY LAW: family matters. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
PAKISTAN LAW vs HOME-COUNTRY LAW: family matters. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
KEY FRAMEWORK (summary):
- Marriage: a marriage in Pakistan involving a foreign national is registered under
  Pakistani law (nikahnama) where performed in Pakistan; marriage to a Pakistani citizen
  does NOT by itself confer Pakistani citizenship.
- Citizenship through marriage (Citizenship Act, 1951 framework): a foreign woman married
  to a Pakistani citizen may acquire citizenship on the prescribed conditions; a foreign
  man married to a Pakistani woman does not gain citizenship through the marriage alone
  (gender-specific historical rule — verify the current act).
- Divorce/child custody: governed by Pakistani family law where the matter is within
  Pakistani jurisdiction; a foreign court order may need recognition/execution in Pakistan,
  and vice versa — the applicable law depends on jurisdiction (see cross-border family
  records).
- Birth of a child: children born in Pakistan to foreign parents do not automatically
  become Pakistani citizens (citizenship is by descent/documented grounds under the
  Citizenship Act, 1951).
SOURCE: Citizenship Act, 1951; family-law framework. VERIFICATION: metadata-verified
(citizenship conditions should be checked against the current act).

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: DISTINCTION: emergency and consular support. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
chunks.text:
DISTINCTION: emergency and consular support. COVERAGE: PARTIAL.
- PAKISTAN SIDE: emergency services (Rescue 1122, hospitals, police 15) serve everyone in
  Pakistan regardless of nationality; the foreigner pays for medical treatment like any
  private patient unless covered.
- HOME-COUNTRY SIDE: consular protection (lost passport, emergency travel document, legal
  referrals, welfare checks) is provided by the foreigner's own embassy/consulate — this is
  the home country's service, NOT a Pakistani government function. Pakistan's Ministry of
  Foreign Affairs facilitates access to foreign missions but does not provide consular
  services to foreign nationals.
- Lost documents: report the loss to the local police (FIR/duly reported) and to the home
  embassy; the embassy issues replacement/emergency travel documents, then the Ministry of
  Interior/immigration is approached for exit formalities where required.
SOURCE: MOFA facilitation practice; consular practice of foreign missions.
VERIFICATION: metadata-verified.

chunks.title: Foreigners in Pakistan — Residence, Registration, Work, Study, Family & Emergencies (Depth Expansion)
chunks.chunkTitle: RULE FOR ANSWERS: whenever a question concerns what a foreigner's OWN country can or must do
chunks.text:
RULE FOR ANSWERS: whenever a question concerns what a foreigner's OWN country can or must do
(consular assistance, home-country documents, home-country marriage/divorce rules), answer
from the home country's framework and say it is home-country law — do not answer it with
Pakistani law. Pakistani law governs entry, stay, registration, offences and remedies within
Pakistan.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: University Admission Criteria and Merit-Based Selection
chunks.text:
University Admission Criteria and Merit-Based Selection
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy Guidelines + University Statutes

All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan must follow transparent, merit-based admission criteria.
Key principles:
- Admissions must be based on merit as determined by academic records, entry tests, and/or interviews.
- Universities must publish their admission criteria, merit formula, and seat distribution before the admission cycle.
- Reserved seats: Provincial quotas exist for public sector universities as per government policy (e.g., Sindh has a 40% rural quota for provincial universities).
- Foreign students: HEC regulates admission of foreign students under the Self-Financing Scheme.
- Provisional admission: Universities may offer provisional admission subject to document verification. If documents are found fake, admission stands cancelled.
- Merit list: Universities must display merit lists publicly (on website and notice boards).
Source: HEC Policy Guidelines on Admissions; Individual University Admission Policies.
Note: Specific merit formulas and cut-off scores vary by university and programme. Consult your university's applicable regulations for exact criteria.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: University Fee Structure and Disclosure Requirements
chunks.text:
University Fee Structure and Disclosure Requirements
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / University Syndicates
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

Universities must disclose their complete fee structure before admission:
- Tuition fee, examination fee, library fee, laboratory fee, student welfare fund, and other charges must be clearly listed.
- Fee structure must be approved by the University Syndicate/Governing Body.
- Any revision in fee structure requires prior approval of the Syndicate and must be communicated to students.
- Universities cannot impose arbitrary or hidden charges beyond the approved fee structure.
- Fee challan/receipt must be issued for every payment.
- Self-financing programmes may have higher fees but must be disclosed upfront.
Source: HEC Guidelines on Fee Structure; University Syndicate Resolutions.
Note: Fee amounts vary significantly by university, programme, and province. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: HEC National Fee Refund Policy
chunks.text:
HEC National Fee Refund Policy
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: Official HEC Policy Guidelines
Source URL: https://www.hec.gov.pk

HEC National Fee Refund Policy at Higher Education Institutions:
1. Full (100%) refund of tuition fee if student applies for admission cancellation up to 7th day of commencement of classes.
2. Half (50%) refund of tuition fee if student applies for admission cancellation between 8th and 15th day of commencement of classes.
3. No (0%) refund of tuition fee if applied after 16th day of commencement of classes.
4. Security deposit is always 100% refundable upon withdrawal, regardless of timing.
5. Admission fee is generally non-refundable once classes have commenced.
6. Hostels: Refund of hostel fees follows separate university hostel rules.
Application procedure:
- Submit written application to the Registrar/Controller of Examinations.
- Attach original fee receipts and admission letter.
- University must process refund within 30 days of application.
Source: HEC National Fee Refund Policy (https://www.hec.gov.pk).

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: Fee Concession and Waiver Policies for Deserving Students
chunks.text:
Fee Concession and Waiver Policies for Deserving Students
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Provincial Governments / University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All Public Sector Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + Provincial Laws + University Statutes

Fee concessions and waivers are available for:
- Orphan students: Full or partial fee waiver as per university policy.
- Disabled students: Fee concessions under the Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) framework and university-specific policies.
- Low-income students: Need-based fee waivers assessed through means testing.
- Merit-based waivers: Universities offer merit scholarships that waive tuition fees for top performers.
- Government employee wards: Some universities offer concessions for children of government employees.
- Zakat funds: Public sector universities may allocate Zakat funds for student fee support.
Application procedure:
- Submit application to the Student Affairs/Financial Aid Office.
- Attach supporting documents (income certificates, orphan certificates, disability certificates).
- University committee evaluates and approves/rejects applications.
Source: HEC Need-Based Merit Scholarship Policy; University Fee Concession Rules.
Note: Eligibility criteria and concession amounts vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: Provincial Quotas and Seat Reservations in Public Universities
chunks.text:
Provincial Quotas and Seat Reservations in Public Universities
Authority: Provincial Governments / Higher Education Commission
Jurisdiction: Public Sector Universities (Province-specific)
Legal Status: Provincial Laws + HEC Guidelines

Public sector universities in Pakistan follow provincial quota systems:
Sindh:
- 40% rural quota for Sindh-domiciled students in provincial universities.
- 60% merit-based (open merit) for all Sindh-domiciled students.
- Universities of Sindh (University of Sindh, MUET, Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences) follow Sindh provincial quotas.
Punjab:
- Merit-based admissions with reserved seats for minorities (5% in public sector institutions).
Khyber Pakhtunkhwa:
- Merit-based with reserved seats for merged tribal districts.
Balochistan:
- Significant quotas for underrepresented districts.
Federal universities:
- Federal quotas apply to federally-chartered universities (e.g., NUST, UET, Quaid-i-Azam University).
Source: Provincial Education Department Policies; HEC Admission Guidelines.
Note: Quota percentages and eligibility vary by province and university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: Provisional Admission and Document Verification
chunks.text:
Provisional Admission and Document Verification
Authority: Individual Universities
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes

Universities may offer provisional admission subject to document verification:
- Provisional admission is granted when original documents (mark sheets, certificates) are not immediately available.
- Student must submit original documents within the timeframe specified by the university (typically 30-60 days).
- If documents are found to be fake, forged, or tampered with:
  - Admission stands cancelled immediately.
  - University may initiate disciplinary proceedings.
  - Criminal proceedings under PPC Section 471 (using as genuine a forged document) may be filed.
- Student has right to be heard before admission is cancelled (due process under Article 10-A of the Constitution).
Source: University Admission Regulations; Pakistan Penal Code Section 471.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: Admission Grievance and Appeal Mechanism
chunks.text:
Admission Grievance and Appeal Mechanism
Authority: Universities / Provincial Ombudsman / Courts
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes + Constitutional Law

If a student believes their admission was unfairly denied or cancelled:
1. Internal appeal: Submit representation to the University Registrar/Vice-Chancellor within the timeframe specified (typically 15-30 days).
2. Provincial Ombudsman: For public sector universities, complaint can be filed with the Provincial Ombudsman for maladministration.
3. Writ petition: If fundamental rights are violated (e.g., discrimination under Article 25), student may approach the High Court under Article 199 of the Constitution.
4. HEC complaint: For HEC-recognized universities, complaint can be filed with HEC if university violates HEC admission policies.
Grounds for appeal:
- Merit formula was not applied correctly.
- Quota was misapplied.
- Discrimination on basis of gender, religion, ethnicity, or province.
- Procedural irregularity in admission process.
Source: Constitution of Pakistan Articles 25 (Equality), 199 (High Court jurisdiction); University Statutes.

chunks.title: University Admissions, Fee Structure, Refund Policy, and Fee Concessions
chunks.chunkTitle: Hyderabad Universities — Admission Information
chunks.text:
Hyderabad Universities — Admission Information
Authority: University of Sindh / Mehran University (MUET) / Liaquat University (LUHMS)
Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Sindh
Legal Status: University-specific statutes and Sindh provincial policies

Major universities in Hyderabad and their admission frameworks:
University of Sindh (Jamshoro):
- Public sector university established in 1947.
- Follows Sindh provincial quotas (40% rural, 60% merit).
- Admissions governed by University of Sindh Statutes.
- Programmes: Arts, Science, Law, Medicine, Islamic Studies, Management.
Mehran University of Engineering and Technology (MUET), Jamshoro:
- Public sector engineering university.
- Admissions based on entry test (MUET Entry Examination) + intermediate marks.
- Follows Sindh provincial quotas.
Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences (LUMHS), Jamshoro:
- Public sector medical university.
- Admissions based on MDCAT (Medical and Dental College Admission Test) + HSSC marks.
- Follows Sindh provincial quotas and medical admission policies.
Note: Specific admission criteria, merit formulas, fee structures, and deadlines are set by each university annually. Consult the respective university's official admission advertisement and applicable regulations for current information.
Source: University of Sindh Statutes; MUET Admission Policy; LUMHS Admission Policy; Sindh Higher Education Commission.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: University Attendance Requirements
chunks.text:
University Attendance Requirements
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

HEC and universities prescribe minimum attendance requirements:
- Minimum attendance: Most universities require 75-80% attendance in each course to be eligible for examinations.
- Shortage of attendance: If a student falls below the minimum attendance threshold:
  - University may debar the student from appearing in examinations for that course.
  - Student may be required to repeat the course.
  - Some universities allow condonation of shortage on medical or genuine grounds with supporting evidence.
- Medical exemption: Students with certified medical conditions may apply for attendance condonation with medical certificates.
- Practical/laboratory courses: Higher attendance requirements (often 80-90%) apply for lab-based courses.
- Distance learning: HEC-recognized distance learning programmes have relaxed attendance requirements.
Source: HEC Policy on Academic Standards; Individual University Academic Regulations.
Note: Specific attendance percentages and condonation rules vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: University Grading System and CGPA Calculation
chunks.text:
University Grading System and CGPA Calculation
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

HEC recommends a standardized grading system for universities:
Grade scale (typical):
- A: 85-100% (4.0 grade points)
- B+: 80-84% (3.5 grade points)
- B: 75-79% (3.0 grade points)
- C+: 70-74% (2.5 grade points)
- C: 65-69% (2.0 grade points)
- D: 50-64% (1.0 grade point) — minimum passing grade in most universities
- F: Below 50% (0 grade points) — fail

CGPA calculation:
- CGPA = Sum of (Credit Hours × Grade Points) / Total Credit Hours
- Minimum CGPA for degree completion: typically 2.0 on a 4.0 scale.
- Minimum CGPA for good academic standing: varies by university (often 2.0-2.5).
Source: HEC Policy on Grading System; Individual University Academic Regulations.
Note: Grading scales and CGPA requirements vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Backlog and Course Repeat Policies
chunks.text:
Backlog and Course Repeat Policies
Authority: Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes

When a student fails a course (receives F grade):
- The student must repeat the course in a subsequent semester.
- Maximum attempts: Most universities allow 2-3 attempts to pass a course. If the student fails after maximum attempts:
  - The student may be required to change programme.
  - In some cases, the student may be rusticated/expelled from the programme.
- Backlog: A failed course that has not yet been repeated. Students must clear backlogs within the maximum programme duration.
- Maximum programme duration: Typically, universities allow 1.5-2 times the normal programme duration (e.g., for a 4-year BS, maximum 6-8 years).
- Improvement: Some universities allow students to reappear in examinations to improve grades in passed courses.
Source: Individual University Academic Regulations.
Note: Backlog policies, maximum attempts, and programme duration limits vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Degree Completion Requirements
chunks.text:
Degree Completion Requirements
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

To complete a degree, a student must:
- Pass all required courses with minimum passing grades.
- Achieve minimum CGPA (typically 2.0 on 4.0 scale).
- Complete the required credit hours for the programme.
- Fulfil any additional requirements (thesis, project, internship, comprehensive exam).
- Clear all university dues (fees, library, laboratory).
- Complete the programme within the maximum allowed duration.
Degree conferral:
- Degrees are conferred by the Syndicate/Academic Council of the university.
- Convocation ceremonies are held annually or biannually.
- Students who complete requirements between convocations receive provisional certificates.
Source: HEC Policy on Degree Requirements; Individual University Statutes.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Academic Probation and Academic Standing
chunks.text:
Academic Probation and Academic Standing
Authority: Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes

Academic probation is imposed when a student's academic performance falls below the minimum standard:
- Criteria: Typically, CGPA below 2.0 in a semester, or failure in multiple courses.
- Consequences of academic probation:
  - Student is placed on academic warning/probation.
  - Student may be required to meet with academic advisor.
  - Course load may be reduced.
  - If performance does not improve in subsequent semesters:
 - Student may be required to withdraw from the programme.
 - Student may be rusticated/expelled.
- Appeal: Student has the right to appeal against academic probation/rustication to the relevant academic committee or Vice-Chancellor.
- Due process: Student must be given notice and opportunity to explain before rustication.
Source: Individual University Academic Regulations; Constitutional Article 10-A (Right to Fair Trial).
Note: Academic probation criteria and consequences vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Transcript and Mark Sheet Issuance
chunks.text:
Transcript and Mark Sheet Issuance
Authority: Individual University Registrar/Controller of Examinations
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes + HEC Guidelines

Transcripts and mark sheets are official academic records:
- Transcript: Comprehensive record of all courses, grades, and CGPA across all semesters.
- Mark sheet/Detailed Marks Certificate: Semester-wise breakdown of marks and grades.
- Issuance:
  - Students can apply for transcripts through the Registrar/Controller of Examinations.
  - Processing time: Typically 7-30 days.
  - Fee: Prescribed transcript fee applies.
- Universities cannot withhold transcripts for:
  - Unpaid fees unrelated to the student's own dues.
  - Disciplinary disputes (unless there are legitimate outstanding dues).
- HEC attestation: Transcripts must be attested by HEC for use abroad or for employment in government.
- Digital transcripts: Some universities now issue digital transcripts with QR verification.
Source: HEC Guidelines on Transcript Issuance; Individual University Regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Academic Integrity and Plagiarism Policy
chunks.text:
Academic Integrity and Plagiarism Policy
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All HEC-recognized universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

HEC has issued comprehensive guidelines on academic integrity:
- Plagiarism: Using someone else's work, ideas, or words without proper attribution.
- HEC Plagiarism Policy:
  - All thesis/dissertations must be checked through plagiarism detection software (e.g., Turnitin).
  - Acceptable similarity index: Typically below 19% for thesis/dissertations.
  - Assignments and coursework: Universities set their own plagiarism policies.
- Consequences of plagiarism:
  - Minor: Warning, requirement to resubmit.
  - Major: Zero grade in the course, academic probation.
  - Severe: Rustication/expulsion, degree cancellation.
- Fabrication/falsification: Submitting fake data, forged documents, or fabricated research is a serious academic offence.
- Due process: Students accused of plagiarism must be given notice, hearing, and right to appeal.
Source: HEC Plagiarism Policy; Individual University Academic Integrity Policies.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Examination Regulations and Student Rights
chunks.text:
Examination Regulations and Student Rights
Authority: Individual University Examination Committees
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: University Statutes

University examination regulations cover:
- Examination scheduling: Universities must publish examination schedules at least 30 days in advance.
- Date sheet conflicts: If two exams are scheduled on the same date, student may request rescheduling.
- Examination hall rules: Students must follow prescribed conduct (no unfair means, no electronic devices).
- Unfair means: Copying, use of prohibited materials, impersonation, and other malpractices are punishable.
- Right to re-evaluation: Students have the right to apply for rechecking/re-evaluation of answer scripts within the prescribed timeframe (typically 15-30 days of result declaration).
- Result declaration: Universities must declare results within the timeframe prescribed by their statutes (typically 60-90 days after examinations).
- Supplementary examinations: Students who fail in up to a specified number of courses may appear in supplementary exams.
Source: Individual University Examination Regulations.
Note: Examination rules vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Student Transfer and Migration Between Universities
chunks.text:
Student Transfer and Migration Between Universities
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) / Individual University Statutes
Jurisdiction: All Universities in Pakistan
Legal Status: HEC Policy + University Statutes

Transfer/migration between universities:
- Inter-university transfer: Students may apply to transfer from one university to another, subject to:
  - Availability of seats in the receiving university.
  - Equivalence of courses completed.
  - No-Objection Certificate (NOC) from the current university.
  - Meeting the admission criteria of the receiving university.
- Migration: Temporary study at another university (e.g., for a semester) with credit transfer.
- HEC role: HEC facilitates inter-university transfers and ensures credit equivalence.
- Limitations:
  - Most universities do not allow transfer into final year.
  - Professional programmes (medicine, engineering) have stricter transfer rules.
Source: HEC Guidelines on Credit Transfer; Individual University Transfer Policies.
Note: Transfer policies vary by university and programme. Consult your university's applicable regulations.

chunks.title: University Academic Rules — Attendance, Grading, Probation, Transcripts, and Degree Completion
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Academic Rules and Resources for Students in Hyderabad
chunks.text:
Title: Academic Rules and Resources for Students in Hyderabad
Authority: University of Sindh Act; MUET Act; LUMHS Act; HEC
Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Sindh
Legal Status: Statutory and Institutional
Source: University of Sindh Act, 1972; MUET Act, 1976; LUMHS Act, 2006; HEC Guidelines

Hyderabad-Specific Information:
- University of Sindh (Jamshoro/Hyderabad): Academic rules governed by the University of Sindh Act, 1972 and Statutes framed thereunder. Attendance, grading, CGPA, backlog, and examination rules are set by the Academic Council and notified by the Registrar. Students may consult the Registrar's office or the university website for current academic regulations. Appeals against academic decisions lie with the Academic Committee / Vice-Chancellor as per the University of Sindh Statutes.
  Official website: https://www.usindh.edu.pk | Admissions: https://admissions.usindh.edu.pk | Examinations Wing: https://www.usindh.edu.pk (Examinations section)
- MUET (Jamshoro): Academic rules governed by the Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1976 and Statutes. Engineering programmes have specific attendance and examination rules set by the Academic Council. Students may consult the Registrar or the Academic Office for current regulations.
  Official website: https://www.muet.edu.pk | Admissions: https://www.muet.edu.pk/admissions
- LUMHS (Hyderabad): Academic rules governed by the Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences Act, 2006 and Statutes. Medical programmes follow HEC/PMDC (now PMC) academic standards with specific attendance, clinical training, and examination requirements. Students may consult the university's Academic Office for current regulations.
  Official website: https://www.lumhs.edu.pk | Admissions: https://www.lumhs.edu.pk/admissions/undergraduate_admission.php
- Inter-university transfer: Students in Hyderabad may apply for transfer between University of Sindh, MUET, and LUMHS subject to HEC guidelines, seat availability, and the receiving university's transfer policies. Professional programmes (engineering, medicine) have stricter transfer rules.
- Sindh Higher Education Commission (SHEC): Oversees higher education in Sindh and may be approached for grievances not resolved at the university level.
- Students may approach the Sindh Provincial Ombudsman for complaints against provincial universities.
- Sindh High Court (Hyderabad Bench) is available for writ petitions under Article 199 of the Constitution.

Note: Specific academic rules, regulations, and procedures vary by university. Consult your university's applicable regulations and statutes for current information.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 — Applicability to Educational Institutions
chunks.text:
Title: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 — Applicability to Educational Institutions
Authority: Parliament of Pakistan (Federal Statute)
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Active Statutory Law
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010

Key Provisions:
- The Act defines "workplace" to include any organization, institution, or premises where employees, students, or other persons carry out activities related to employment or education.
- Educational institutions (universities, colleges, schools, madrassas, training centres) are covered workplaces under this Act.
- Harassment means any unwelcome sexual advance, request for sexual favours, sexual conduct, or sexually coloured remarks, or any other conduct of a sexual nature that creates a hostile, intimidating, or offensive environment.
- The Act protects all persons within the covered workplace, regardless of gender, though the statutory title references women.
- Provincial governments have adopted or mirrored this Act through provincial legislation (e.g., Sindh Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010; Punjab Protection Against Harassment of Women Act, 2012).

Note: The specific provincial version applicable to you depends on your institution's location. Consult the relevant provincial Act for your jurisdiction.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Inquiry Committee — Composition and Mandate
chunks.text:
Title: Inquiry Committee — Composition and Mandate
Authority: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 (Section 3) / HEC Anti-Harassment Policy Guidelines
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Statutory Requirement
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010; HEC Policy Guidelines

Key Requirements:
- Every covered institution (including educational institutions) must constitute an Inquiry Committee to investigate harassment complaints.
- The Committee shall consist of at least three (3) members.
- At least one member must be a woman.
- At least one member should be a senior faculty member or administrator.
- The Committee's mandate is to inquire into complaints of harassment and submit findings and recommendations to the competent authority.
- The Committee must act in a time-bound manner as prescribed by the applicable Act.

Note: The specific composition, nomination process, and term of Committee members varies by institution. Consult your university's applicable regulations for the current Committee members and procedures.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Filing a Harassment Complaint — Procedure
chunks.text:
Title: Filing a Harassment Complaint — Procedure
Authority: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 (Sections 4-5) / HEC Anti-Harassment Policy
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Statutory Procedure
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010; HEC Policy Guidelines

Procedure:
1. The complainant (or any person with knowledge of the incident) may file a written complaint to the Inquiry Committee.
2. The complaint should describe the incident(s), including date(s), time, location, nature of harassment, and any witnesses.
3. The complainant may also report to the institution's designated focal person for harassment complaints, if one has been appointed.
4. Upon receipt of the complaint, the Inquiry Committee shall initiate an inquiry.
5. The Committee shall provide the respondent (the person accused) a copy of the complaint and an opportunity to respond.
6. Both parties have the right to present evidence and witnesses.
7. The Committee must complete its inquiry and submit its report within the timeframe prescribed by the applicable Act (typically 30 days from receipt of complaint).
8. The Committee's report shall include findings of fact and recommendations for action, if any.

Note: Specific timelines, forms, and submission procedures vary by institution and province. Consult your university's applicable regulations and the relevant provincial Act.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Available Relief and Remedies for Harassment
chunks.text:
Title: Available Relief and Remedies for Harassment
Authority: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 (Sections 6-7)
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Statutory Remedies
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010

Available Remedies (as per applicable law):
- The competent authority, upon receiving the Inquiry Committee's report, may take appropriate disciplinary action against the respondent if the complaint is substantiated.
- Disciplinary measures available under the applicable law may include written warning, censure, withholding of promotion, recovery of losses, suspension, dismissal, or other measures as prescribed by the relevant statute and institutional regulations.
- The complainant may also seek interim protection measures during the pendency of the inquiry.
- The complainant retains the right to approach law enforcement authorities if the conduct constitutes a criminal offence under the Pakistan Penal Code (e.g., Section 354A PPC — stalking, Section 509 PPC — word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman).

Note: The specific disciplinary measures and their applicability depend on the relevant Act and institutional regulations. Consult the applicable provincial Act and your university's regulations.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Appeal Against Inquiry Committee Decision
chunks.text:
Title: Appeal Against Inquiry Committee Decision
Authority: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010 (Section 8)
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Statutory Right
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010

Appeal Process:
- Any aggrieved party (complainant or respondent) may appeal against the decision or order passed by the competent authority.
- The appeal lies to the Federal Ombudsman or Provincial Ombudsman (as applicable based on the institution's jurisdiction) within the timeframe prescribed by the Act.
- The Ombudsman shall hear the appeal and pass an order.
- Further appeal against the Ombudsman's order lies to the competent court as prescribed by the applicable law.

Note: The specific appellate authority and timelines depend on whether the institution falls under federal or provincial jurisdiction. Consult the relevant Ombudsman's office for your area.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: External Complaint Routes — When Institution Fails to Act
chunks.text:
Title: External Complaint Routes — When Institution Fails to Act
Authority: Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010; Constitution of Pakistan
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal & Provincial)
Legal Status: Statutory and Constitutional Rights
Source: Gazette of Pakistan, 2010; Constitution of Pakistan, 1973

External Routes:
- If the institution fails to constitute an Inquiry Committee or fails to act on a complaint within a reasonable time, the complainant may approach:
  1. Federal Ombudsman (Wafaqi Mohtasib) — for federal institutions. Helpline: 1055.
  2. Provincial Ombudsman — for provincial institutions.
  3. HEC Complaint Cell — for HEC-recognized universities. HEC may issue directives to the institution.
  4. Law enforcement (local police station) — if the conduct constitutes a criminal offence under PPC.
  5. High Court — via writ petition under Article 199 of the Constitution if fundamental rights are violated or the institution/inquiry mechanism is failing to perform its statutory duty.

Note: Jurisdiction determines which route is appropriate. Federal institutions go to the Federal Ombudsman; provincial institutions go to the Provincial Ombudsman.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: HEC Anti-Harassment Policy Requirements for Universities
chunks.text:
Title: HEC Anti-Harassment Policy Requirements for Universities
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan
Jurisdiction: All HEC-Recognized Universities and Degree-Awarding Institutions
Legal Status: HEC Policy Regulation
Source: HEC Policy Guidelines; https://www.hec.gov.pk

HEC Requirements:
- All HEC-recognized universities must adopt and implement an Anti-Harassment Policy consistent with the Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010.
- Universities must constitute an Inquiry Committee as required by the Act.
- Universities must designate a focal person for harassment complaints.
- Universities must display the Anti-Harassment Policy and complaint procedure prominently on campus and on the university website.
- Universities must conduct awareness sessions on harassment prevention and student rights.
- HEC may take action against universities that fail to comply, including directives, show-cause notices, or other regulatory measures.

Note: HEC policy sets minimum standards. Individual universities may have additional provisions. Consult your university's applicable Anti-Harassment Policy for specific procedures and contacts.

chunks.title: Anti-Harassment in Educational Institutions — Act 2010, HEC Policy, Complaint Procedure, and Appeals
chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Anti-Harassment Resources for Students in Hyderabad

Jurisdiction: Hyderabad, Sindh

Source: Sindh Protection Against Harassment of Women at the Workplace Act, 2010; University Acts; HEC Guidelines

Hyderabad-Specific Information:
