# 3. Procedure
Title: HEC faculty appointment and eligibility frameworks: Tenure Track, IPFP, Professor of Practice, Meritorious Professor, DNP, Professor Emeritus, Visiting Faculty, BUTA
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan
Section: 3. Procedure
Official page: https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/policies/Pages/Framework-PE.aspx
Source file: https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/policies/Documents/Framework-PE.pdf
Version: Frameworks as published; notification dates from the HEC register
Notification / publication date: 2026-10-10
Effective date: 2026-10-10
Legal status: Mixed — per-framework status recorded in each section
Extracted verbatim from the official HEC source on 2026-10-10; only layout was repaired (line wraps, page markup) — no wording was changed.

3. Procedure:
3.1. All such cases be decided by the concerned university through Syndicate/Appointing Authority in light of the HEC’s guidelines .
3.2. Those who are desirous to join as Professor Emeritus in the concerned university may submit or get no minated by the concerned Chair or Dean in writing , preferably 06 months before the age of superannuation .
4. Terms and Conditions:
4.1. Whereas the conferment of PE status will be for life time, the financial benefits will be given for a maximum period of 10 years or up to the age of 70 years , whichever is earlier .
The PE is expected to contribute to the academic life of the university to a great extent in consonance with the status and caliber of the title and PE shall carry no formal statutory administrative positions in a university, where other senior faculty is/are available for such positions. However, at young universities, where se nior faculty is not available to take up administrative positions, PE may be asked to take up administrative position s .
4.2. Professor Emeritus up to the age of 65 years, would be eligible to apply for HEC research funding, but he/she would be required to include at least one Co - PI from the host Institution .
4.3. The Professor Emeritus, at least for the period during which he/she enjoys financial bene fits from the University, will have the following responsibilities:
4.3.1. Mandatory presence on campus at least for three working days a week.
4.3.2. Provide guidance or continue research with faculty and/or students.
4.3.3. G raduate student’s supervision.
4.3.4. Seminars and/or writing o f textbooks in the field of his/her specialization.
4.3.5. Any other assignment by the Vice Chancellor, including statutory academic administrative positions temporarily, particularly in young universities where indigenous senior faculty is not yet available.
5. Honorarium/Remuneration:
5.1. Professor Emeritus shall be entitled for financial benefits for a maximum period of 10 years or up to the age of 70 years whichever is earlier and draw a consolidated amount of honorarium of Rs. 200,000/p.m . (all inclusive) with an annual increase of 5%.
5.2. The concerned parent u niversity will bear financial liability of Professor Emeritus out of its own resources for both categories of PE i.e. Professors/Vice Chancellors .
However, HEC will bear remunerations of only those category of Vice Chancellors who offer their services as Professor Emeritus in newly developed universities, other than their parent university (reference Section 2) .
5.3. The initial offer of appointment will be for a period of 5 years , extendable on a yearly basis for the purpose of financial benefits .
5.4. The conferment of Emeritus Status shall normally be for lifetime but can be terminated if the Professor so desired or the Syndicate terminates by ¾ majority on groun ds of inefficiency, moral turpitude or physical or mental incapacity or gross misconduct .
5.5. During the paid tenure of Prof essor Emeritus, he/she will not get financial benefits from any other university/institution/organization . In case, PE gets appointed o n any other full time position during the paid tenure, within or outside parent university, the payment for PE will be discontinued for that period.
Similarly, those Vice Chancellors who join as Professor Emeritus at a newly developed university, other than the parent university , will also not be paid the honorarium of PE if he/she is employed with any other university/institution/organization , or employed by the host university on another position within the paid tenure of P rofessor Emeritus .

1. Purposes and Principles
For the purpose of recognizing the achievements of outstanding academicians and researchers , the title of Distinguished National Professor (D N P) shall be awarded to scholars who are leaders in their respective fields and have made significant contributions to their academic disciplines at national and international level s .
DNP is a prestigious title and an exceptional honor, which shall be awarded solely based on merit as assessed against prescribed eligibility and evaluation criteria as well as upon the recommendation s of a high - level HEC selection committee , mentioned at Section - 4 .

2.2 Guidelines for grading the candidates
The following principles will be observed w hile grad ing the candidates under various indicators , given at Table - 1 above:
i. Research Contributions :
• The maximum marks to be given under “ Invention /Innovation” should be 10 , even if the
candidate obtains full marks in all indicators under this head.
• The candidates will be ranked within one broad subject category on percentile basis,
which means that a candidate with the highest Cumulative Impact Factor of his/her publications as a Corresponding Author in a given broad category of subjects will get maximum marks (100%) . Other candidates will get marks accordingly (e.g. if 0 5 is taken as the benchmark for the highest Cumulative IF, then the others will get 0 4 marks for IF of 0 4, 0 3 marks for IF of 3 and so on).
• Similarly, the candidate with the highest number of total citations, h - index and ci tation
per article will get max imum marks (100%) , while o thers will get marks accordingly.
• In case, there is only one candidate in the broad discipline, top percentile scores to be
used will be mean/average of top scores candidates in all disciplines .
ii. Mentorship
• The h ighest Cumulative Impact Factor of publications emerged from PhD thesis of
respective PhD graduate(s) will get maximum marks (100%) , while others will get marks accordingly.
iii. Research Grants :
• M arks on research projects will be given only , if the applicant is Principal Investigator
(PI).
iv. Recognition & Engagement
• Only those International Awards that are listed in the Annex - II of this framework will be
considered for grading .
• No marks will be awarded for certificate of appreciation/participation or research
fellowship/scholarship.
• No marks will be assigned in case of membership of Boards, Committees & other
Governing bodies within the universities .

3. Procedure for nomination and recommendations
T he following procedure wil l be adopted for receiving nominations and finalization of recommendations:
I. The nomination and selection of Distinguished National Professors will take place annually.
II. The universities will issue a call for nomination from all faculties and departments upon
initiation of the annual cycle by HEC .
III. The application/nomination will be supported with the following:
a. A covering note and complete data on D N P Evaluation Parameters (Table 1).
b. Latest CV of the candidate .
c. Evidence/supporting documents required for achievements claimed under :
i. Research Contributions :
• Official documents or evidence of patents /service/process/crops
( c ommercialized /not commercialize d) .
• List of articles published including authors, title, name of journal, year of publication,
pages and DOI assigned along with impact factor of each article in the respective year of publication , as well as citation index (total citations, H - Index and citations per article), using Web of Science (WOS) as the data source. The weblink allowing access to Web of Science Profile ID must also be provided .
ii. Mentorship :
• Evidence/notifications of supervis ion as main supervisor, list of PhD scholars
supervised along with research titles of PhD thesis and list of publications emerged from PhD thesis combined with IF of respective journal(s), degree completion year/status, copies of degrees and registration n umber in HEC Directory .
• A statement by candidate that publications listed under this category are from PhD
thesis under his/her supervision (as main supervisor) and that he/she is corresponding author in all publication under this category . Incorrect state ment can lead to debar for three years, applying to DNP; debarring to other facilities of HEC, such as research funding and other awards may also be affected depending on level of violation of ethics .
iii. R esearch G rants :
• List of local/international research grants won/received including information on
funding source, start & end dates of project, grant amount and role of candidate i.e.
PI/Co - PI .
iv. Services to Community :
• Evidence/official documents of campaigns, policies (developed or contributed in its
formulation) , tv/media shows, articles in print media etc.
v. Recognition, Engagement and other C ontributions :
• List and certificates of national/international awards received .
• N otifications /evidence of editorship of journal including weblink of the respective
journal as well as evidence for Chair of Academic Chair(s) .
• List and letters of fellowships/memberships along with engagement status
(Lifetime/ specific t erm) .
• L etters / evidence of industry collaboration (s) and data/reports on outcomes.
• L ist and dates of reputed conferences / seminars (regularly held at least for the
last 05 years), where the candidate was invit ed as keynote speaker .
vi. Endorsement :
• List of three referees with name s, academic title, postal address, email IDs
(institutional email, in case still serving) as well as their short biography and assessment of DNP candidate’s contributions/impact in the relevant field(s). At least one of the referees must describe/assess the impact of the DNP candidate’s contribution in service to the university, community and country .
• A statement on Conflict of Interest , that the candidate ha s not collaborated with
the referee at least in last 5 years , either in terms of joint publication, co supervision of a graduate student, or Co - PI in a r esearch g rant .
• It will be the responsibility of the university to examine profiles of the referees
who are themselves qualified and willing to make judgement of the DNP candidates .
d. Two one - page statements prepared by the candidates, covering the below:
i. Contributions in relevant field at national and international level and its impact .
ii. S ervice s rendered at the community /university le vel and its impact.
IV. Each participating university will set up a permanent /Standing selection committee, to be
chaired by the Vice Chancellor including the Registrar, Director QEC, up to two existing DNPs and up to three senior Deans to review the applications and recommend one candidate for the award of D N P.
V. The selection committee wo uld make the decision and convey the results to HEC within
deadlines specified by HEC.
VI. All the documents of the recommended nominee would be provided by the universities to
HEC in the form of a dossier, duly tagged and page numbers inserted. Soft copies of the dossier must also be provided in a USB or uploaded on online storage/file sharing platforms.
VII. Candidates recommended by the universities shall be evaluated at national level by the HEC
Se lection Committee ( Table 2 ), which shall meet annually to finalize its recommendations.
VIII. The candidates can be called to appear in an interview if the national level selection
committee deems it necessary .
IX. Only those whose applications and supporting docum ents were submitted on or before the
specified deadline and recommended by the parent university will be considered for the award of title .
X. The National Level Selection Committee will review the recommendations and approve
select ion of the DNPs under the below subjects/categories . A maximum of five DNPs will be selected per cycle with not more than one DNP in any of the below mentioned subject s /categor ies :
i. Education .
ii. Social Sciences, Journalism and Information
iii. Information and Communication Technology
iv. Health and Welfare
v. Arts and Humanities
vi. Natural Sciences, Mathematics and Statistics .
vii. Engineering, Manufacturing and Construction .
viii. Agriculture, Forestry, Fisheries and Veterinary
ix. Services
x. Business, Administration and Law

3. Selection Procedure

recommendation, duly signed by all members, to HEC

candidates’ dossier for facilitation of the S election C ommittee.

covering letter, specifically addressing the criteria outlined in Table 1. The CV must include supporting information, consistent with the required cri teria.

6. Maximum of 05 Distinguished National Professors will be appointed in a cycle under the list of broad categories of disciplines (mentioned at Section 3 “ Procedure for nomination and recommendations” ) and that no t more than one from a broad category of discipline will be appointed in a cycle . The decision of HEC will be final.
7. Anyone who provides false or misleading evidence will b e barred for three years from the competition as well as from other facilities of HEC ( Res ea rch Funding or Awards) . An award granted on the basis of false an d misleading evidence will be withdrawn and penalty implemented .

FRAMEWORK FOR HEC BEST UNIVERSITY TEACHER AWARD (HEC BUTA) 202 5 FRAMEWORK FOR HEC BEST UNIVERSIY TEACHER AWARD The Best University Teacher Award was established in 2003 to recognize outstanding teachers, and incentivize all teachers to enhance their pedagogical skills. It is open to BPS, TTS, and contract teacher from public as well as private universities.
The framework of Best University Teacher Award was revised in 2019 wherein a different set of awards criteria, based on indicators of effective teaching, was incorporated with an aim to encourage more attention to teaching.
Objectives : Best University Teacher Award has three objectives.
• Incentive : Provide an incentive to teachers to improve the quality of their teaching and
andr agogy;
• Andr agogical : build a national consensus on what constitutes good teaching;
• Capacity Building : build a national database, accessible to all teachers, especially
junior teachers, of syllabuses, grading systems (including tests, exams, quizzes), lesson plans, and lecture slides (PPTs).
A. Award Levels The Best University Teacher Award has been split into two levels:
a. University - Level Best University Teacher Award The university level awards would be conferred directly by the universities. Each university's best teacher awards will consist of a certificate of merit, plus, if a university Syndicate so decides, a cash award of up to Rs. 200,000/ - .
Only the winners of uni versity level awards would be eligible for competing in the HEC national award competition.
b. National - Level Best University Teacher Award HEC would confer one or more national awards, to a limited number of recipients, to ensure their exclusivity and prestige. The HEC National Level Best University Teacher Award consists of a cash prize of Rs. 1,000,000/ - (Rupees ten l ac s only) along with a certificate of merit and a n HEC Medal .
B. Award Criteria and Assessment Mechanism The basic eligibility and revised set of criteria is placed below and at Annex - I .
i. Eligibility Requirements
Only those teachers who meet all these eligibility requirements will be considered for University - Level as well as National - Level Best University Teacher Awards. Selecting “ No ” will render the applicant ineligible to compete for BUTA.

C. PROCEDURE
a. All awards pertain to a particular academic year (Fall to Spring).
b. Upon announcement by HEC, the participating universities will issue the call f or nominations, widely disseminating the information to all the departments, for University - Level Best University Teacher Award competitions.
c. Each participating university would set up a permanent selection committee, chaired by
the Vice Chancellor (and including the Registrar, Director QEC, and two senior most Deans ) to review the applications or nominations and select the winners. The selectio n committee would finalize its decision and the results conveyed to HEC within the prescribed deadline.
d. University - level best university teacher awards would be distributed at the time of the
university convocation.
e. The winners of the university - level best teacher awards would automatically be entered into the competition for the HEC national best university teacher award. Only those whose application and supporting documents that were submitted for university - level a ward will be eligible for the national award.
f. One copy of the complete dossier, comprising all the documents and assessment (properly ordered, tagged/annexed with page numbers inserted) of the winner of the university - level best teacher award, must be subm itted to HEC for consideration for National - Level Best University Teacher Award. The dossier must include the following:
i. A covering note prepared by the teacher.
ii. Filled nomination form, duly signed by the VC/Registrar.
iii. Latest CV of the teacher.
iv. A certificate, duly signed by all members of the University’s Selection
Committee (in original), certifying that all eligibility criteria has been met by the to g raduate students.
Student Evaluations Student evaluations are one of the means of assessing teaching effectiveness. Students’ feedback will also show the improvement in teaching.
This helps make comparative assessment of teachers.
Assign a comparative grade based on review of all evaluation results .
20% university - level award winner.
v. Completed questionnaire (see Annex - I ) with marks added and supporting
documents of the teacher included, pertaining to the particular assessment period. The supporting documents must include the following:
• The syllabus or syllabuses, including grading systems, exams, tests, quizzes,
assignments and lesson plans.
• Video tapes of lectures and PowerPoint presentation (PPTs). The videos are
to be provided within a USB or uploaded at any hosting service over internet, for which a working link along with access rights assigned to everyone, is to be provided.
• Student evaluations of the courses being considered for the award, and the
average evaluation scores of teacher and courses across the department, faculty, and the entire university. Student evaluations are confidential documents, and would be av ailable only to the evaluation committees and will be shared with HEC.
• Three one - page statements prepared by the teacher. The three statements
are:
1. Statement of teaching philosophy and ethics .

Title: HEC faculty appointment and eligibility frameworks: Tenure Track, IPFP, Professor of Practice, Meritorious Professor, DNP, Professor Emeritus, Visiting Faculty, BUTA
Authority: Higher Education Commission (HEC) of Pakistan

D. TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE AWARD
1. The HEC Best University Teacher Award consists of a cash prize of Rs. 1,000,000 (Rupees ten Lac only) and a certificate of merit with a n HEC Medal.
2. Each university level best teacher award will consist of a certificate of merit, plus, if a university Syndicate so decides, a cash award of up to Rs. 200,000.
3. Only those who have won the competition for the University - Level Best Teacher Award are eligible to compete for the national level Best University Teacher Award.
4. The following are the eligibility requirements for university - level best teacher awards as well as the national level best university teacher awards:
i. They are full - time permanent teachers, including those on TTS, BPS, or long - term
contract, at any public or private sector university or DAI recognized by the HEC.
ii. They have completed a minimum of three years of consecutive /active service as a
teacher of the nominating university or DAI prior to the date of the award.
iii. They are less than 60 years of age.
iv. They should have been physically present at the nominating university in the
previous three years.
v. They did not miss any class during the calendar year. An exemption may be provided
in cases of ill health or medical emergency, on the production of documentary evidence, and if the absence was compensated by the organization of make - up classes in consultation with the students. QEC is responsible for validating this information.
vi. They did not avail long - term leave (i.e., exceeding 3 weeks during the year of
evaluation).
vii. There were no disciplinary proceedings against them, e.g., on charges of plagiarism.
viii. There are no adverse remarks in their ACRs during the previous three (03) years.
ix. They did not serve as Vice - Chancellors or on other key administrative positions in
the university in the past three years.
x. Their application/ nomination along with all supporting documents have been
provided on or before the annual deadline.
xi. The teacher must have taught a minimum of 6 credit hours in each semester during
the evaluation period (Fall - Spring) . The number of courses taught will be verified through student evaluations.
xii. The teacher did not receive national level Best University Teacher Award after 2019.
5. The Selection Committee will certify that all eligibility criteria have been met by the nominee , and send the certificate, duly signed by all members, to HEC.
6. The Selection Committee of the University/DAI will select a winner and two runners up for the university - level award process.
7. HEC will only entertain nominations received according to the prescribed chan nel and procedure. HEC's decision will be based solely on the documentary record, plus the recommendation of the university ’s selection committee.
8. A teacher may receive Best University Teacher Award once in their life time.
9. The university will set up a mechanism to address grievances , if any.
10. The University/DAI is responsible to ensure the transparency of the process.
11. HEC has the right to not make an award in a particular year.
12. The decision of the HEC will be final.
13. Anyone who provides false or misleading evidence will be barred from the competition for life. An award granted on the basis of false and misleading evidence will be withdrawn.
14. The teacher shall have no pending liabilities with any D ivision of HEC. He/ s he will provide a certificate countersigned by the Director QEC/Registrar of the university .
ANNEX - I Questionnaires on Best University Teacher Award Evaluation Parameters Important Notes:
i). Universities are required to follow “Parameters and Assessment Mechanism” mentioned in Table 2
above while responding to questions and assigning weights against each of the parameters.
ii). Response to all the questions within the questionnaires is mandatory. The questions carry equal
marks, as below , except question xviii in Parameter - 6 (Classroom Teaching) :
Yes = 2, Somewhat = 1, No = 0
iii). Weightage against each parameter must be calculated as per the following formulae:
(Marks Secured divided by Maximum Marks multiply by Weightage) x 100 Below is the solved example for Parameter 3 (Course Syllabus) in a scenario where the teacher’s answer to 9 questions is “Yes” and to 2 questions is “Somewhat”:
Total questions in parameter 3 are 1 2 , thus maximum marks of the parameter are 2 4 Weightage of parameter 3, as per Table 2 above, is 10 % or 10/100 Marks Secured for “Yes”: 9 x 2 = 18 and for “Somewhat”: 2x1 = 2, so total marks secured are 20 Weight calculation as per above mentioned formulae = (20/2 4 x 10/100) x 100 = 8 . 33 (weight obtained by the teacher in parameter 3) The total weight obtained by the teacher in all parameters will be the sum of weights obtained by the teacher in each of the nine parameters.
(Weight calculated on any other method or without responding against all questions will not be accepted) .
iv). Universities are required to use the provided template in responding against each question under
various evaluation parameters. Questionnaires not filled as per the below format will not be accepted.

GUIDELINES FOR ENGAGEMENT OF VISITING FACULTY IN HEIs
1.0 Preamble and Authority
1.1 The Higher Education Commission (HEC) acknowledges the critical contribution of Visiting Faculty in enhancing the academic rigor and practical relevance of programs offered by Pakistani universities. They provide indispensable in dustry expertise, specialized skills, and contemporary knowledge that complement the permanent faculty.
1.2 However, unregulated or excessive reliance on Visiting Faculty, particularly in public sector institutions, poses significant risks to academic qual ity, the sustainability of research culture, and long - term institutional development. These guidelines are established to standardize the engagement, roles, and management of Visiting Faculty across HEC recognized public and private sector HEIs. The object ive is to leverage their expertise while safeguarding educational standards, institutional integrity, and student welfare.
1.3 These guidelines are issued under the powers vested in the HEC by its Ordinance No.
LIII of 2002, Section 10(1)(q) & (r) . All HEIs are required to develop their own policy guidelines for hiring Visiting Faculty, which must be fully aligned with these guidelines and contemporary best practices. The institutional policy must be reviewed by the Institutional Quality Circle (IQ C) or equivalent body and receive formal ratification from the relevant statutory forum.
2.0 Definition and Scope
2.1 A Visiting Faculty member is an individual engaged on a temporary basis , typically part - time , to deliver specific courses or provide instr uctional support that addresses academic needs . Such an engagement does not confer any implicit or automatic right to a permanent, regular position within the HEI.
3.0 Eligibility Criteria
3.1 The minimum qualification for any Visiting Faculty position must be equivalent to the HEC's prescribed criteria for the corresponding regular faculty rank, as specified for general and professional disciplines. The current criteria are available at the official HEC website :
https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/services/universities/qa/Pages/faculty appointmentcriteria.aspx 3.2 HEIs are encouraged to establish and apply more stringent criteria than the HE C minimums, commensurate with the specific requirements and strategic objectives of their academic programs.
..
4.0 Permissible Limits
To maintain academic quality and ensure the primacy of a strong core faculty, the following limits are mandated:
4.1 Overall Limit at Department Level : The total number of Visiting Faculty members within an academic department must not exceed 25% of the department's total full - time regular faculty strength.

4.2 Overall Limit at Program Level: For any degree program, the core and major courses taught by Visiting Faculty must not constitute more than 25% of the total core/major credit hours required for degree completion.
4.3 Student - Teacher Ratio Calculation: Visiting Faculty shall not be count ed in the calculation of the student - teacher ratio, which shall be determined exclusively based on the number of full - time regular faculty.
5.0 Recruitment and Selection Procedure
5.1 Advertisement: Vacancies for Visiting Faculty positions must be publicly advertised on the HEI’s official website and prominent institutional notice boards. Wider circulation through local or national newspapers may be employed if deemed necessary.
5.2 Advertisement Content: The advertisement must explicitly state:
i. The minimum eligibility criteria, aligned with HEC standards.
ii. The intended duration of the appointment (e.g., semester, academic year).
iii. The approved remuneration structure (e.g., per credit hour, fixed honorarium).
5.3 Selection Committee for V isiting Faculty : A Selection Committee, constituted by the Vice Chancellor/Rector upon the recommendation of the relevant Dean, shall be responsible for the hiring process. The respective Dean shall oversee the recruitment and subsequent performance of the Visiting Facult y.
5.4 Documentation: The entire selection process — including application screening, interviews, and teaching demonstrations — must be formally documented. A standardized scorecard with evaluation criteria must be used and the records duly approved by the com petent authority.
5.5 Formal Document of Engagement: A comprehensive, standardized agreement must
be executed with each Visiting Faculty member. The engagement shall, at a minimum, stipulate :
i. The specific course title(s) and code(s) assigned.
ii. The duration of the engagement (not to exceed one academic year without a
formal performance review).
..
iii. Detailed remuneration and payment terms.
iv. A clear outline of roles, responsibilities, and the institution's code of conduct.
v. Intellectual Property (IP) rights and confidentiality clauses.
5.6 Conflict of Interest Declaration: Prior to engagement , the candidate must submit a formal declaration disclosing any potential conflicts of interest and confirming their current professional affiliation s with any other institution or organization.
6.0 Roles, Responsibilities, and Institutional Integration
6.1 Primary Responsibilities: The primary role of Visiting Faculty is confined to course delivery, student assessment and evaluation, and contributing to course design and development as requested.

6.2 Governance and Administrative Roles: Visiting Faculty are expressly prohibited from holding substantive administrative positions (e.g., Head of Department, Dean) or exercising voting rights in statutory bodies such as the Syndicate, Senate, or Academic Council. Their advisory participation in academic bodies is however, encouraged.
6.3 Mandatory Orientation: The HEI must conduct a comprehensive orientation
program for all new Visiting Faculty. This program shall cover university policies, academic regulations, the use of the Learning Management System (LMS), examination procedures, and pedagogical guidelines. Orientation materials must explicitly communicate expected ethical, moral, and professi onal conduct.
7.0 Performance Monitoring and Evaluation
7.1 Student Feedback: Mandatory, anonymous student feedback must be collected for every course at the conclusion of each semester. The summarized results must be formally communicated to the relevant Head of Department and Dean.
7.2 Performance Dossier: The concerned academic department is responsible for
maintaining a continuous performance dossier for each Visiting Faculty member, which shall include student feedback, peer observation reports (if any), and other relevant performance metrics.
7.3 Agreement Renewal and Termination:
i. Renewal: Any agreement renewal is strictly contingent upon a documented
record of satisfactory performance.
ii. Termination: The HEI reserves the right to terminate the agreement by providing
due notice in cases of unsatisfactory performance, violation of university policies, or professional misconduct.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: GCU Hyderabad Directorate of Student Affairs — role and status
chunks.text:
Title: GCU Hyderabad Directorate of Student Affairs — role and status
Institution: Government College University Hyderabad
Authority: Government College University Hyderabad
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Sindh — GCU Hyderabad, institution-specific)
Document Type: Institutional overview page (not an operative regulation)
Source URL: https://www.gcuh.edu.pk/pages/student_affairs.html
Retrieval Date: 2026-10-14
Verification Status: Page text retrieved and read from the official site; the underlying student rules themselves are not published on this page, so no procedural detail below is verified beyond this statement.

The Directorate of Student Affairs at Government College University Hyderabad is a central administrative unit responsible for supporting student welfare, development, and engagement within the university. The Directorate works to maintain a safe, inclusive, and disciplined academic environment in which students are supported in their academic pursuits and personal development, in accordance with university rules and regulations.
The Directorate plans, coordinates, and supervises student-related activities, including registered student societies, co-curricular and extra-curricular programs, leadership initiatives, and student welfare services. It functions as a liaison between the university administration and the student body, facilitating communication, addressing student concerns through established procedures, and ensuring compliance with institutional policies.
In collaboration with academic departments, administrative offices, and student representatives, the Directorate of Student Affairs aims to develop responsible and confident graduates by promoting ethical conduct, civic responsibility, and constructive participation in university life.
Contacts published on the page: Directorate of Student Affairs, Government College University Hyderabad. Ms. Attia Amir, Incharge Director Students Affairs. Mr. Mukhtiar Ali, Incharge Deputy Director Student Affairs.

Title: GCU Hyderabad Student Affairs — vision and mission statements
Institution: Government College University Hyderabad
Authority: Government College University Hyderabad
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Sindh — GCU Hyderabad, institution-specific)
Document Type: Institutional policy statement (mandate wording, no sanctions or timelines)
Source URL: https://www.gcuh.edu.pk/pages/student_affairs.html
Retrieval Date: 2026-10-14
Verification Status: Published mandate text read from the official page; amendment status not independently verified.

Vision: To promote a respectful, inclusive, and student-centered campus environment that supports academic excellence, ethical behavior, leadership capacity, and responsible citizenship.
Mission: To protect and promote student rights, welfare, dignity, and well-being in accordance with university rules and applicable regulations.
Mission: To maintain a supportive and disciplined campus environment based on fairness, due process, and mutual respect.
Mission: To plan and facilitate co-curricular and extra-curricular activities that support students' personal, social, and professional development.
Mission: To regulate, support, and oversee student societies and representative bodies in alignment with university values, policies, and ethical standards.
Mission: To promote leadership development, civic responsibility, and community engagement among students through structured initiatives.
Mission: To ensure transparent, timely, and effective communication between students and the university administration through established channels.

Title: GCU Hyderabad student grievance, discipline and counselling functions
Institution: Government College University Hyderabad
Authority: Government College University Hyderabad
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Sindh — GCU Hyderabad, institution-specific)
Document Type: Institutional functions list (mandate wording, no complaint form, forum or deadline published)

Verification Status: Functions quoted from the official page. The page states that grievances and discipline are handled "through established mechanisms" and "based on established rules"; those rules, the competent forum, the acknowledgement period and the appeal route are NOT published on this page and remain unverified.

Functions and responsibilities published by the Directorate:
- Oversight and coordination of registered student societies and clubs in accordance with university policies.
- Promotion and enforcement of student discipline based on established rules, principles of fairness, and due process.
- Facilitation and coordination of student counseling, guidance, and welfare services in collaboration with relevant units.
- Receiving, processing, and addressing student grievances through established mechanisms, ensuring confidentiality and impartiality.
- Planning and organizing leadership, cultural, and student development programs approved by the university.
- Promoting inclusive student participation and fostering respect for diversity within the campus community.
Student Support and Human-Centered Services: The Directorate is committed to upholding student rights and promoting equitable access to opportunities for all students in accordance with university policies. Student support services are structured to promote well-being, dignity, and personal development, and to provide guidance in academic, personal, and social matters through respectful, confidential, and established procedures.

Higher Education Commission (HEC) is committed to its founding objective that no one should be denied access to higher education in Pakistan, and this includes making possible equal opportunities of higher education for students with disabilities.
This Policy aims to enable an environment in the Higher Education Sector which not only motivates students with disabilities to undertake higher education, but also facilitates their participation in all academic and extra-curricular aspects of a university education.

Title: HEC Need-Based Scholarship — eligibility criteria
Authority: Higher Education Commission of Pakistan, Scholarships & Grants
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: HEC Need Based Scholarships — Eligibility Criteria page
Source URL: https://www.hec.gov.pk/english/scholarshipsgrants/NBS/Pages/Eligibility-Criteria.aspx
Retrieval Method: Official page text read on 2026-10-14

Financial assistance & scholarships are available for study at the Undergraduate level in all disciplines at HEC-selected public sector Pakistani universities and degree-awarding institutions.
Students need to compete for securing admission at the participating institution as per the admission policy of the institution and be enrolled in Undergraduate (4-5 years) programs.
Students in financial need who are already enrolled in participating institutions are also eligible to apply.
The eligibility of a candidate is linked to his/her financial needs as assessed by the Institutional Scholarship Award Committee. The financial background of the family of the applicant will be kept in view in this regard.
The number of slots will be decided by the universities keeping in view the budget of the current year.
Funding for slots will continue for the complete duration of the program. In case any students drop out, they will be replaced by other candidates on the waiting list of the current year.
All disciplines will be kept open. The selected university will decide whether to include or exclude any discipline keeping in view its grant, program cost, and number of allocated slots, etc.
In the case of Medicine, Pharm-D and other five-year programs, funding will be made available for the complete program.
Considering the allocated grant, the university may adjust the total number of scholarships to an extent in order to cover the university fee.
In addition to the university fee, every grantee will be paid Rs.6000/- stipend per month for the complete program.
Those students who secure admission on self-finance are not eligible for HEC Need-Based Scholarship Program.
Note: The complete application should be sent to relevant Financial Aid Offices where the applicant intends to secure admission.

Special Friends (Disabled Persons): Families with two or more disabled members are recognized as "Special Friends" and supported with financial assistance — Rs. 20,000/- for families with one disabled person and Rs. 30,000/- for families with two or more disabled persons. Combination rule as published: assistance under categories such as medical treatment, general financial assistance, education stipend and rehabilitation may be granted within one year, except General assistance and Rehabilitation cannot be combined. Priority is given to widows, disabled and infirm individuals.

Age limits, qualification requirements, tuition or fee amounts, free-of-cost status, seat numbers and current intake openness are set per programme and are NOT established by this record. Do not state that all technical or vocational programmes are free, open, or share one eligibility rule. Do not apply HEC degree-awarding recognition rules as though they governed every technical-training programme.

Authority: Government College University Hyderabad (GCUH); refund quantified by the latest HEC Fee Refund Policy

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Benazir Kafaalat — how beneficiaries are identified, and the published PMT cut-off scores
chunks.text:
Title: Benazir Kafaalat — how beneficiaries are identified, and the published PMT cut-off scores
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Programme page "Benazir Kafaalat"
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal programme; provincial disbursement partners differ)
Source: BISP official website, Benazir Kafaalat programme page
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

"Beneficiaries of \"Benazir Kafaalat Programme\" are identified/selected through scientific mode of Proxy Means Test (PMT) through National Socio Economic Registry (NSER) survey."
"The current PMT cut-off score of 32 was approved by the BISP Board in its 52 nd meeting held on 23 rd September, 2021. However, for families with a differently abled person, the PMT cut-off score is set at 37 for eligibility."
Read the two numbers correctly: the cut-off is a ceiling on the household's proxy-means score, and a household containing a differently abled person is assessed against the more generous 37 threshold rather than 32.
Spelling note: BISP publishes this programme name as "Benazir Kafaalat" on its programme pages and as "BENAZIR Kafaalat" / "BISP Kifalat Programme" in its own registration leaflets, and it is commonly written "Benazir Kafalat". All of these spellings refer to the same cash-transfer programme described in this record.
Consequence for a citizen: eligibility is decided by the NSER/PMT household record, not by an application form alone. Where the record is stale, the route is a roster update or a new survey, described in the NSER registration record in this file.
Phrasings this answers: "which forum decides BISP eligibility", "how is the kafalat score worked out", "kafalat ki ahliyat kaun decide karta hai aur score kaise banta hai", "8171 eligibility ka form kaun sa hai". Urdu script: «بے نظیر کفالت کی اہلیت کا فورم کون سا ہے اور اسکور کیسے طے ہوتا ہے؟», «اہلیت کا تعین کس بنیاد پر ہوتا ہے؟». The forum named by the record is the BISP Board approving a PMT cut-off score computed from the NSER survey — not a form the applicant fills in.
The 32/37 figures are the Board-approved values as published on this page and read on 2026-10-16; a later Board meeting could change them, so re-verify before quoting a cut-off as current.

Title: Benazir Kafaalat stipend amount as published, the published conflict, and the biometric disbursement banks
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP)

Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

The programme page states: "Starting from Rs. 3,000/-per beneficiary per quarter, the present Benazir Kafaalat stipend is Rs. 8,500/- per beneficiary per quarter."
"Benazir Kafaalat cash assistance is disbursed to the eligible beneficiaries after Biometric Verification System (BVS) through two partner banks namely HBL in Punjab, Sindh and Baluchistan and Bank Alfalah in KP, GB and AJK."
Published conflict, recorded rather than resolved: a BISP news page dated "Islamabad, August 28, 2023" describes "quarterly financial assistance of Rs 9,000". The two figures are both on bisp.gov.pk; the programme page read on 2026-10-16 states Rs 8,500 and the 2023 news item states Rs 9,000. Because the amount is time-sensitive and BISP publishes no dated revision table on the programme page, the correct answer to a citizen is that the stipend is a quarterly per-beneficiary amount in this range and the amount payable to that beneficiary must be confirmed on the 8171 portal record or at the Tehsil office — not quoted as a settled single figure.
The bank that pays a beneficiary depends on the province or territory of residence; the stipend is released only after biometric verification.

"CNIC can be checked on 8171 portal to check the eligibility status of an individual."
"In case female is eligible and declared as beneficiary she will receive an SMS from 8171."
"On receipt of SMS the beneficiary will be required to visit nearest HBL / BAFL POS / retailer in her tehsil along with her original CNIC to receive the first installment through biometric verification."
"Next installments may also be received from ATM besides POS/ retailer."
"In case there is no record on 8171 portal, any adult member of the household may visit nearest Benazir registration desk, established at BISP Tehsil Office, for household survey."
The leaflet's own numbered steps: "STEP 1:- A household falls within approved cut off will be declared as \"Eligible\". STEP 2:- Only an ever married female with valid CNIC and cleared from profiling in an eligible household will be declared as beneficiary. STEP 3:- Message/SMS will sent to eligible beneficiary on provided mobile number from 8171. STEP 4:-After receiving SMS,Beneficiary will visit nearest POS in her Tehsil / District and receive her first cash grant after biometric verification. STEP 5:- For grievance Redressal she will register her complaint in the respective BISP Tehsil office."
Two conditions a citizen is often told wrongly: the household being eligible is not the same as being declared a beneficiary, and the beneficiary is the ever-married female member of the household with a valid CNIC who has cleared profiling — not any applicant who submits a form.

"The citizen can check their survey and eligibility status through: a) Online on https://8171.pass.gov.pk b) SMS your CNIC number on 8171".
CNIC screening at the desk: "If already Surveyed and need to perform roaster update will be issued Token for Roaster Update. - If not surveyed yet will be issued token for New Survey."
"At data entry desk provide your CNIC, Household member's CNIC and B Form of all children in your family. (All CNICs should be updated as per your current status in NADRA e.g. marital status, widow status, or disability etc)"

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: The 8171 web portal's two published functions and its form fields
chunks.text:
Title: The 8171 web portal's two published functions and its form fields
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), 8171 web portal
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: 8171 portal pages, read 2026-10-16
Source URL: https://8171.bisp.gov.pk/

The portal is titled "8171 ویب پورٹل" and its footer states "حقوق نقل و اشاعت ۲۰۲۵ بے نظیر انکم سپورٹ پروگرام۔ جملہ حقوق محفوظ ہیں۔" (Benazir Income Support Programme, 2025).
It publishes exactly two navigation functions: "اہلیت کے بارے میں جانیۓ" (learn about eligibility) at TrackingMain.aspx and "شکایت درج کروائیں" (register a complaint) at TrackingComplaints.aspx.
The eligibility form exposes a CNIC field limited to 13 characters, a captcha field, and a submit control labelled "معلوم کریں".
Verification limits, recorded honestly: the complaint page returned HTTP 520 and then 404 on 2026-10-16, so the complaint form's fields, required documents and any processing timeline are unverified. The eligibility enquiry itself requires entering a citizen's own CNIC into BISP's checker; this assistant does not perform that check and does not report an eligibility result — the citizen uses the portal, the 8171 SMS channel, or a BISP Tehsil Office.
The portal's stated purpose is enquiry and complaint tracking. It is not a registration route: household survey registration happens at a BISP Registration Centre or Tehsil office, per the BISP leaflets.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Benazir Kafaalat after a beneficiary's death — the documents for a legal-heir substitution
chunks.text:
Title: Benazir Kafaalat after a beneficiary's death — the documents for a legal-heir substitution
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Benazir Kafaalat programme page
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP official website
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

"the legal heirs from the deceased beneficiary family can become beneficiary of the programme through a well devised appeal mechanism. In case of death of a beneficiary, her family is required to submit necessary documents (CNIC of the deceased, CNIC cancellation certificate from NADRA, death certificate from union council and CNIC of family members) in nearest BISP Tehsil Office."
The four documents named are therefore: the deceased's CNIC; NADRA's CNIC cancellation certificate; the death certificate issued by the union council; and the CNICs of the surviving family members.
Where to take them: the nearest BISP Tehsil Office — this is a substitution of the beneficiary's name in the programme record, and BISP describes it as an appeal mechanism run through that office, not through a court.
Phrasings a bereaved family uses for this: "the BISP beneficiary died, who gets the money now", "my mother was receiving the 8171 stipend and she has passed away", "after the death of a kafalat beneficiary what documents are needed", "beneficiary ki maut ke baad qist kis ke naam hogi", "8171 payment death ke baad kya hoga", "kafalat mein heir/waris ka naam kaise hoga". Urdu script: «بینظیر کفالت کی مستحق خاتون وفات پا گئیں، اب قسط کس کے نام ہوگی؟», «وارثوں کے نام کے لیے کون سی دستاویزیں درکار ہیں؟».
Scope limit: BISP's page describes this as the route for a deceased beneficiary's family. It does not publish a written appeal procedure against a household that was simply assessed above the PMT cut-off — that gap is recorded in the unverified-facts section of this file.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: How a BISP beneficiary registers a complaint — the published channels, and the fraud warnings
chunks.text:
Title: How a BISP beneficiary registers a complaint — the published channels, and the fraud warnings
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP)
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP Benazir Kafaalat programme page and BISP news releases
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

The programme page's grievance section states: "To lodge complaints, beneficiaries can visit nearest Tehsil office of BISP or call at BISP HQs, Islamabad toll free help line (0800-26477)."
BISP's own authenticity warning: "It is essential to note that official communication from the Benazir Income Support Programme only originates from the number 8171."
Deduction and corruption: "If a person demands any kind of deduction or fee for payment, beneficiaries should immediately report to BISP's toll free helpline 080026477 and contact the nearest BISP Tehsil Office." and "For complaints related to deductions or corruption, beneficiaries should contact the BISP Helpline at 0800-26477."
The Kafaalat leaflet's step 5 is the same route: "For grievance Redressal she will register her complaint in the respective BISP Tehsil office." For Taleemi Wazaif specifically, "BISP field offices are mainly responsible for handling all the complaints."
So the two substantive beneficiary channels are the BISP Tehsil/field office in person and the toll-free helpline 0800-26477; 8171 is the official number for BISP messages and eligibility enquiry, not a complaint-handling office.
This is an administrative grievance route inside the programme. BISP's own pages for beneficiaries state no court step and no written appeal deadline for a payment complaint, so the first remedy on the record is the helpline and the Tehsil office, not a civil suit.
Phrasings a beneficiary uses for this: "someone is taking money out of my BISP payment", "a cut is being deducted from my 8171 stipend", "the person at the bank demanded a fee", "my qist has not come for two quarters", "kafalat ki qist mein katoti ho rahi hai kahan shikayat karun", "8171 payment nahi aa rahi complaint kaise karun", "qist kam aa rahi hai". Urdu script: «بینظیر کفالت کی قسط میں کٹوتی ہو رہی ہے، کہاں شکایت کروں؟», «قسط نہیں آ رہی، کس نمبر پر رابطہ کروں؟», «بازرس فیس مانگ رہا ہے».

chunks.text:
Title: BISP's 15-day and 5-day complaint timelines belong to bidders under Public Procurement Rules 2004, not to beneficiaries
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Procurement Complaint Redressal mechanism
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal — procurement)

Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/ZDk4ZWViMTUtZWQ4ZS00ZjM4LTk3ZGYtYzlkOTAwMGVkOWY4

These numbers are a procurement safeguard for suppliers and contractors. They are not a beneficiary's grievance timeline and must never be attached to a Kafaalat, Taleemi Wazaif, Nashonuma or payment complaint. BISP publishes no equivalent committed acknowledgement or decision period for beneficiary complaints; the beneficiary routes are the Tehsil/field office and 0800-26477. The procurement wording those figures come from is quoted below.
"In compliance of Public Procurement Rules, 2004, BISP provides a forum to bidders… a separate portal i.e. \"Bidders Complaint Redressal\" is created on BISP's Website".
"Complaints from bidders are inevitable… the aggrieved bidders may lodge a written complaint with BISP not later than 15 days after announcement of Bid Evaluation results".
"The complainant will be notified of receipt of his/her complaint within 05 working days." and "The Committee shall investigate and decide upon the complaint within fifteen days."

chunks.text:
Title: Taleemi Wazaif — enrolment place, documents, NADRA verification and the attendance co-responsibility
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Taleemi Wazaif programme
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP Taleemi Wazaif programme page and published leaflet
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YzNlY2Q2ZGYtNjIwZS00MjNiLWFhMmEtZGM5NWNkMjZhMjQ3

"Beneficiary has to visit enrolment camp/field offices along with her child with following documents… CNIC of the beneficiary; B-form/CRC issued by NADRA; School admission slip…"
"B-form/CRC verification through NADRA database is mandatory".
"BISP field offices are mainly responsible for handling all the complaints."
Attendance co-responsibility: BISP publishes that it will "Suspend the beneficiary children from the program who have not complied with the attendance co-responsibility for three consecutive compliance quarters."
A separate self-enrolment mobile application is published by BISP on the Play Store (pk.gov.bisp.enrollment).
Practical reading for a family: enrolment is done with the child at a camp or field office, the child must already have a NADRA B-form/CRC, and the school admission slip is required — so a child without a registered B-form cannot be enrolled until NADRA registration is complete. Suspension for three consecutive compliance quarters of poor attendance is a published rule, and it is appealable through the field office complaint route above.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Nashonuma — facilitation-centre enrolment, required documents, and two conflicting published stipend sets
chunks.text:
Title: Nashonuma — facilitation-centre enrolment, required documents, and two conflicting published stipend sets
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Nashonuma programme
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP Nashonuma programme page and the 2022 Nashonuma leaflet
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YjAyMjI5ZDQtN2RlYS00N2NhLTllY2UtY2NhNGE0ZDk3NmM2

"All the eligible beneficiaries have to visit nearby Nashonuma Facilitation centre (FC) for the purpose of enrolment…" with the documents listed there as pregnancy screening, a valid CNIC, an FRC for the child's registration, and immunization — "Valid Immunization Card from EPI".
Conflict recorded rather than resolved: the current programme page lists stipend amounts of Rs 3,500, Rs 3,500 and Rs 4,000 with a total of "up to Rs. 42,500/-", while BISP's own 2022 Nashonuma leaflet states different, lower quarterly amounts (PKR 2,000 and PKR 2,500 withheld per quarter). The two publications are not reconciled on the site.
Because of that conflict, the honest answer to a citizen is that Nashonuma amounts are payable per conditional milestone after enrolment at a facilitation centre, and the amount applicable to that beneficiary must be confirmed at the facilitation centre or Tehsil office. Do not quote one figure as authoritative, and do not average or merge the two sets.
Enrolment requires the child's FRC and an EPI immunization card, so the health and civil-registration steps are conditions of the grant, not paperwork formalities.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: BISP / 8171 — facts that could not be verified from official sources, and channels that are not what they appear to be
chunks.text:
Title: BISP / 8171 — facts that could not be verified from official sources, and channels that are not what they appear to be
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP) and related federal systems
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: Official-source verification pass on 2026-10-16
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk

Verification status: each item below was sought from official BISP or related federal sources during the verification pass of 2026-10-16 and could not be confirmed. The gap itself is the published state of the record, so an answer about these points is complete when it names the gap.
- No written appeal procedure against a rejected PMT/NSER score is published by BISP. BISP documents an appeal mechanism only for a deceased beneficiary's legal heirs, and the NSER page carries a row labelled "Implementation of Appeal Cut Off" with no procedure text. The routes that are published for such a household are a roster update or a new survey at a BRC/Tehsil office; no appeal form and no appellate body for a score rejection appear in BISP's own publications.
- The SMS reply format for "SMS your CNIC number on 8171" is not published on any page reached.
- The 8171 portal's complaint tab exists as a navigation label; its page returned HTTP 520 then 404 on 2026-10-16, so its fields, required documents and processing timeline are unverified.
- https://8171.pass.gov.pk (cited by BISP's own NSER leaflet) was unreachable from this host on 2026-10-16.
- https://ehsaas.gov.pk did not resolve; https://nser.nadra.gov.pk did not resolve; https://pcp.bisp.gov.pk/complaint.aspx exceeded the redirect limit; the BISP "FAQs" detail page contains only embedded videos and the "Help Desk / FAQ" navigation entry is an empty link. Several BISP navigation labels (8171, NSER, HBL biometric ATM, Non-BVS) resolve only to YouTube videos, which are not rule sources.
- BISP's published navigation labels are not procedural content: the site's menu is generated by script and the substantive text sits in the detail pages and leaflets, so a menu label on its own establishes no rule.
Disambiguation: the Pakistan Citizen Portal (citizenportal.gov.pk, run by PMDU) is a different system from BISP's 8171. Its homepage contains no occurrence of "8171", "BISP" or "Benazir", and BISP links it once, labelled "PMDU", under its Complaint Cell. A complaint filed through the Citizen Portal is not a BISP grievance, and 8171 is not a citizen-complaint helpline — BISP's own complaint channels are the Tehsil/field office and 0800-26477.
Also disambiguated: pmsa.gov.pk is the Pakistan Maritime Security Agency, not a social-security body, despite the similar acronym.

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: How the Kafaalat score is built — the published 0-100 PMT scale, the Board's fiscal-space basis, and the published reach of the programme
chunks.text:
Title: How the Kafaalat score is built — the published 0-100 PMT scale, the Board's fiscal-space basis, and the published reach of the programme
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Benazir Kafaalat programme page
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP official website, Benazir Kafaalat programme page, re-read 2026-10-18
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

"The welfare status of a household is determined on a scale between 0-100 of the PMT. The PMT cut-off score for eligibility is decided by BISP Board on the basis of available fiscal space. All families falling within the approved PMT cut-off score are being provided cash assistance under Benazir Kafaalat Programme."
"BISP is providing cash assistance to around 9 million families under Benazir Kafaalat programme."
Two things a citizen can conclude from this wording, and one they cannot. It establishes that the household's own score sits on a published 0-100 scale, and that the cut-off line on that scale is a Board decision tied to available fiscal space rather than a fixed statutory number — so a cut-off quoted today can be revised by a later Board meeting, and the 32/37 figures elsewhere in this file are the values published as of the date on this record. What it does not establish is any person's position on the scale: the score is computed from the NSER survey record, so nothing in this wording lets an assistant — or a neighbour — declare a household's score or its eligibility.
Phrasings this answers: "is the BISP cut-off fixed by law", "why did the 8171 cut-off change", "what is the PMT score range", "kafalat ka score kis scale par banta hai", "cut-off qanoon se tay hota hai ya board se", "itni families ko kyun nahi mil raha". Urdu script: «پی ایم ٹی اسکور کس پیمانے پر بنتا ہے؟», «کٹ آف کیا قانون میں مقرر ہے؟», «کفالت کا کٹ آف کون بدل سکتا ہے؟».

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Transgender inclusion in Benazir Kafaalat — the published conditions, and the relaxed cut-off
chunks.text:
Title: Transgender inclusion in Benazir Kafaalat — the published conditions, and the relaxed cut-off
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), Benazir Kafaalat programme page ("INCLUSION OF TRANSGENDER IN BENAZIR KAFAALAT PROGRAMME")
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP official website, Benazir Kafaalat programme page, re-read 2026-10-18
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5

"BISP's Board has recently approved Policy for inclusion of transgenders for cash assistance under Benazir Kafaalat Progrmme. Transgenders are required to obtain CNICs from NADRA clearly mentioning gender as transgender. Survey is mandatory at Benazir Registration Centers established in every BISP Tehsil Office. However, PMT cut-off restrictions are relaxed i.e. all transgenders whose survey is conducted successfully, are eligible to apply for inclusion in the programme. After validation/verification of data by NADRA, transgenders are declared as beneficiaries and they can start receiving cash assistance through BISP's partner banks."
Quoted exactly as published, including BISP's own misprint "Progrmme" in that sentence.
The procedure this establishes, in order: a transgender applicant's first step is a NADRA CNIC recording gender as transgender; the second is a survey, which BISP states is mandatory and is done at a Benazir Registration Centre, which the page says is established in every BISP Tehsil Office; the third is NADRA validation/verification of the data, after which the person is declared a beneficiary and is paid through BISP's partner banks. The published relaxation is specific: the PMT cut-off restriction is lifted for this group, so a successful survey — not a score below 32 — is the condition the page states.
Scope limits, stated plainly: the page refers to a Board-approved "Policy" but this record does not reproduce it, because the page's own link labelled "Inclusion of Transgenders in Benazir Kafalaat Programme" resolves to a YouTube video, which is not a rule source, and no policy PDF was reached from this page. So the published conditions are the four quoted above; no additional quota, reserved amount, appeal forum or timeline for transgender applicants exists on this record, and none may be inferred. Disbursement after declaration follows the same Biometric Verification System and the same partner-bank allocation by province recorded in the stipend section of this file.
Phrasings this answers: "can a transgender person get BISP Kafalat", "what did the BISP board approve for transgenders", "do transgender applicants need the PMT score", "transgender ke liye kafalat ka rule kya hai", "kya transgender ki survey lazmi hai". Urdu script: «ترنسینڈرز کے لیے بے نظیر کفالت کے کیا شرائط ہیں؟», «ان کے لیے پی ایم ٹی کٹ آف لاگو ہوتا ہے؟».

chunks.chunkTitle: Title: Taleemi Wazaif — the published age bands per level, the school-admission precondition, and the self-enrolment application
chunks.text:
Title: Taleemi Wazaif — the published age bands per level, the school-admission precondition, and the self-enrolment application
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), "BENAZIR TALEEMI WAZAIF Registration Process" leaflet
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP official publication, English text layer of the published PDF (file dated 09162022 in its published name)
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/SiteImage/Misc/files/Taleemi%20Wazaif_09162022.pdf

"Eligibility criteria for enrollment of children in Benazir Taleemi Wazaif program are as under: Children of active BISP Kafalat Beneficiary. Age criteria of child is 4 - 12 years for enrollment in Primary Education. Age criteria of child is 8 - 18 years for enrollment in Secondary Education. Age criteria of child is 13 - 22 years for enrollment in Higher Secondary Education."
"In order to become a beneficiary child of the Programme, an eligible child has to be admitted in school/college of any district of the country."
"School admission slip containing information of class, school name verified by the teacher."
"A digital application is established for self - enrollment. Children of active Kafalat beneficiaries can also be enrolled in Benazir Taleemi Wazaif programme through this digital application by their parents/teachers, link for download the application is given below: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=pk.gov.bisp.enrollment"
Read the bands as level gates, not as a single cut-off: the published ranges overlap by design (8-12 appears in both Primary and Secondary, 13-18 in both Secondary and Higher Secondary), so the child's enrolled level, not age alone, decides which band applies. The admission precondition is equally important: a child who is not admitted in a school or college cannot be enrolled, and the admission slip must show the class and school name verified by the teacher — the grant follows an actual school roll entry. The band limits also mean a child aged 22 or above cannot be enrolled under Higher Secondary, and a child under 4 cannot be enrolled under Primary, on this published wording.
The documents and the mandatory NADRA B-form/CRC verification, and the attendance co-responsibility and three-quarter suspension rule, are recorded in the Taleemi Wazaif section earlier in this file; this section adds the age bands, the admission precondition and the self-enrolment application, and the two must be read together.
Phrasings this answers: "what age does Taleemi Wazaif cover", "can my 6-year-old be enrolled in Taleemi Wazaif", "is school admission required for Taleemi Wazaif", "Taleemi Wazaif ke liye bachay ki age kitni honi chahiye", "admission slip ka rule kya hai". Urdu script: «تعلیمی وظائف میں بچے کی عمر کی شرط کیا ہے؟», «کیا اسکول میں داخلہ لازمی ہے؟».

chunks.text:
Title: Nashonuma — published target population, enrolment and compliance procedure, the 90% nutrition condition, and the quarterly amounts withheld against compliance
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP), "BENAZIR NASHONUMA Registration Process" leaflet
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: BISP official publication, English text layer of the published PDF (Urdu/English leaflet, 2022)
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk/SiteImage/Misc/files/NashonomaUrdu_2022.pdf

"BISP Target population: Pregnant and Lactating Women (PLW). Children 6 – 23 months of age."
"Following would be the eligibility criteria for the inclusion of the beneficiaries in the Nashonuma programme: Active BISP beneficiaries receiving unconditional cash transfer under Kafalat programme. Resides in any district of Pakistan. It is mandatory that eligible individuals for registration under Nashonuma shall be in any of these three categories i.e., Pregnant and Lactating Woman (PLW) or child 6 – 23 months of age in the family."
"All the eligible beneficiaries have to visit nearby Nashonuma Facilitation centre (FC) for the purpose of enrolment in Nashonuma programme. To further verify and confirm the status of beneficiaries in NSER database through search CNIC numbers in Nashonuma Android Application."
Verifications at enrolment, as published: "Pregnant Women – pregnancy test results/ confirmation report & EPI card of vaccination (TT Vaccination in 2nd trimester)"; "Lactating Mother – B-form of new-born/infant child and EPI card for vaccination proof."; "Children 6 - 23 months – B – form and EPI card for vaccination proof."
"In case of non - verification of pregnancy, lactating and children (0 - 23 months), target population will be referred to registration counter for marking the status of non - eligibility for the intervention."
Conditionality: "To accelerate the uptake of nutritional and PHC services, the transfer of an agreed portion of the cash transfer will be made conditional to the consumption of at least 90 percent of provided specialized nutrition foods by PLW and/or children in the support households and compliance to ANC, PNC, and routine immunization." "As BISP transfers funds on quarterly basis, the compliance monitoring and reporting will also be aligned with the transfer schedule."
The specialised nutrition foods named: "PLW – will be provided with SNF – Maamta (75 gram sachet – one per day)"; "Child 6 - 23 months – will be provided with SNF – Wawamum (50 gram sachet – one per day)".
Amounts on this leaflet: "A sum PKR 2,000 (to PLW and to a male child registered in Nashonuma Programme) and PKR 2,500 to a girl child registered in the Nashonuma Programme over a quarter will be withheld and linked with the consumption of SNF and utilization of essential PHC services i.e. Immunization, ANC and PNC. This amount will be transferred to beneficiaries upon ascertaining compliance by verifying consumption of at least 90% of the provided SNF and other associated services." "This condition shall also apply on twins and triplet children too and PKR 2000/2500 shall be considered as conditionality compliance amount for such cases."
What this settles and what it does not. It identifies which BISP publication carries the 2,000 / 2,500 quarterly figures: the 2022 Nashonuma registration-process leaflet, and it states what those figures are — a portion withheld against documented compliance, released once 90% consumption and ANC/PNC/immunization are verified, not a separate bonus. It does not resolve the conflict recorded in the Nashonuma section earlier in this file: the current programme page still publishes the higher 3,500 / 3,500 / 4,000 amounts and a total "up to Rs. 42,500/-", and BISP publishes no dated revision table reconciling the two. So the honest answer remains: the structure (quarterly, withheld against compliance, girl child at a higher rate) is documented, and the amount applicable to a given beneficiary must be confirmed at the facilitation centre or Tehsil office.
Note also what the enrolment conditions mean for a family: Nashonuma enrolment is stated for active Kafaalat beneficiaries, so on this leaflet a household outside the Kafalat roll is directed to the registration counter for a non-eligibility marking rather than enrolled; and the proof required is health-registry proof (EPI card, pregnancy confirmation report) plus NADRA B-form — so an unregistered birth blocks the grant's health condition.
Phrasings this answers: "what do I have to do to keep getting Nashonuma money", "why is part of my Nashonuma payment being held back", "is an EPI card required for Nashonuma", "Nashonuma ki qist mein se paisa kyun roka ja raha hai", "shartain kya hain Nashonuma ke liye". Urdu script: «نشونما کی رقم جاری ہونے کے لیے کیا شرائط ہیں؟», «ای پی آئی کارڈ لازمی ہے؟».

Title: BISP / 8171 — which official sources were re-checked on 2026-10-18, with their measured status
Authority: Benazir Income Support Programme (BISP); verification performed by INSAaf AI
Jurisdiction: Pakistan (Federal)
Source: Direct HTTP verification of bisp.gov.pk, 8171.bisp.gov.pk and the published PDFs on 2026-10-18
Source URL: https://bisp.gov.pk

This record exists so that a citizen can tell which BISP procedure rests on a source that is reachable right now. Measured statuses from the verification pass of 2026-10-18 (HTTP code, then what the response actually contained):
- Kafaalat programme page /Detail/YTgzNjkxM2YtN2ViMC00MjA5LWI0MDMtNzM4ZWJmMGVlNzc5 — HTTP 200, 77,110 bytes, 14,714 characters of readable page text. The quoted PMT, stipend, next-of-kin and grievance wording in this file is still present on the page today.
- Taleemi Wazaif programme page /Detail/YzNlY2Q2ZGYtNjIwZS00MjNiLWFhMmEtZGM5NWNkMjZhMjQ3 — HTTP 200, 139,439 bytes.
- Nashonuma programme page /Detail/YjAyMjI5ZDQtN2RlYS00N2NhLTllY2UtY2NhNGE0ZDk3NmM2 — HTTP 500 (server error, 9,698 bytes, no programme text). The Nashonuma wording carried in this file comes from the 2022 leaflet, whose URL returns HTTP 200, and from the programme page as read on 2026-10-16; the page being unavailable today does not invalidate that text, but it means the higher Nashonuma amounts could not be re-read today.
- Procurement complaint page /Detail/ZDk4ZWViMTUtZWQ4ZS00ZjM4LTk3ZGYtYzlkOTAwMGVkOWY4 — HTTP 200; Contact list page /Detail/Zjk0OGQ2NTgtZGVlZi00NmFiLWFiNzgtNDg5YThkOTQ0OWU0 — HTTP 200; PIO / Right to Information page /Detail/NWMwMzQwNWItZTUzMS00ODQ4LWJkNmEtYjMwMzZkN2Y3NDU5 — HTTP 200.
- "BENAZIR Kafaalat Registration Process" leaflet — the URL quoted in the registration-steps section of this file, /SiteImage/Misc/files/KifalatEngUr_2022.pdf, returns HTTP 404 today. The page's own navigation label for the same leaflet points to /SiteImage/Misc/files/KifalatEngUrdu_2022.pdf, which returns HTTP 200 (1,351,632 bytes) but could not be parsed: the PDF reader reported "Invalid PDF structure" and yielded no text. So the Kafaalat registration steps are preserved here from the verbatim capture made on 2026-10-16 when the leaflet was readable, and the correct current address of the leaflet is the KifalatEngUrdu_2022.pdf URL above.
- "BENAZIR TALEEMI WAZAIF Registration Process" leaflet /SiteImage/Misc/files/Taleemi%20Wazaif_09162022.pdf — HTTP 200, 2,241,117 bytes, 2 pages, English text extracted (age bands, enrolment process, self-enrolment application). "BENAZIR NASHONUMA Registration Process" leaflet /SiteImage/Misc/files/NashonomaUrdu_2022.pdf — HTTP 200, 130,915 bytes, 2 pages, English text extracted.
- BISP Digital Wallet publication /SiteImage/Misc/files/BISP%20book_compressed.pdf — HTTP 200, 1,387,728 bytes, 11 pages, but only 1,306 extractable characters, which are garbled Urdu. No usable procedure text, so nothing from it is ingested; a citizen asking about the BISP digital wallet has no verified record here.
- BISP Act 2010 /SiteImage/Misc/files/BISP_ACT_2010.pdf — HTTP 200, 1,941,518 bytes, 10 pages, 0 extractable characters. The Act is image-only, and no OCR of it has been performed, so the statute's own wording on the Programme's powers, survey and eligibility is NOT in this corpus. Do not answer "what does the BISP Act say" from this record; the accurate answer is that the Act is published but not yet readable by this assistant.
- 8171 web portal: https://8171.bisp.gov.pk/ and /TrackingMain.aspx both returned HTTP 200 with the same 13,573-byte page (the portal is one navigation shell). /TrackingComplaints.aspx returned HTTP 404 again ("The resource cannot be found. Server Error in '/' Application."), so the complaint form's fields, documents and timeline remain unverified — as recorded in the 8171 portal functions section and the unverified-facts section of this file.
- The historical URL /page.php?cat=8171 returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-18 as it did previously. It is not a route to rely on; the live 8171 material is the portal above and the detail pages.
- Navigation labels are still not content: the site menu's "8171", "NSER", "HBL biometric ATM" and "Non-BVS" entries resolve to YouTube videos, the "NSER Registration Centers" label points to nser.nadra.gov.pk (which does not resolve from this host), and "BISP Beneficiaries Portal" points to https://dli7.bisp.gov.pk/. Several BISP hrefs are published malformed as "..//SiteImage/..." — they work in a browser because the browser normalises them, and the normalised forms are the ones recorded above.
